entries.title: Accessible Job Search Lesson 1
entries.snippet: Accessible Accessible Job Search Lesson 1: Set a Career Goal and Search Keywords.

entries.title: Chrome Lesson 1
entries.snippet: Accessible Google Chrome Lesson 1: Chrome Layout, Address Bar, and Basic Navigation.
entries.text: chrome lesson 1 chrome lesson 1 accessible google chrome lesson 1: chrome layout, address bar, and basic navigation. chrome lesson 1 - accessible learning center google chrome course chrome lesson 1 chrome layout, address bar, and basic navigation chrome manual all chrome lessons my progress goal navigate chrome’s main controls, enter a web address, and move safely through page history. step-by-step instructions open chrome and press ctrl+l to focus the address bar. type https://accessiblelearning.github.io/accessible-learning-center/ and press enter. press alt+left arrow to go back and alt+right arrow to go forward. press alt+home to open the configured home page, then return to the learning site. press ctrl+r to reload the current page. press esc to stop a page that is still loading or dismiss an open browser control. press f6 repeatedly to move among the webpage, address bar, toolbar, and tab strip. with jaws, press insert+t to confirm the window and insert+tab to identify focus. record each command and the browser area it controls. save as chrome-lesson-1.txt. screen-reader help: with jaws, press insert+t for the window title, insert+tab for focused-control information, and insert+1 for keyboard help. chrome controls and labels can change after browser updates. your assignment create the report described above using fictional or public information only. save it as chrome-lesson-1.txt . docx, pdf, and brf versions are also accepted. before submitting address bar, back, forward, reload, and f6 are explained. the report names the practice site. the student distinguishes browser controls from webpage content. the file is chrome-lesson-1.txt. chrome manual next lesson chrome lesson 1.html

entries.title: Chrome Lesson 10
entries.snippet: Accessible Google Chrome Lesson 10: Final Accessible Workplace Research Project.
entries.text: chrome lesson 10 chrome lesson 10 accessible google chrome lesson 10: final accessible workplace research project. chrome lesson 10 - accessible learning center google chrome course chrome lesson 10 final accessible workplace research project chrome manual all chrome lessons my progress goal combine chrome, jaws, research, tabs, bookmarks, forms, and file-safety skills. step-by-step instructions choose a fictional workplace question that can be answered from public information. search for two authoritative sources and open them in separate tabs. use headings, links, lists, and find to locate relevant information. record each page title, organization, address, and publication or update date. compare one fact across both sources. bookmark the strongest source with a meaningful name. locate one form and identify its fields without submitting private information. locate one downloadable file and record its name and type without opening it if unnecessary. write the answer, commands used, accessibility observations, and safety decisions. review with jaws say all and save as chrome-lesson-10.txt. screen-reader help: with jaws, press insert+t for the window title, insert+tab for focused-control information, and insert+1 for keyboard help. chrome controls and labels can change after browser updates. your assignment create the report described above using fictional or public information only. save it as chrome-lesson-10.txt . docx, pdf, and brf versions are also accepted. before submitting two authoritative sources are documented. at least eight chrome or jaws commands are recorded. a bookmark, form, and potential download are evaluated. no private information is submitted. the file is chrome-lesson-10.txt. chrome manual review my progress chrome lesson 10.html

entries.text: chrome lesson 2 chrome lesson 2 accessible google chrome lesson 2: tabs, windows, and restoring work. chrome lesson 2 - accessible learning center google chrome course chrome lesson 2 tabs, windows, and restoring work chrome manual all chrome lessons my progress goal open, switch, close, reopen, and organize browser tabs and windows. step-by-step instructions press ctrl+t to open a new tab. open a safe practice website from the address bar. press ctrl+tab and ctrl+shift+tab to move forward and backward among tabs. press ctrl+1 through ctrl+8 to move to a numbered tab and ctrl+9 to move to the last tab. press ctrl+w to close only the active tab. press ctrl+shift+t to reopen the most recently closed tab. press ctrl+n to open a new chrome window. use alt+tab to move between chrome windows and other applications. close the extra chrome window with alt+f4 after confirming it is the intended window. write a tab-and-window guide in chrome-lesson-2.txt. screen-reader help: with jaws, press insert+t for the window title, insert+tab for focused-control information, and insert+1 for keyboard help. chrome controls and labels can change after browser updates. your assignment create the report described above using fictional or public information only. save it as chrome-lesson-2.txt . docx, pdf, and brf versions are also accepted. before submitting tab and window commands are distinguished. closing and reopening a tab are explained. the student confirms windows before closing them. the file is chrome-lesson-2.txt. chrome manual next lesson chrome lesson 2.html

entries.text: chrome lesson 4 chrome lesson 4 accessible google chrome lesson 4: web search, research, and source evaluation. chrome lesson 4 - accessible learning center google chrome course chrome lesson 4 web search, research, and source evaluation chrome manual all chrome lessons my progress goal search efficiently and record trustworthy workplace information. step-by-step instructions press ctrl+l and type a specific research question. review search results by heading with h and by link with tab or insert+f7. open one promising result in a new tab with ctrl+enter from the address bar suggestion or the available link context command. check the page title, organization, publication or update date, and web address. prefer official government, educational, manufacturer, or primary-source pages for factual instructions. compare the same fact with a second reliable source. do not enter personal information into an unfamiliar search form. record the question, two sources, dates, and the fact verified. return to the original tab and close unused tabs. save the research report as chrome-lesson-4.txt. screen-reader help: with jaws, press insert+t for the window title, insert+tab for focused-control information, and insert+1 for keyboard help. chrome controls and labels can change after browser updates. your assignment create the report described above using fictional or public information only. save it as chrome-lesson-4.txt . docx, pdf, and brf versions are also accepted. before submitting the research question is specific. two sources and their organizations are recorded. the report explains why the sources are trustworthy. the file is chrome-lesson-4.txt. chrome manual next lesson chrome lesson 4.html

entries.text: excel lesson 1 excel lesson 1 accessible microsoft excel lesson 1: excel basics: workbooks, worksheets, and cells. excel lesson 1 - accessible learning center microsoft excel course excel lesson 1 excel basics: workbooks, worksheets, and cells excel manual all excel lessons my progress goal open excel, understand the worksheet grid, enter a simple workplace contact list, and save a workbook. skills practiced identify a workbook, worksheet, row, column, cell, and cell address. move one cell at a time with the arrow keys. enter and correct text in cells. save an excel workbook as an xlsx file. step-by-step instructions open microsoft excel and create a blank workbook. jaws announces the active cell address and its contents. the first cell is a1. type name in a1, press tab, type department in b1, press tab, and type extension in c1. press home to return to column a in the current row. in row 2, enter jordan lee, training, and 4101. use tab after each entry. in row 3, enter morgan reed, technology, and 4102. in row 4, enter casey hall, employment, and 4103. use the arrow keys to review each cell. press insert+up arrow to hear the current line or cell information when useful. press ctrl+s. choose a folder you can locate later. save the workbook as excel-lesson-1.xlsx. jaws help: press insert+spacebar, then j, to search jaws commands when you forget a keystroke. ribbon keytips can differ slightly by microsoft 365 update, so alt+q search is included where useful. your assignment create a three-column employee contact list with the headers name, department, and extension. include at least five fictional employees. save the finished assignment as excel-lesson-1.xlsx . before submitting row 1 contains clear column headers. at least five fictional employee records are included. there are no completely blank rows inside the list. the file is saved as excel-lesson-1.xlsx. excel manual next lesson excel lesson 1.html

entries.title: Excel Lesson 10
entries.snippet: Accessible Microsoft Excel Lesson 10: Final Employment Workbook Project.
entries.text: excel lesson 10 excel lesson 10 accessible microsoft excel lesson 10: final employment workbook project. excel lesson 10 - accessible learning center microsoft excel course excel lesson 10 final employment workbook project excel manual all excel lessons my progress goal independently build an accessible workbook that organizes, calculates, summarizes, and communicates workplace information. skills practiced plan an accessible table structure. use formulas and functions accurately. organize multiple worksheets. create an accessible summary for a supervisor. step-by-step instructions create a workbook for a fictional department's monthly supply budget. create a purchases worksheet with the headers date, item, category, quantity, unit cost, and line total. enter at least ten fictional purchases across at least three categories. use a formula to calculate each line total. format dates and currency appropriately without merging cells. convert the purchase list to a table and give it a meaningful name. create a summary worksheet. calculate the grand total, average line total, lowest line total, and highest line total. use countif to count at least one category or status. create one simple chart from summary data, add meaningful alt text, and keep its source data available. add a plain-text summary that explains the most important result. run the accessibility checker and review every worksheet using only the keyboard. save the workbook as excel-lesson-10-final.xlsx. jaws help: press insert+spacebar, then j, to search jaws commands when you forget a keystroke. ribbon keytips can differ slightly by microsoft 365 update, so alt+q search is included where useful. your assignment complete an accessible monthly supply-budget workbook with at least ten purchases, formulas, a table, summary calculations, a chart with alt text, and a written summary. save the finished assignment as excel-lesson-10-final.xlsx . before submitting the purchases worksheet contains at least ten complete records. all line totals and summary calculations use formulas. the workbook includes a clearly named summary worksheet. the chart has alt text and its source data remains available. there are no merged cells or color-only instructions. the accessibility checker was reviewed. the file is saved as excel-lesson-10-final.xlsx. previous lesson view course progress excel lesson 10.html

entries.title: Excel Lesson 2
entries.snippet: Accessible Microsoft Excel Lesson 2: Navigating, Editing, Finding, and Filling Data.
entries.text: excel lesson 2 excel lesson 2 accessible microsoft excel lesson 2: navigating, editing, finding, and filling data. excel lesson 2 - accessible learning center microsoft excel course excel lesson 2 navigating, editing, finding, and filling data excel manual all excel lessons my progress goal move efficiently through a worksheet, edit cells, find and replace information, and copy values without relying on a mouse. skills practiced move to data boundaries with ctrl+arrow. use ctrl+g to go directly to a cell. edit a cell with f2. use find and replace. copy and paste a value or formula. step-by-step instructions open excel-lesson-1.xlsx. press ctrl+home to move to a1. press ctrl+end to move to the last used cell. press ctrl+g, type b3, and press enter to move directly to cell b3. press f2, change the department in b3 to customer service, and press enter. press ctrl+f, type employment, and press enter to locate that word. press escape to close find. press ctrl+h. replace training with learning services, then close the dialog. add a fourth column header in d1 named status. type active in d2. copy d2 with ctrl+c, select d3 through the last employee row with shift+down arrow, and press ctrl+v. review the list with ctrl+arrow and arrow keys. press f12 or use file, save as, and save a copy as excel-lesson-2.xlsx. jaws help: press insert+spacebar, then j, to search jaws commands when you forget a keystroke. ribbon keytips can differ slightly by microsoft 365 update, so alt+q search is included where useful. your assignment update the contact list so one department is customer service, training is replaced with learning services, and every employee has active in the status column. save the finished assignment as excel-lesson-2.xlsx . before submitting the original headers remain present. customer service and learning services appear in the department column. every employee row has active in the status column. the file is saved as excel-lesson-2.xlsx. previous lesson next lesson excel lesson 2.html

entries.title: Excel Lesson 3
entries.snippet: Accessible Microsoft Excel Lesson 3: Formulas, AutoSum, and Basic Calculations.
entries.text: excel lesson 3 excel lesson 3 accessible microsoft excel lesson 3: formulas, autosum, and basic calculations. excel lesson 3 - accessible learning center microsoft excel course excel lesson 3 formulas, autosum, and basic calculations excel manual all excel lessons my progress goal create a small expense worksheet and calculate totals and averages with formulas. skills practiced enter formulas beginning with an equals sign. use cell references in calculations. use autosum with alt+equals. use sum, average, min, and max. step-by-step instructions create a blank workbook. in a1 through c1, enter item, quantity, and unit cost. enter five fictional office supply items in rows 2 through 6 with quantities and unit costs. in d1, enter line total. in d2, type =b2*c2 and press enter. copy d2 and paste it into d3 through d6. excel adjusts the row references. in c8, enter grand total. in d8, press alt+equals, confirm the range d2:d6, and press enter. in c9, enter average cost. in d9, type =average(d2:d6) and press enter. in c10, enter lowest cost. in d10, type =min(d2:d6). in c11, enter highest cost. in d11, type =max(d2:d6). use f2 on each result cell to review the formula, then press escape without changing it. save the workbook as excel-lesson-3.xlsx. jaws help: press insert+spacebar, then j, to search jaws commands when you forget a keystroke. ribbon keytips can differ slightly by microsoft 365 update, so alt+q search is included where useful. your assignment create an office-supply expense worksheet with at least five items, line totals, a grand total, an average, a minimum, and a maximum. save the finished assignment as excel-lesson-3.xlsx . before submitting all formulas begin with an equals sign. line totals use quantity multiplied by unit cost. summary formulas reference the correct range. the file is saved as excel-lesson-3.xlsx. previous lesson next lesson excel lesson 3.html

entries.title: Excel Lesson 4
entries.snippet: Accessible Microsoft Excel Lesson 4: Accessible Formatting and Number Formats.
entries.text: excel lesson 4 excel lesson 4 accessible microsoft excel lesson 4: accessible formatting and number formats. excel lesson 4 - accessible learning center microsoft excel course excel lesson 4 accessible formatting and number formats excel manual all excel lessons my progress goal apply meaningful formatting and number formats while keeping the worksheet usable with screen readers and magnification. skills practiced open format cells with ctrl+1. apply currency, percentage, date, and text formats. use bold and clear headers. avoid merged cells and color-only meaning. step-by-step instructions open excel-lesson-3.xlsx. select the header row from a1 through d1 and press ctrl+b. select the unit cost and line total values. press ctrl+1 to open format cells. choose currency or accounting with two decimal places, then press enter. add a discount column in e1. enter percentages such as 5%, 10%, and 0% in e2 through e6. use ctrl+1 to confirm the discount cells use percentage format. add a purchase date column in f1 and enter valid dates for each item. use ctrl+1 to apply a clear date format. do not merge cells. keep one header for every column and one record per row. if you use color, also include text such as approved or review so color is not the only cue. run review, check accessibility by pressing alt+q, typing check accessibility, and choosing the command. save the workbook as excel-lesson-4.xlsx. jaws help: press insert+spacebar, then j, to search jaws commands when you forget a keystroke. ribbon keytips can differ slightly by microsoft 365 update, so alt+q search is included where useful. your assignment format the expense worksheet with bold headers, currency, percentage, and date formats. keep the structure accessible and do not merge cells. save the finished assignment as excel-lesson-4.xlsx . before submitting headers are bold and descriptive. money, percentages, and dates use appropriate number formats. no cells are merged. color is not the only way information is communicated. the file is saved as excel-lesson-4.xlsx. previous lesson next lesson excel lesson 4.html

entries.title: Excel Lesson 5
entries.snippet: Accessible Microsoft Excel Lesson 5: Tables, Sorting, and Filtering.
entries.text: excel lesson 5 excel lesson 5 accessible microsoft excel lesson 5: tables, sorting, and filtering. excel lesson 5 - accessible learning center microsoft excel course excel lesson 5 tables, sorting, and filtering excel manual all excel lessons my progress goal convert data into an accessible excel table and use keyboard commands to sort and filter records. skills practiced create a table with ctrl+t. confirm that the table has headers. open a column filter with alt+down arrow. sort and filter workplace data. step-by-step instructions create a blank workbook with the headers employee, department, training status, and due date in row 1. enter at least eight fictional employee records. use complete, in progress, or not started in the training status column. select any cell in the list and press ctrl+t. confirm the correct range and check my table has headers, then press enter. move to a header cell and press alt+down arrow to open its filter menu. in the department header, sort a to z using the menu. in the training status header, filter the table so only not started records remain. review the visible rows with the arrow keys. open the filter again and choose clear filter so all records return. give the table a meaningful name through table design if available, such as trainingtracker. save the workbook as excel-lesson-5.xlsx. jaws help: press insert+spacebar, then j, to search jaws commands when you forget a keystroke. ribbon keytips can differ slightly by microsoft 365 update, so alt+q search is included where useful. your assignment create a training tracker with at least eight fictional employees, convert it to a table, sort by department, and confirm that filtering by training status works. save the finished assignment as excel-lesson-5.xlsx . before submitting the list is formatted as an excel table. the table includes unique, descriptive headers. at least eight records are included. there are no blank rows or columns inside the table. the file is saved as excel-lesson-5.xlsx. previous lesson next lesson excel lesson 5.html

entries.title: Excel Lesson 6
entries.snippet: Accessible Microsoft Excel Lesson 6: IF, COUNTIF, and Conditional Results.
entries.text: excel lesson 6 excel lesson 6 accessible microsoft excel lesson 6: if, countif, and conditional results. excel lesson 6 - accessible learning center microsoft excel course excel lesson 6 if, countif, and conditional results excel manual all excel lessons my progress goal use logical and counting functions to turn raw workplace data into useful status information. skills practiced use if to return one of two text results. use countif to count records that meet a condition. copy formulas down a column. check formula ranges and quotation marks. step-by-step instructions create a workbook with the headers employee, completed hours, required hours, and status. enter six fictional employees. give each person completed hours and a required-hours goal. in d2, type =if(b2>=c2,"complete","needs training") and press enter. copy the formula from d2 through all employee rows. below the list, enter complete count in c10. in d10, type =countif(d2:d7,"complete") and press enter. adjust the ending row if your list is longer. enter needs training count in c11. in d11, type =countif(d2:d7,"needs training") and press enter. use f2 to inspect a copied if formula and confirm its row references changed. use ctrl+grave accent to show formulas if available, then press it again to return to results. save the workbook as excel-lesson-6.xlsx. jaws help: press insert+spacebar, then j, to search jaws commands when you forget a keystroke. ribbon keytips can differ slightly by microsoft 365 update, so alt+q search is included where useful. your assignment create a six-person training-hours tracker that automatically labels each person complete or needs training and counts both results. save the finished assignment as excel-lesson-6.xlsx . before submitting the if formula compares completed hours with required hours. every employee row contains a status formula. countif totals both status categories. the file is saved as excel-lesson-6.xlsx. previous lesson next lesson excel lesson 6.html

entries.title: Excel Lesson 7
entries.snippet: Accessible Microsoft Excel Lesson 7: Managing Worksheets and Cross-Sheet References.
entries.text: excel lesson 7 excel lesson 7 accessible microsoft excel lesson 7: managing worksheets and cross-sheet references. excel lesson 7 - accessible learning center microsoft excel course excel lesson 7 managing worksheets and cross-sheet references excel manual all excel lessons my progress goal organize related information across worksheets and create a summary that refers to another sheet. skills practiced insert a worksheet with shift+f11. move between sheets with ctrl+page up and ctrl+page down. rename worksheets. reference a cell on another worksheet. step-by-step instructions create a blank workbook and rename sheet1 to january. use alt+q and search for rename sheet if ribbon keytips differ. enter category and amount in a1 and b1. enter five fictional january expenses in rows 2 through 6. press shift+f11 to insert a new worksheet and rename it february. enter the same headers and five fictional february expenses. press shift+f11 again and rename the new worksheet summary. use ctrl+page up and ctrl+page down to move among the three worksheets. on january, calculate the total in b8 with =sum(b2:b6). do the same on february. on summary, enter january total in a1 and type =january!b8 in b1. enter february total in a2 and type =february!b8 in b2. enter combined total in a3 and type =sum(b1:b2) in b3. save the workbook as excel-lesson-7.xlsx. jaws help: press insert+spacebar, then j, to search jaws commands when you forget a keystroke. ribbon keytips can differ slightly by microsoft 365 update, so alt+q search is included where useful. your assignment create january, february, and summary worksheets. enter expenses on the monthly sheets and show both monthly totals plus a combined total on summary. save the finished assignment as excel-lesson-7.xlsx . before submitting all three worksheets have meaningful names. monthly totals use sum formulas. summary references the monthly worksheets. ctrl+page up and ctrl+page down move among the sheets. the file is saved as excel-lesson-7.xlsx. previous lesson next lesson excel lesson 7.html

entries.title: Excel Lesson 8
entries.snippet: Accessible Microsoft Excel Lesson 8: Charts, Alternative Text, and Accessibility Checker.
entries.text: excel lesson 8 excel lesson 8 accessible microsoft excel lesson 8: charts, alternative text, and accessibility checker. excel lesson 8 - accessible learning center microsoft excel course excel lesson 8 charts, alternative text, and accessibility checker excel manual all excel lessons my progress goal create a simple chart, provide a text equivalent, and use excel accessibility checks. skills practiced create a chart from a small data table. add meaningful alternative text. provide the same key information in worksheet cells. run the accessibility checker. step-by-step instructions create a two-column table with month and completed trainings. enter january through june and fictional completion totals. select the table, including headers. press alt+f1 to create a chart on the current worksheet. use f6 to move focus among the worksheet, ribbon, and chart objects until jaws announces the chart. open the chart context menu with shift+f10. use format chart area or alt text options to add a description. write concise alt text that explains the chart's purpose and important trend, not every visual detail. keep the source data table in the workbook so screen-reader users can inspect exact values. add a cell below the table containing a short text summary of the trend. press alt+q, type check accessibility, and run the accessibility checker. review and resolve issues that apply. do not remove the source table. save the workbook as excel-lesson-8.xlsx. jaws help: press insert+spacebar, then j, to search jaws commands when you forget a keystroke. ribbon keytips can differ slightly by microsoft 365 update, so alt+q search is included where useful. your assignment create a six-month training-completion chart, add meaningful alternative text, retain the source data, and include a plain-text trend summary. save the finished assignment as excel-lesson-8.xlsx . before submitting the chart is based on a clearly labeled data table. the chart has useful alternative text. a text summary identifies the main trend. the accessibility checker was reviewed. the file is saved as excel-lesson-8.xlsx. previous lesson next lesson excel lesson 8.html

entries.title: Excel Lesson 9
entries.snippet: Accessible Microsoft Excel Lesson 9: Data Validation, Consistent Entry, and Review.
entries.text: excel lesson 9 excel lesson 9 accessible microsoft excel lesson 9: data validation, consistent entry, and review. excel lesson 9 - accessible learning center microsoft excel course excel lesson 9 data validation, consistent entry, and review excel manual all excel lessons my progress goal create a reliable data-entry sheet with controlled choices and check it for common accessibility problems. skills practiced create a drop-down list with data validation. use consistent data types. find blanks and errors. document instructions inside the workbook. step-by-step instructions create a blank workbook with the headers request id, request type, priority, assigned to, and status. enter five fictional requests. in a separate area, list the allowed status values: new, in progress, waiting, and closed. select the status entry cells. press alt+q, type data validation, and choose the command. choose list and set the source to the cells containing the allowed status values. use alt+down arrow in a validated status cell to open its choices, then select a value. apply a similar list to priority using low, medium, and high. add an instructions worksheet explaining what each column contains and which values are allowed. use ctrl+f to search for blank required fields and review the used range with ctrl+end. run check accessibility and correct merged cells, unclear sheet names, or missing object descriptions. save the workbook as excel-lesson-9.xlsx. jaws help: press insert+spacebar, then j, to search jaws commands when you forget a keystroke. ribbon keytips can differ slightly by microsoft 365 update, so alt+q search is included where useful. your assignment create a small service-request tracker with validated status and priority choices plus an instructions worksheet. save the finished assignment as excel-lesson-9.xlsx . before submitting status and priority use controlled lists. every request has a unique request id. the instructions worksheet explains the fields. no required cells are blank. the file is saved as excel-lesson-9.xlsx. previous lesson next lesson excel lesson 9.html

entries.snippet: Accessible Google Gemini Lesson 1: Open Gemini and Navigate the Chat Interface.
entries.text: gemini lesson 1 gemini lesson 1 accessible google gemini lesson 1: open gemini and navigate the chat interface. gemini lesson 1 - accessible learning center google gemini course gemini lesson 1 open gemini and navigate the chat interface gemini manual all gemini lessons my progress goal identify the prompt field, send control, new-chat control, response area, and account controls. before you begin use only fictional or public information. do not enter client, medical, financial, password, confidential workplace, or personally identifying information. do not purchase a subscription or start a paid trial. you—not the ai tool—are responsible for the final work. step-by-step instructions open the google gemini manual and review the prompting, verification, privacy, and screen-reader sections. open an available ai tool in a regular browser tab. if an account or feature is unavailable, study the sample prompt and write the expected process instead. navigate by headings and form controls. find the prompt edit field and confirm its label before typing. use this practice prompt or adapt it without adding private information: act as an accessible workplace skills coach. help me identify the prompt field, send control, new-chat control, response area, and account controls. use fictional or public information only. organize the response with descriptive headings and numbered steps. identify anything i must verify. read the complete response by heading, paragraph, list item, and link. do not assume the first answer is correct. send at least one follow-up prompt that improves clarity, accuracy, accessibility, or completeness. verify important claims using the original source or another authoritative source. record unsupported statements and corrections. edit the final result in your own words. remove generic, inaccurate, biased, or unnecessary content. create a short process note naming the tool, prompts used, facts checked, changes made, and remaining uncertainty. save the assignment as gemini-lesson-1.txt . screen-reader help: jaws and nvda users can press h for headings, b for buttons, and e for edit fields in browse mode. narrator users can navigate with scan mode. press tab and shift+tab for interactive controls. because ai interfaces change frequently, listen to each control’s current accessible name. your assignment identify the prompt field, send control, new-chat control, response area, and account controls. include the original prompt, at least one follow-up prompt, a revised result, a verification record, and a one-paragraph reflection on what required human judgment. save it as gemini-lesson-1.txt . docx, pdf, and brf versions are also accepted. before submitting no private or confidential information is included. the result uses descriptive headings and clear organization. important claims were checked against an authoritative source. the student—not the ai tool—made the final decisions. the filename entries.snippet: Word Lesson 1 - Accessible Learning Center Microsoft Word Lesson 1 Opening Word, Creating, and Saving a Document Goal Learn how to open Microsoft Word, create a blank document, enter text, and save the document. Instructions Press the Windo
entries.text: word lesson 1 microsoft word lesson 1  word lesson 1 - accessible learning center microsoft word lesson 1 opening word, creating, and saving a document goal learn how to open microsoft word, create a blank document, enter text, and save the document. instructions press the windows key. type word. press enter on microsoft word. press ctrl+n to create a blank document. type the heading: my first word document press enter twice. type: i am learning to use microsoft word independently with a screen reader. press enter twice. type: i can create, type, save, and reopen word documents. press ctrl+s. choose a location you can find again. name the file word-lesson-1. save it as a docx file. your assignment complete the assignment and save it as: word-lesson-1.docx before submitting make sure all required text is present. make sure the file is saved as docx. make sure the filename is word-lesson-1. view my progress return to lessons word lesson 1.html

entries.title: Microsoft Word Lesson 10
entries.snippet: Word Lesson 10 - Accessible Learning Center Microsoft Word Lesson 10 Final Independent Word Assignment Goal Demonstrate the Microsoft Word skills you have practiced throughout Lessons 1 through 9. Your Assignment Create a one-page document
entries.text: word lesson 10 microsoft word lesson 10  word lesson 10 - accessible learning center microsoft word lesson 10 final independent word assignment goal demonstrate the microsoft word skills you have practiced throughout lessons 1 through 9. your assignment create a one-page document titled my accessible technology skills . requirements create the document independently. use the title my accessible technology skills. apply heading 1 to the title. create at least two heading 2 sections. write at least two paragraphs of body text. include one bulleted or numbered list containing at least three items. include one simple table containing at least three columns and three rows. make the first table row a header row. include one descriptive hyperlink. use at least one example of bold or italic formatting. run spelling and grammar review. run accessibility checker or accessibility assistant. correct important accessibility issues that word identifies. save the document as word-lesson-10-final.docx. create a pdf copy if you are able to do so. what the assignment checker will review document structure correct use of headings paragraph content lists table structure meaningful hyperlink text basic formatting accessibility filename overall organization remember the goal is not perfection. the goal is to demonstrate that you can create and organize a word document independently. feedback will identify what you did well and a small number of things to improve next time. view my progress return to lessons word lesson 10.html

entries.title: Microsoft Word Lesson 2
entries.snippet: Word Lesson 2 - Accessible Learning Center Microsoft Word Lesson 2 Moving, Selecting, and Editing Text Goal Practice moving through text, selecting words, correcting mistakes, copying, cutting, pasting, undoing, and redoing. Instructions Op
entries.text: word lesson 2 microsoft word lesson 2  word lesson 2 - accessible learning center microsoft word lesson 2 moving, selecting, and editing text goal practice moving through text, selecting words, correcting mistakes, copying, cutting, pasting, undoing, and redoing. instructions open microsoft word and create a blank document. type: the quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog. press enter twice. type: microsoft word makes document editing easy. use ctrl+left arrow and ctrl+right arrow to move by word. use left arrow and right arrow to move by character. select the word easy using ctrl+shift+left arrow or ctrl+shift+right arrow. replace easy with efficient. select the words microsoft word. press ctrl+c to copy them. move to the end of the document. press enter twice and press ctrl+v. press ctrl+z to undo the paste. press ctrl+y to redo it. save the file as word-lesson-2.docx. your assignment submit word-lesson-2.docx . before submitting the word easy should have been replaced with efficient. microsoft word should appear again at the bottom of the document. the file should be saved correctly. view my progress return to lessons word lesson 2.html

entries.title: Microsoft Word Lesson 3
entries.snippet: Word Lesson 3 - Accessible Learning Center Microsoft Word Lesson 3 Find, Replace, Save, Close, and Reopen Goal Learn how to find text, replace text, save a document, close it, and reopen it. Instructions Create a new Word document. Type thr
entries.text: word lesson 3 microsoft word lesson 3  word lesson 3 - accessible learning center microsoft word lesson 3 find, replace, save, close, and reopen goal learn how to find text, replace text, save a document, close it, and reopen it. instructions create a new word document. type three short paragraphs containing the word computer at least four times. press ctrl+f. search for computer. move through the search results. close the navigation pane with escape. press ctrl+h. replace one occurrence of computer with technology. do not use replace all. save the file as word-lesson-3.docx. press ctrl+w to close the document. press ctrl+o. locate word-lesson-3.docx and reopen it. press ctrl+home and verify the document contents. your assignment submit word-lesson-3.docx . before submitting the document should contain three paragraphs. at least one occurrence of computer should be changed to technology. the document should have been successfully saved and reopened. view my progress return to lessons word lesson 3.html

entries.text: word lesson 4 microsoft word lesson 4  word lesson 4 - accessible learning center microsoft word lesson 4 formatting text and paragraphs goal practice bold, italics, underline, alignment, and basic paragraph formatting. instructions create a blank word document. type the title: accessible technology skills press enter twice. type: technology can increase independence at work, school, and home. press enter twice. type: learning keyboard commands can make common tasks faster. make the title bold. center the title using ctrl+e. make the words increase independence italic. underline the words keyboard commands. make sure both body paragraphs are left aligned using ctrl+l. save the document as word-lesson-4.docx. your assignment submit word-lesson-4.docx . before submitting the title should be bold and centered. the requested phrase should be italic. the requested phrase should be underlined. the body paragraphs should be left aligned. view my progress return to lessons word lesson 4.html

entries.title: Microsoft Word Lesson 5

entries.snippet: Word Lesson 6 - Accessible Learning Center Microsoft Word Lesson 6 Bulleted and Numbered Lists Goal Create structured bulleted and numbered lists that screen readers can recognize. Instructions Create a blank Word document. Type the heading
entries.text: word lesson 6 microsoft word lesson 6  word lesson 6 - accessible learning center microsoft word lesson 6 bulleted and numbered lists goal create structured bulleted and numbered lists that screen readers can recognize. instructions create a blank word document. type the heading: daily technology checklist apply heading 1. press enter and return to normal style. press ctrl+shift+l to begin a bulleted list. enter: check email enter: review calendar enter: complete assignments enter: save important files press enter twice to end the list. type the heading: steps for saving a document apply heading 2. create a numbered list containing: open the file menu, choose save as, choose a folder, enter a filename, and choose save. save the file as word-lesson-6.docx. your assignment submit word-lesson-6.docx . before submitting the document should contain one true bulleted list. the document should contain one true numbered list. headings should use built-in heading styles. view my progress return to lessons word lesson 6.html

entries.title: Microsoft Word Lesson 7
entries.snippet: Word Lesson 7 - Accessible Learning Center Microsoft Word Lesson 7 Creating Accessible Tables Goal Learn to create and navigate a simple table with a header row. Instructions Create a blank Word document. Type the heading: Training Schedule
entries.text: word lesson 7 microsoft word lesson 7  word lesson 7 - accessible learning center microsoft word lesson 7 creating accessible tables goal learn to create and navigate a simple table with a header row. instructions create a blank word document. type the heading: training schedule apply heading 1. insert a table with 3 columns and 4 rows. use these column headings in the first row: topic, date, status. enter microsoft word, monday, complete in the second row. enter excel, tuesday, in progress in the third row. enter powerpoint, wednesday, not started in the fourth row. make the first row the table's header row. use tab and shift+tab to move through the cells. avoid merged or split cells. save the file as word-lesson-7.docx. your assignment submit word-lesson-7.docx . before submitting the table should contain 3 columns and 4 rows. the first row should contain topic, date, and status. the first row should be designated as a header row. the table should not contain merged cells. view my progress return to lessons word lesson 7.html

entries.title: Microsoft Word Lesson 8
entries.snippet: Word Lesson 8 - Accessible Learning Center Microsoft Word Lesson 8 Links, Alt Text, and Accessibility Goal Practice creating meaningful links, working with images, and checking document accessibility. Instructions Create a blank Word docume
entries.text: word lesson 8 microsoft word lesson 8  word lesson 8 - accessible learning center microsoft word lesson 8 links, alt text, and accessibility goal practice creating meaningful links, working with images, and checking document accessibility. instructions create a blank word document. type the heading: accessible documents apply heading 1. type: accessible documents can be used effectively by people with disabilities. press enter twice. type the words microsoft accessibility. select those words. press ctrl+k. enter a microsoft accessibility web address. confirm that the visible link text remains microsoft accessibility instead of displaying only a raw url. if you are able to insert an image, add one practice image. add concise alt text describing the image's purpose. if the image is decorative, mark it decorative instead. open review and run accessibility checker or accessibility assistant. correct any accessibility problems you can identify. save as word-lesson-8.docx. your assignment submit word-lesson-8.docx . before submitting the document should contain a real heading 1. the hyperlink should have meaningful text. any informative image should have alt text. accessibility checker should have been reviewed. view my progress return to lessons word lesson 8.html

entries.title: Microsoft Word Lesson 9
entries.snippet: Word Lesson 9 - Accessible Learning Center Microsoft Word Lesson 9 Spelling, Comments, and Track Changes Goal Practice reviewing a document using Word's spelling, comment, and revision tools. Instructions Create a new document. Type: This s
entries.text: word lesson 9 microsoft word lesson 9  word lesson 9 - accessible learning center microsoft word lesson 9 spelling, comments, and track changes goal practice reviewing a document using word's spelling, comment, and revision tools. instructions create a new document. type: this sentance contains a spelling mistake. press f7 to open editor or spelling and grammar review. correct sentance to sentence. type another paragraph containing at least two sentences. select one word or phrase. press ctrl+alt+m to create a comment. type: review this section. post the comment. press ctrl+shift+e to turn on track changes. add one word to the paragraph. delete one word. press ctrl+shift+e again to stop tracking new changes. use the review tab to inspect the tracked changes. accept one change. reject the other change. save as word-lesson-9.docx. your assignment submit word-lesson-9.docx . before submitting the spelling error should be corrected. the document should contain a comment. you should have practiced track changes. one change should have been accepted and one rejected. view my progress return to lessons word lesson 9.html

slide placeholders with the keyboard, and save the file. skills practiced understand presentations, slides, layouts, and placeholders. move among powerpoint panes with f6. move among objects with tab area, thumbnails pane, notes pane, and ribbon. return to the slide area. press tab to move between the title and subtitle placeholders. type workplace technology training in the title placeholder. move to the subtitle placeholder and type prepared by followed by a fictional name. press ctrl+m to create a new slide. type training goals in the title placeholder. in the content placeholder, enter learn keyboard commands, practice accessible documents, and complete workplace assignments as separate lines. press page up and page down in the thumbnails pane to review both slides. press ctrl+s and save the presentation as powerpoint-lesson-1.pptx. keyboard help: press alt+q to search powerpoint commands when ribbon keytips differ. for jaws help, press insert+spacebar, then j, and search for the task. your assignment create a two-slide workplace technology training presentation with a title slide and a training goals slide. save the finished assignment as powerpoint-lesson-1.pptx . before meaningful image with alt text. include either an accessible table or a chart with alt text, source values, and a text summary. include at least one meaningful hyperlink. check the reading order on every slide. use strong contrast and do not communicate by color alone. add concise speaker notes to every content slide. run check accessibility and resolve applicable errors and warnings. present the entire deck using only the keyboard. save the presentation as powerpoint-lesson-10-final.pptx. keyboard help: press alt+q to search powerpoint commands when ribbon keytips differ. for jaws help, accessibility features. save the finished assignment as powerpoint-lesson-10-final.pptx . before submitting the deck contains at least seven logically ordered slides. every slide has a unique title entries.text: powerpoint lesson 6 powerpoint lesson 6 accessible microsoft powerpoint lesson 6: accessible tables and charts. powerpoint lesson 6 - accessible learning center microsoft powerpoint course powerpoint lesson 6 accessible tables and charts powerpoint manual all powerpoint lessons my progress goal present structured data with clear headers, accessible descriptions, and a text summary. skills practiced insert a simple table. use a header row. create a chart from clear source data. add alt text and a text equivalent. step-by-step instructions create a presentation titled monthly training report. add a slide titled training completion table. use alt+q to find insert table. create a table with three columns and five rows. enter the headers month, enrolled, and completed in the first row. enter fictional data for january through april. confirm that the first row is designated as a header row through table design options. add a slide titled completion trend. create a simple chart from the same data using insert chart and its data worksheet. add alt text describing the chart's purpose and main trend. keep the table slide so exact values remain available. add a short text statement on the chart slide summarizing the trend without relying on color. run check accessibility and review the table and chart. save the presentation as powerpoint-lesson-6.pptx. keyboard help: press alt+q to search powerpoint commands when ribbon keytips differ. for jaws help, press insert+spacebar, then j, and search for the task. your assignment create a training report containing an accessible table, a chart with alt text, and a plain-text trend summary. save the finished assignment as powerpoint-lesson-6.pptx . before submitting the table has descriptive column headers. the chart has meaningful alt text. exact values remain available in the table. the trend is explained in text. the file is saved as powerpoint-lesson-6.pptx. previous lesson next lesson powerpoint lesson 6.html

powerpoint course powerpoint lesson 7 meaningful links and contact information powerpoint manual all powerpoint lessons my progress goal add links that clearly identify their destination and work with keyboard navigation. skills practiced insert a hyperlink with ctrl+k. write meaningful link text. add an email link. test links without relying on their visual appearance. step-by-step instructions create a presentation titled new employee resources. add a slide titled technology resources. type microsoft accessibility help, select the text, and press ctrl+k. enter https://support.microsoft.com/accessibility as the address and confirm the dialog. add the meaningful link text freedom scientific jaws training and link it to https://www.freedomscientific.com/training/jaws/. add a slide titled department contacts. enter a fictional contact name and email address. use ctrl+k to create a mailto link if appropriate. avoid link text such as click here or read more because it does not identify the destination. press tab through the slide objects and listen to each link with jaws. use shift+f10 and edit link if a destination needs correction. run check accessibility and review link-related suggestions. save the presentation as powerpoint-lesson-7.pptx. keyboard help: press alt+q to search powerpoint commands when ribbon keytips differ. for jaws help, press insert+spacebar, then j, and search for the task. your assignment create a three-slide employee-resources presentation with two meaningful web links and one fictional department contact. save the finished assignment as powerpoint-lesson-7.pptx . before submitting link text explains each destination. no link uses vague text such as click here. the entries.title: PowerPoint Lesson 8
entries.snippet: Accessible Microsoft PowerPoint Lesson 8: Color, Contrast, Fonts, and Accessible Design.
entries.text: powerpoint lesson 8 powerpoint lesson 8 accessible microsoft powerpoint lesson 8: color, contrast, fonts, and accessible design. powerpoint lesson 8 - accessible learning center microsoft powerpoint course powerpoint lesson 8 color, contrast, fonts, and accessible design powerpoint manual all powerpoint lessons my progress goal apply a professional design that remains readable with low vision and does not communicate by color alone. skills practiced use a consistent built-in theme. check text and background contrast. use readable font sizes. add text labels for color-coded information. step-by-step instructions open powerpoint-lesson-7.pptx. use alt+q to search for themes and choose a simple built-in theme. keep body text large enough to read from a distance. use approximately 18 points or larger for body text and larger sizes for titles when the layout allows. keep strong contrast between text and its background. do not place text over a busy image unless a solid background makes it readable. if a status is shown in red, yellow, or green, also write words such as needs action, in progress, or complete. avoid rapidly flashing content and excessive animations. keep the same typeface and heading treatment across slides. review each slide at increased zoom and with jaws object navigation. run check accessibility and fix contrast or color-use warnings when available. save the presentation as powerpoint-lesson-8.pptx. keyboard help: press alt+q to search powerpoint commands when ribbon keytips differ. for jaws help, press insert+spacebar, then j, and search for the task. your assignment apply a consistent, high-contrast design to the employee-resources presentation and ensure no meaning depends on color alone. save the finished assignment as powerpoint-lesson-8.pptx . before submitting text and backgrounds have strong contrast. body text is readable and not crowded. color-coded information also includes text labels. the design is consistent across slides. the file is saved as powerpoint-lesson-8.pptx. previous lesson next lesson powerpoint lesson 8.html

entries.title: Screen Readers Lesson 1

entries.text: screen readers lesson 1 screen readers lesson 1 accessible screen-reader lesson 1: choose, start, and stop a screen reader, with jaws, narrator, and nvda options. screen readers lesson 1 - accessible learning center screen readers course screen readers lesson 1 choose, start, and stop a screen reader screen readers manual all screen readers lessons my progress choose your screen reader complete this lesson with jaws, windows narrator, or nvda . use one primary screen reader at a time. follow the column for your selection whenever commands differ. goal choose jaws, narrator, or nvda and start and stop it safely. shared practice steps choose one primary screen reader for this course. do not run multiple screen readers at the same time unless an instructor directs you. confirm that the computer’s speakers or headset are connected and the volume is safe. start the selected screen reader using its method in the comparison table. open notepad and type one short sentence. confirm the screen reader announces the application, focus, and typed text. save the note and stop the screen reader using its documented method. jaws, narrator, and nvda comparison commands and differences for lesson 1 task jaws narrator nvda start search for jaws from start; a configured desktop shortcut may also be available. press windows+ctrl+enter. press ctrl+alt+n if the installation created that shortcut, or search for nvda from start. screen-reader modifier jaws key: insert; caps lock may be configured on laptops. narrator key: caps lock or insert by default. nvda key: insert or caps lock, based on keyboard layout. stop or exit press insert+f4 and confirm exit. press windows+ctrl+enter. press nvda+q and confirm exit. command note: jaws key, narrator key, and nvda key each mean that screen reader’s modifier key. commands can vary by keyboard layout, software version, application, and user settings. confirm differences in the official references linked from the manual. your assignment create a one-page choice report naming the selected screen reader, why it fits the practice computer, and how to start and stop it. use fictional, public, instructor-provided, or redacted information only. never submit passwords, license information, account codes, or private workplace data. save your work with a filename beginning screen-readers-lesson-1 . before submitting the selected screen reader is named. the commands match jaws, narrator, or nvda. shared windows commands are distinguished from screen-reader commands. the file contains no credentials or sensitive information. next lesson jaws lesson 1.html

upported screen readers. part 17 - folder backup personal onedrive can back up supported windows folders such as desktop, documents, and pictures through onedrive folder backup. availability differs for work/school accounts and administrator policy. 17.1 review folder backup settings what you will learn: understand which windows folders are being redirected/backed up. before you begin: onedrive personal account is configured where supported. exactly how to do it open onedrive settings. find sync and backup or manage backup. review desktop, documents, pictures, and any other offered folders. do not turn a backup off/on casually if those folders contain important work. close settings without changing anything until you understand the current configuration. what should happen: you know which important windows folders are stored in onedrive. if that does not happen: if backup controls are unavailable, the account/policy may not support them. practice: review backup state only. part 18 - shared and recent items 18.1 open shared or recent on the web what you will learn: locate cloud files outside my files. before you begin: onedrive.com is open. exactly how to do it use tab/ctrl+f6 to reach the navigation area. move to shared or recent. press enter. move through the items. check the owner/source before opening unfamiliar shared files. what should happen: shared or recent items are listed. if that does not happen: if an item appears in shared but not my files, it may belong to another person and your actions can be permission-limited. practice: review one shared item without changing it. part 19 - narrator with onedrive microsoft tests onedrive accessibility with narrator. in file explorer, use normal windows focus/navigation. on the web, narrator scan mode may need to be adjusted when onedrive needs direct grid/command interaction. 19.1 use narrator in file explorer onedrive what you will learn: navigate synced files with standard windows commands. before you begin: narrator is on and file explorer is open. exactly how to do it press f6 until the navigation pane is announced. move to onedrive. press enter. press f6 until the file list is active. use arrow keys through files. press narrator+tab if you need narrator to repeat the current item. press enter to open a safe file/folder. what should happen: narrator follows file explorer focus and announces onedrive items. if that does not happen: if narrator is reading unrelated controls, use f6/shift+f6 to return to the file list. practice: navigate five onedrive items. 19.2 use narrator on onedrive web what you will learn: interact with the onedrive web grid and commands. before you begin: narrator is on and onedrive.com is open. exactly how to do it use ctrl+f6/f6 to reach onedrive content. turn scan mode off with narrator+spacebar if arrow/space commands need direct interaction. use up/down arrow through files. press spacebar to select. press enter to open. turn scan mode on temporarily when page-style reading is useful. what should happen: narrator supports both direct application interaction and normal webpage review. if that does not happen: if letters/arrows move webpage structure instead of onedrive items, verify the current scan mode state. practice: select and open a practice folder. part 20 - nvda with onedrive 20.1 use nvda in file explorer what you will learn: navigate onedrive files through windows. before you begin: nvda is running. exactly how to do it press windows+e. move to onedrive in the navigation pane. enter the folder. use arrow keys through items. press nvda+tab to repeat the focused item when needed. use f2, enter, shift+f10, and standard file explorer commands normally. what should happen: nvda follows the active onedrive file/folder. if that does not happen: if nvda announces another region, use f6 to return to the file list. practice: rename a disposable practice item and undo the rename manually. 20.2 use nvda on onedrive web what you will learn: use direct focus mode when the content grid needs application interaction. before you begin: onedrive.com is open. exactly how to do it press nvda+space to enter focus mode when needed. use tab/ctrl+f6 to reach my files/content grid. use arrow keys through items. press spacebar to select and enter to open. return to browse mode only when you intentionally want normal webpage reading. what should happen: onedrive receives direct grid commands. if that does not happen: if h/k quick keys take over, nvda is in browse mode. practice: navigate and select three items. part 21 - jaws with onedrive 21.1 use jaws in file explorer onedrive what you will learn: use normal windows file commands with jaws feedback. before you begin: jaws is running. exactly how to do it open file explorer with windows+e. navigate to onedrive. move through items with arrow keys. press insert+tab to repeat the current item when useful. use enter/f2/shift+f10/delete as standard file explorer commands. what should happen: jaws announces item names and states. if that does not happen: if jaws quick navigation is acting like a webpage, verify file explorer is the active application. practice: navigate and inspect five items. 21.2 use jaws on onedrive web what you will learn: let onedrive receive its grid/application commands. before you begin: onedrive.com is open. exactly how to do it press jaws+z to turn the virtual pc cursor off when direct grid interaction is needed. use ctrl+f6/tab to reach files. use arrow keys through items. press spacebar to select. press s to share in supported work/school web contexts or use the command bar/context menu. turn virtual pc cursor on temporarily only for page-style review, then off again. what should happen: onedrive shortcuts and jaws focus work together. if that does not happen: if h or other jaws quick keys take over, virtual pc cursor is on. practice: open the web content grid and select one item. part 22 - voiceover on mac microsoft documents onedrive for work or school with voiceover on macos, including synced files in finder. 22.1 navigate synced onedrive in finder what you will learn: use onedrive as a normal finder location on mac. before you begin: onedrive is configured and signed in. exactly how to do it open finder. use voiceover navigation to the sidebar. locate onedrive or the organization onedrive location. interact with the file list. use vo+arrow commands to move among files/folders. open the selected item with command+o or the finder activation method. what should happen: voiceover follows synced onedrive files in finder. if that does not happen: if onedrive is absent, open the onedrive app and verify sync setup. practice: open onedrive and identify three files. part 23 - braille displays braille support comes through narrator, nvda, jaws, or voiceover. onedrive exposes the same file names, statuses, web controls, and dialogs that the screen reader converts to braille. 23.1 test braille with onedrive what you will learn: verify local and web navigation. before you begin: configure the braille display in the active screen reader. exactly how to do it open onedrive in file explorer. move through several filenames and confirm braille changes. open onedrive.com. move to my files. navigate file names and sharing controls. use routing keys where supported in search/edit fields. what should happen: braille follows both file explorer and onedrive web focus. if that does not happen: if braille works elsewhere but not onedrive, check app/browser focus and screen-reader mode before changing braille settings. practice: test output, input, and routing. part 24 - iphone/ipad and android 24.1 iphone/ipad with voiceover swipe right/left to move voiceover focus; double-tap to activate. use files/my files to locate content. use add/new to upload or create items when available. use more actions for share, download/make available offline, move, rename, and delete. review the recipient and permission before sharing. 24.2 android with talkback swipe right/left to move talkback focus; double-tap to activate. use files/my files to navigate onedrive content. use more actions for share, save offline, move, rename, and delete. be aware that offline/downloaded copies use device storage. verify the account when multiple microsoft/work accounts are configured. part 25 - security and privacy verify whether you are in personal or work onedrive before uploading confidential information. use the least-powerful sharing permission that meets the need. avoid broad anonymous/anyone links for sensitive files. do not open unexpected shared files until you verify the sender. remember that synced deletion/rename/move actions propagate to other devices. do not free up local space on files you need while offline. organization onedrive can be subject to retention, auditing, legal hold, and administrator access policies. treat browser downloads from onedrive like any downloaded file: verify filename, type, and source before opening. 25.1 review an unexpected shared file what you will learn: verify ownership before opening suspicious content. before you begin: a file was shared unexpectedly. exactly how to do it open onedrive shared view. read the filename and owner. open details instead of opening the file when possible. verify the sender through a trusted channel. do not download or open risky file types until verified. what should happen: you decide whether to trust the file before opening it. if that does not happen: if the sender cannot be verified, leave the file unopened and report/block through available organizational processes. practice: inspect one safe shared item. part 26 - troubleshooting 26.1 onedrive is missing from file explorer what you will learn: restore sync access without assuming files are gone. before you begin: windows is running. exactly how to do it press windows key and type onedrive. open onedrive. sign in if prompted. open onedrive settings and confirm the intended account. open file explorer again and check the navigation pane. what should happen: the onedrive location reappears when setup is valid. if that does not happen: if the organization disabled sync, use onedrive on the web instead. practice: locate the onedrive app and account. 26.2 a file is visible but will not open offline what you will learn: check files on-demand status. before you begin: you are offline or have unstable internet. exactly how to do it open the file context menu. look for always keep on this device. if the file is cloud-only and you have internet again, choose always keep on this device and wait for download. do not assume cloud-only files are corrupt merely because they cannot open offline. what should happen: the file becomes available locally once downloaded. if that does not happen: if download fails, resolve sync/network issues first. practice: identify one file suitable for offline access. 26.3 a file change does not appear on another device what you will learn: check sync completion before making duplicate edits. before you begin: the same onedrive account is used on both devices. exactly how to do it open onedrive sync status on the first device. confirm the file finished syncing. check network connectivity. on the second device, allow time for sync and refresh/reopen the folder. confirm both devices are signed in to the same onedrive account/location. what should happen: the same file version appears after sync. if that does not happen: if conflicts exist, preserve both copies until you know which version contains needed changes. practice: review current sync status. 26.4 you deleted the wrong file what you will learn: use recycle bin before trying to recreate the file. before you begin: the file was recently deleted from onedrive. exactly how to do it open onedrive.com. open recycle bin. find the file. select it. activate restore. search my files for the restored file. what should happen: the file is restored if still retained. if that does not happen: if permanently deleted or past retention, contact your organization/admin promptly when applicable. practice: restore the practice deletion. 26.5 onedrive web keyboard commands behave like browser commands what you will learn: identify web focus and mode. before you begin: onedrive.com is open. exactly how to do it press escape to close dialogs. use ctrl+f6/f6 to move into onedrive. narrator: turn scan mode off when direct interaction is needed. nvda: enter focus mode. jaws: turn virtual pc cursor off. try arrow/space/enter in the files grid. what should happen: onedrive receives its own interaction keys. if that does not happen: if ctrl+o or another shortcut opens browser ui, remember that some shortcuts belong to the browser in onedrive web. practice: practice moving between browser and onedrive. part 27 - independent practice course
