and does not use the zoomax s1 through s4 arrangement. important: both models have 20 braille cells and perkins-style keys, but their navigation and file commands are not interchangeable. humanware model: basic and advanced how-tos keyboard commands: humanware ereader commands use braille chords, thumb keys, enter, and backspace as described in each task. return to the main menu and open a book device commands: space with m, dots 1-3-4, opens the main menu. up and down thumb keys move through items. enter opens the selected item. press space with m. move to book reader and press enter. open book list. use the thumb keys to find the intended title. press enter and use the panning keys to read. you should feel: the selected title followed by its opening text. if that does not happen: press space with m once and confirm whether book reader stopped or another message is displayed. navigate, search, and identify your position device commands: space+dot 1 or space+dot 4 moves by paragraph; space+dot 2 or space+dot 5 moves by page; space+f, dots 1-2-4, searches; space with the w-h sign, dots 1-5-6, gives where am i. open a practice book. move forward and backward by paragraph, then by page. press space+f, type a word, and press enter. use space+n for the next result or space+p for the previous result. press space with dots 1-5-6 to confirm the location. if that does not happen: check spelling and whether the search started after the current position. insert and return to a bookmark device commands: enter+b, dots 1-2, inserts a quick bookmark. enter+j, dots 2-4-5, opens the bookmark list. move to a passage you want to save. press enter+b and note the bookmark confirmation. move several pages away. press enter+j, enter the bookmark number if requested, and press enter. use where am i to verify the restored position. if that does not happen: open the bookmark menu with enter+m and inspect saved bookmark numbers. find and download a bard title connect to a trusted wi-fi network. press space+m and open online services, then nls bard. open search collection, enter a title, author, or keyword, and press enter. move through results and press enter for title information. choose download or download then open. wait for completion, return to book reader, and confirm the title in book list. if that does not happen: check the wi-fi and bard status. never include bard credentials in a lesson file. manage a file without losing it device commands: space+d selects a drive; space+i gives information; backspace+c copies; backspace+x cuts; backspace+v pastes. open file manager and press space+d to select the drive. use thumb keys to select the file and press space+i to confirm its name and location. use backspace+c to preserve the original or backspace+x only when moving it. open the verified destination and press backspace+v. confirm both source and destination before deleting anything. if that does not happen: preserve every copy and check available storage with space+i. zoomax model: basic and advanced how-tos return to the main menu and open a book device commands: s1 or space with m, dots 1-3-4, opens the main menu. navigate up or down with n-up, n-down, d1, d3, d4, or d6. dot 8, n-center, or a cursor router activates the selected item. press s1. move to book reader and press enter. open book list. move through titles until the intended book is displayed. press enter and use d2 or the left panning key to pan left; use d5 or the right panning key to pan right. you should feel: the selected title followed by its opening text. if that does not happen: press s1 once and check for a startup, storage, or error message before reopening book reader. navigate and identify your reading position device commands: dot 1 moves to the previous paragraph and dot 4 to the next paragraph. dot 2 moves to the previous page and dot 5 to the next page. space with the w-h sign, dots 1-5-6, gives the current position. open a practice book. move forward and backward by paragraph. move forward and backward by page. press space with dots 1-5-6. read the reported page, volume, and position information. if that does not happen: confirm that focus is inside the open book rather than book list or a menu. search for text device commands: space with f, dots 1-2-4, opens find. space with n, dots 1-3-4-5, finds the next occurrence; space with p, dots 1-2-3-4, finds the previous occurrence. move to a known point in the book. press space+f, type the search term, and press enter. read the surrounding line to confirm the match. press space+n for the next match or space+p to move backward. use where am i to record the result’s location. if that does not happen: check spelling, braille grade, and whether the search begins from the current position. create and return to a bookmark device approach: press s3 for the context menu, then select the bookmark command shown for the current book. move to the passage you want to save. press s3 and find set bookmark. activate it and confirm the bookmark message. move several pages away. open the context menu again, choose go to bookmark, select the bookmark, and press enter. use where am i to verify the restored position. if that does not happen: confirm that the book supports bookmarks and that the bookmark was created in the current title. find and download a bard title device command: space with a, dot 1, opens bard from anywhere after the device is configured. connect to trusted wi-fi and press space+a. choose a title, author, subject, or keyword search. enter the search text and press enter. move through results, open the intended title, and review its information. choose download or the current download-and-open option. wait for completion, then open book list and verify the title. if that does not happen: check wi-fi and bard sign-in status without putting credentials in a lesson file. use file manager safely device commands: space with f, dots 1-2-4, opens file manager. s2 opens the application menu; s3 opens the context menu. press space+f and identify the current drive and folder. move to the file and confirm its complete name. press s3 and choose copy when the original must remain, or move only when relocation is intended. navigate to the destination folder and use its context or application menu to paste. verify both locations before deleting anything. if that does not happen: preserve every copy and check available storage before repeating the operation. connect the zoomax ereader as a braille display device commands: space with t, dots 2-3-4-5, toggles bluetooth. the power on quick menu also offers bluetooth and usb modes. save current reading position and work. choose bluetooth or usb mode on the ereader. on the computer or mobile device, open the screen reader’s braille-display settings. select the nls ereader zoomax and complete pairing or usb setup. move focus on the host device and verify matching braille. if that does not happen: confirm the selected mode, cable or bluetooth state, screen-reader display choice, and paired device before restarting. ten-lesson learning path lesson 1: orientation, power, and main menu — create a tactile orientation and power checklist. lesson 2: bookshelf and file organization — submit a bookshelf navigation log. lesson 3: read and navigate a book — create a reading-navigation command reference. lesson 4: search, bookmarks, and reading position — submit a search-and-bookmark report. lesson 5: notes and the editor — create nls-ereader-lesson-5.txt or brf. lesson 6: obtain and transfer nls bard content — write a credential-free bard transfer checklist. lesson 7: terminal mode and computer connection — submit a terminal-mode connection log or a model-capability report. lesson 8: settings, language, and status — create a settings inventory without serial numbers. lesson 9: safe troubleshooting and updates — create a safe troubleshooting decision guide. lesson 10: final independent reading project — complete an independent accessible-reading workflow. accessible working routine confirm the window, document, device, or webpage title. identify keyboard focus before typing or activating a control. navigate by real structure—headings, lists, fields, tables, or menus—when available. review the result with jaws or a braille display from beginning to end. verify the destination and filename before saving, uploading, sharing, or deleting. save the requested practice file locally with the exact filename given in the lesson. assignment uploads are currently paused. important: these course controls complement, and do not replace, browser, operating-system, screen-reader, braille-display, or other assistive-technology settings. official references use these primary sources when a label or command differs from the lesson: nls braille ereader resources nls humanware ereader user guide nls zoomax ereader user guide start nls braille ereader lesson 1 return to manuals

entries.title: NLS Braille eReader EMZ-20 Manual
entries.snippet: NLS Braille eReader EMZ-20 Manual: step-by-step keyboard and screen-reader instructions, practice, troubleshooting, and command references.
entries.text: nls braille ereader emz-20 manual - accessible learning center skip to main content accessible learning center manual nls braille ereader emz-20 manual zoomax 20-cell refreshable braille ereader independent self-study guide all manuals table of contents start of manual model emz-20 • nls talking book program official nls braille ereader zoomax user guide purpose: this manual is written directly to the person learning the nls braille ereader model emz-20. it assumes you may be touching the device for the first time. every procedure identifies exactly where a button or port is located, what to press, what should appear on the 20-cell braille display, and what to do if the result is different. device identity: the emz-20 is the zoomax version of the nls braille ereader. nls also distributes a different humanware 20-cell ereader. the button layout and commands are not interchangeable. official reference: this manual is original training material based on the current nls braille ereader zoomax user guide and getting started information from the national library service for the blind and print disabled, library of congress. how to use this manual begin with parts 1 through 7 even if you already know braille. they teach the physical layout and command system used throughout the rest of the device. orient the device with the 20 braille cells closest to your body unless a procedure says otherwise. dot 7 is the backspace key. dot 8 is the enter key. the six display keys are d1, d2, d3 on the left and d4, d5, d6 on the right. the four system keys are s1 and s2 on the far-left front area, and s3 and s4 on the far-right front area. the two large rectangular front keys are bl and br. they act like space for many commands and act as panning keys while reading a book. the five center navigation keys are n-left, n-up, n-right, n-down, and n-center. do one action, then stop and read the display before pressing another key. when you forget a command, use s3 to open the context menu or open help from the main menu. table of contents part 1 - identify the emz-20 and what it does part 2 - physical layout: top surface part 3 - physical layout: front controls identify the emz-20 and what it does the emz-20 is the zoomax nls braille ereader. it is a 20-cell refreshable braille display and standalone electronic braille reader distributed through nls network libraries. it can read electronic braille and other supported documents, download nls content through bard, use external storage, and function as a braille display for compatible computers and apple mobile devices. 20 refreshable braille cells with a routing button behind each cell. eight-key perkins-style braille keyboard: dots 1 through 8. three space-key locations: the center space key plus bl and br for many chord commands. six display keys: d1 through d6. four system keys: s1 through s4. five navigation keys: n-left, n-up, n-right, n-down, and n-center. usb-c for charging and computer connection. usb-a for nls cartridge cable or usb flash drive. sd-card slot for external storage. wi-fi for bard and nfb-newsline. bluetooth for compatible external screen-reader devices. part 2 - physical layout: top surface 2.1 orient the device correctly what you will learn: place the emz-20 in the correct position before learning any buttons. before you begin: place the device on a stable surface. exactly how to do it find the long row of 20 refreshable braille cells. rotate the device until those cells are closest to your body. keep the device in that orientation for all physical descriptions in this manual. place both index fingers lightly on the braille cells and move from the leftmost cell to the rightmost cell. move your fingertips slightly toward the back of the device. directly behind each braille cell is a small round cursor-routing button. move farther toward the back to locate the perkins-style braille keyboard. what should happen: the braille cells are along the front/top edge closest to you, routing buttons are immediately behind them, and the braille keyboard is farther back. if that does not happen: if you cannot identify the row of 20 cells, do not press keys. rotate the unit until the long line of braille cells is nearest you. practice: with the unit powered off, find cells, routing buttons, and keyboard three times. 2.2 learn the perkins keyboard by touch layout: from the center toward the left are dots 1, 2, 3, and dot 7. from the center toward the right are dots 4, 5, 6, and dot 8. dot 7 also serves as backspace; dot 8 also serves as enter. the space key is centered below/between the braille input groups. left-hand group from inner to outer: dot 1, dot 2, dot 3, dot 7. right-hand group from inner to outer: dot 4, dot 5, dot 6, dot 8. dot 7 = backspace. dot 8 = enter. center space is used by itself and in chord commands. part 3 - physical layout: front controls along the angled front panel closest to you are eleven controls. learn them by moving from the outside edges toward the center. control where it is main purpose s1 far-left outer small round system key main menu s2 second small round key from far-left menu for the current application bl large rectangular key left of center acts as space for many chords; pans backward while reading a book n-left left directional navigation key in center cluster move left/backward in books or hierarchy n-up upper directional navigation key move up in menus/lists; previous line in a book n-center middle of navigation cluster select/activate in supported contexts n-right right directional navigation key move right/forward in books or hierarchy n-down lower directional navigation key move down in menus/lists; next line in a book br large rectangular key right of center acts as space for many chords; pans forward while reading a book s3 second small round key from far-right context menu s4 far-right outer small round key open current book at last reading position keyboard lock: pressing s1 and s4 together toggles keyboard lock. when locked, the display reads keyboard locked. press s1+s4 again, or use the power on button as described by nls, to unlock. part 4 - physical layout: left and right sides 4.1 left side with the braille cells closest to you, feel along the left side from front to back. front corner: lanyard attachment point. behind the lanyard point: sd-card slot. the braille letters “sd” are above the sd-card slot. 4.2 right side with the braille cells closest to you, feel along the right side from front to back. the order is critical because this is where power and charging are located. front corner: lanyard attachment point. immediately behind it: small round power on button. braille “on” is above it. immediately behind power on: small round power off button. braille “off” is above it. behind the power buttons: usb-c port. this is the charging port and the port used for usb computer connection. farthest toward the back: usb-a port. this accepts a usb flash drive or the nls cartridge cable. braille “usb” is centered over the two usb ports, with “c” over usb-c and “a” over usb-a. back edge: the back edge has no buttons or ports. part 5 - charging the battery 5.1 charge the emz-20 what you will learn: connect the correct cable to the correct port. before you begin: orient the device with the braille cells closest to you. find the right side. exactly how to do it feel from the front-right lanyard point toward the back: power on, power off, then usb-c. stop at usb-c. it is directly behind the two power buttons. take the smaller usb-c end of the supplied charging cable. insert it into the usb-c port. usb-c is reversible, so either orientation is acceptable. connect the larger usb-a end to the supplied ac adapter. plug the ac adapter into a wall outlet. allow about three hours for a full charge when needed. the original zoomax guide describes roughly ten hours of use per charge; actual battery life varies with settings, battery age, wireless use, and power-saving behavior. what should happen: the ereader charges through the usb-c port on the right side behind the power off button. if that does not happen: if the plug does not enter easily, stop and make sure you are at usb-c rather than the usb-a port. never force the connector. try the supplied adapter/cable and another outlet if charging does not begin. practice: locate usb-c correctly three times before connecting power. part 6 - power on, power off, and suspend 6.1 turn the emz-20 on what you will learn: start the device and recognize the startup sequence. before you begin: charge the ereader first. exactly how to do it orient the device with braille cells closest to you. on the right side, start at the front lanyard point and move slightly toward the back to the first small round button. this is power on. press the power on button once. listen for three ascending tones. read the display. “starting” appears briefly, followed by “nls ereader zoomax,” then startup progress. wait. do not press navigation keys while startup is still occurring. when startup finishes, you hear another ascending tone sequence and the display reaches the main menu, normally at book reader. what should happen: book reader or the top main menu item appears and the ereader is ready. if that does not happen: if nothing happens, connect power and try power on again. make sure you pressed the first of the two small round power buttons, not power off. practice: power the unit on and identify when startup is complete. 6.2 turn the emz-20 off what you will learn: shut down without confusing power off with suspend. before you begin: save/finish any current task first. exactly how to do it on the right side, find the two small round power buttons. power off is the second one, directly behind power on. press power off once. listen for descending tones and read the off menu. move to power off if it is not already selected. press enter (dot 8), n-center, or the routing button corresponding to the power off choice as appropriate. wait while shutdown progress appears. do not disconnect power or press other keys until shutdown is complete. what should happen: the display goes blank after the shutdown sequence. if that does not happen: if the device enters suspend instead, wake it with power on and repeat, carefully selecting power off from the off menu. practice: practice locating power on and power off by touch while the device is already off. 6.3 suspend mode suspend uses less power and lets you resume quickly. the ereader can enter suspend after inactivity according to its settings. you can also select suspend from the main menu or from the menu opened with the power off button. wake from suspend by pressing power on. part 7 - learn the braille keyboard braille letters and commands are entered with dot keys and space. commands written as “space with letter” mean hold space while pressing the dots that form that braille letter, then release. task command backspace dot 7 enter dot 8 escape / back space+e (dots 1-5) main menu s1 or space+m (dots 1-3-4) top of list/document space+dots 1-2-3 bottom of list/document space+dots 4-5-6 switch braille grade space+g (dots 1-2-4-5) battery level space+# (dots 3-4-5-6) context menu s3 part 8 - main menu the current zoomax nls guide organizes the main functions around these primary areas. firmware revisions can rename or reorganize an item, so use the built-in help/user guide if your menu wording differs. book reader online services (bard and nfb-newsline) file manager settings device info battery help suspend power off 8.1 return to the main menu from anywhere what you will learn: use a reliable “home” command when you get lost. before you begin: the device is on. exactly how to do it press s1, the far-left outer small round system key on the front panel. alternatively, hold space and press the braille letter m (dots 1-3-4). read the menu item now shown. use n-up/n-down to identify nearby main menu items. what should happen: you return to the main menu. if that does not happen: if the display reads keyboard locked, press s1+s4 together to unlock, then press s1 again. practice: from book reader, settings, and file manager, return to main menu. part 9 - menu navigation and first-letter navigation 9.1 move through menus what you will learn: choose menu items deliberately. before you begin: be on any menu. exactly how to do it press n-down once to move to the next item. you can also use d3. stop and read the 20-cell display. press n-down again only after identifying the current item. press n-up to move to the previous item. when the desired item is displayed, press enter (dot 8), n-center, or a cursor-routing button over the item where supported. what should happen: the selected menu/submenu opens. if that does not happen: if the wrong item opens, press space+e to go back and repeat one item at a time. practice: open settings and return to main menu. 9.2 use first-letter navigation what you will learn: jump to an item without stepping through every menu entry. before you begin: be in a menu or list that supports first-letter navigation. exactly how to do it type the first braille letter of the item you want. read the item that appears. if another item begins with the same letter, type the same letter again to move to the next matching item. press enter on the correct item. what should happen: the display jumps to an item beginning with that letter. if that does not happen: some book lists use first-letter typing as a filter rather than simply jumping. use backspace (dot 7) to clear the filter in bard lists. practice: from main menu, use the first letter for settings or file manager. part 10 - context menu and global commands 10.1 use the context menu what you will learn: find commands available for what you are currently doing. before you begin: be in a menu, file list, book, or other application context. exactly how to do it press s3, the small round system key second from the far-right side of the front panel. read the first context menu item. use n-up/n-down through actions. press enter or a routing button on the desired action. to cancel, press space+e (dots 1-5). what should happen: a context-specific action runs or the menu closes. if that does not happen: if s3 does not give the command you expected, the available actions may differ in the current application. use s2 for that application’s main menu or help for command lists. practice: open s3 in book reader and file manager and compare the options. part 11 - reading 20-cell braille and panning 11.1 pan through text longer than 20 cells what you will learn: read a line or paragraph in segments. before you begin: open a book or document. exactly how to do it read the current 20 cells from left to right. to move forward, press d5, n-right, or br while reading a book. read the next displayed segment. to move backward, press d2, n-left, or bl while reading a book. repeat until you have read the passage. what should happen: the display advances or retreats through the text. if that does not happen: if the keys move a menu selection rather than the text, you are probably not inside an open book/document. practice: read a passage requiring at least four pans and return to its beginning. part 12 - book reader basics 12.1 open book reader what you will learn: open the built-in reading application. before you begin: be at main menu. exactly how to do it use n-up/n-down until book reader appears, or type b until book reader is selected. press enter. read the book reader menu. choose current book to resume the last book, or book list to choose another title. press s4 from almost anywhere when you want to return directly to the current book at your last reading position. what should happen: a book opens or the book reader list appears. if that does not happen: if current book says the book is empty, open book list and choose an available title. practice: open a book, exit, then reopen it with s4. part 13 - book navigation by line, paragraph, page, volume, and article task command previous / next line d1 / d3, or n-up / n-down previous / next paragraph dot 1 / dot 4 previous / next page dot 2 or d1+d2 / dot 5 or d2+d3 previous / next volume dot 3 or d4+d5 / dot 6 or d5+d6 go to line l (dots 1-2-3) or d1+d2+d3 go to paragraph ch (dots 1-6) or d1+d6 go to page p (dots 1-2-3-4) or d1+d2+d3+d4 go to volume v (dots 1-2-3-6) or d1+d2+d3+d6 previous / next article dots 3-4-5-7 / dots 3-4-5-8 go to article > (dots 3-4-5) or d3+d4+d5 line behavior: book reader can be set so moving down a line goes to the left margin or keeps the same horizontal cell position. the documented toggle is k (dots 1-3). part 14 - where am i, autoscroll, word wrap, and reflow 14.1 find your position in a book what you will learn: ask the ereader where you are. before you begin: be inside an open book. exactly how to do it press the braille “wh” sign, dots 1-5-6. read the position information. note the volume, page, line, and character information that is available. dismiss the message with enter/n-center if needed. what should happen: position information appears. if that does not happen: if the command does not work, verify that the book has focus and consult help > keyboard commands for your firmware. practice: check your position before and after moving several pages. 14.2 use autoscroll what you will learn: read without manually pressing a pan key each display. before you begin: autoscroll must be enabled in book reader settings. exactly how to do it inside a book, press the braille st-sign, dots 3-4. read while the display advances automatically. to slow the rate, press dots 3-4 with dot 7. to increase the rate, press dots 3-4 with dot 8. press dots 3-4 again to stop autoscroll. what should happen: the display advances automatically at the selected speed. if that does not happen: if nothing happens, open settings > book reader settings and make sure autoscroll is on. practice: start autoscroll, change speed once, then stop it. word wrap and reflow: word wrap prevents ordinary words from being split across the 20-cell display. the documented word wrap toggle is w-chord (dots 2-4-5-6). book reflow can also be enabled in book reader settings to improve 20-cell presentation. part 15 - bard: wi-fi and first login before bard can be used directly from the ereader, the device must have a working wi-fi connection and permanent bard credentials. 15.1 open nls bard what you will learn: reach the bard application. before you begin: connect to wi-fi first. exactly how to do it press s1 for main menu. navigate to online services, or type o (dots 1-3-5). press enter. navigate to nls bard. press enter. what should happen: the nls bard menu opens. if that does not happen: if bard cannot access online content, confirm wi-fi connection under settings > wi-fi settings. practice: open bard and return to online services. 15.2 log in to bard the first time what you will learn: enter your bard credentials correctly in braille. before you begin: you need a permanent bard username/password; temporary passwords must be changed through a web browser first. exactly how to do it open nls bard. choose user login if you are not automatically prompted. enter your bard username in uncontracted ueb unless you intentionally select another input code from the context menu. enter your permanent bard password. for email addresses in ueb, enter the at-sign and period using correct ueb symbols; numbers require a number sign. if you prefer computer braille or another available input mode, press s3 and choose the desired code before entering credentials. confirm the login. what should happen: a successful login message appears and future bard sessions can log in automatically. if that does not happen: if login fails, verify the credentials on another device, make sure the password is permanent, and confirm your braille input code. practice: open the user login area and identify the fields without changing a working login. part 16 - bard: browse, search, download, and wish list the bard menu includes browse bard, search bard, wish list, user login, and exit. 16.1 download and open a book from bard what you will learn: find a title and begin reading it. before you begin: wi-fi and bard login must be working. exactly how to do it open bard. choose browse bard or search bard. if browsing, choose most recent books, most popular books, magazine issues, or previous downloads. if searching, choose book title, author name, subjects, or keyword. navigate the result list. in bard lists, typing letters filters titles; press backspace (dot 7) to clear the typed filter. press enter on a title for more information. read the title, author, and description as desired. navigate to download and open if you want to read immediately, or download if you want to continue browsing. press enter. wait for the download to complete. what should happen: the title is added to your book list; download and open also starts the book in book reader. if that does not happen: if download fails, verify wi-fi, bard login, and available device storage. practice: search for a known title and reach the information screen without downloading unless desired. wish list: from a book information screen or context menu, use add to wish list. the wish list area lets you review, download, and remove saved items. part 17 - nfb-newsline 17.1 sign in and download newsline material what you will learn: use an nfb-newsline account directly from the ereader. before you begin: you need wi-fi plus your nfb-newsline id and security code. exactly how to do it press s1 for main menu. open online services. open nfb newsline. the first time, enter your numeric newsline id preceded by the braille number sign. enter the numeric security code the same way. press enter and wait for “login successful.” open publication management. choose sync now to download the latest issues for subscribed/favorite publications. after downloading, return to book reader > book list to read the publications. what should happen: newsline material downloads and appears in book reader. if that does not happen: if login fails, confirm id/security code and wi-fi. practice: open publication management and identify sync now. reading newsline: nls states that newsline articles are usually navigation level 3 and sections usually level 2. while reading, use n-up/n-down to select a navigation level and n-left/n-right to move to the previous/next item at that level. part 18 - file manager 18.1 open and browse file manager what you will learn: find internal, usb, and sd files. before you begin: be at main menu. exactly how to do it navigate to file manager or type f (dots 1-2-4). press enter. the internal files area is always available. use n-up/n-down through storage locations. usb files and sd card files appear only when connected. press enter on a storage location. use n-up/n-down through folders/files. folder names have a slash symbol before them. press enter on a folder to open it. use n-left and n-right to navigate the folder hierarchy. what should happen: you can browse internal and attached storage. if that does not happen: if usb or sd does not appear, remove and reconnect it and wait for recognition. practice: open internal files, enter a folder, and return. 18.2 file manager menus press s2 for file manager menu: sort by name, type, date new first, size, or create directory. press s3 for file context menu: open, cut, copy, paste, rename, delete, file info, select, unselect, toggle selection, select all, and unselect all. part 19 - nls cartridge, usb flash drive, and sd card 19.1 copy an nls cartridge automatically what you will learn: load braille books from an nls cartridge. before you begin: use the supplied nls cartridge-to-usb cable. exactly how to do it orient the ereader with braille cells closest to you. on the right side, locate the farthest-back port: usb-a. connect the nls cartridge to the cartridge cable. connect the cable to the emz-20 usb-a port. wait for the recognition tones. wait for the progress indicator and “auto copy complete.” open book reader > book list and locate the copied books. what should happen: the cartridge books are copied to internal storage and appear in book list. if that does not happen: if powersave is on, nls notes auto copy works only while you are in file manager or book list. move there and reconnect the cartridge if needed. practice: locate usb-a by touch without confusing it with usb-c. a usb flash drive connects directly to usb-a. an sd card inserts into the sd-card slot on the left side behind the lanyard attachment point. use file manager to browse these devices. part 20 - settings open settings from main menu by moving to settings or typing s (dots 2-3-4), then press enter. book reader settings: condense blank lines, formatting, spaces, line-down behavior, autoscroll, book contraction, reflow, and related reading options. file manager settings: includes delete confirmation. braille settings: braille display/input choices. device settings: device-wide behavior such as word wrap and power settings. wi-fi settings. bluetooth mode. usb mode. drives for reader / drives for computer. restore defaults. saving settings: for list-style settings, nls instructs users to press space to cycle options, then navigate to the bottom and press enter on ok to save. part 21 - braille settings and grade the ereader can display content in contracted or uncontracted braille according to settings and document type. the global command space+g (dots 1-2-4-5) switches braille grade in supported contexts. 21.1 change braille grade what you will learn: switch between available braille presentation modes. before you begin: open a book or text where grade switching is supported. exactly how to do it hold space. press dots 1-2-4-5 (the braille letter g). release the keys. read the status change/message. read a familiar sentence to confirm the result. what should happen: braille presentation changes between available grade settings. if that does not happen: if the content is already a prepared brf, translation behavior can differ. review braille settings and the file type. practice: switch grade and restore your preferred setting. part 22 - wi-fi 22.1 connect to a visible wi-fi network what you will learn: join a wireless network directly from the ereader. before you begin: know the exact network name and password. exactly how to do it press s1 for main menu. open settings. open wi-fi settings. confirm wi-fi is on. press enter on the wi-fi on/off item if needed. open visible wi-fi networks. use n-up/n-down until your exact network name appears. press enter. press enter on join. enter the password in uncontracted ueb unless you deliberately choose another input code through s3. navigate to ok and press enter. wait for the connection result. what should happen: the ereader connects to the selected network. if that does not happen: if connection fails, check password capitalization, ueb symbols/numbers, network signal, and input braille code. practice: open known wi-fi networks after connecting and confirm the network is present. 22.2 optional autowifi.txt method nls documents an alternate method: create a plain text file named autowifi.txt with the network name on line 1 and password on line 2, place it in the root of a usb flash drive or sd card, then insert it while the ereader is on. this exposes the wi-fi password in plain text on that media, so protect or delete the file afterward. part 23 - battery, device information, and help task command battery level shortcut space+# (dots 3-4-5-6) main menu help open help; choose keyboard commands or user guide current device information open device info from main menu the built-in help area contains keyboard commands and the full user guide. because the built-in guide tracks the device firmware, use it whenever your menus differ from this manual. part 24 - bluetooth mode 24.1 put the emz-20 into bluetooth mode what you will learn: make the ereader ready to pair with another device. before you begin: the ereader is on. exactly how to do it press s1 for main menu. open settings. navigate to bluetooth mode. press enter. the display should read bt. alternative: tap the power on button and activate the routing button over bt when that quick mode menu is presented. to toggle bluetooth on or off globally, use space+t (dots 2-3-4-5) as documented by nls. what should happen: bt appears and the ereader is ready for bluetooth connection/pairing. if that does not happen: if the external device cannot see the emz-20, leave bluetooth mode, toggle bluetooth, re-enter it, and restart both devices if necessary. practice: enter bluetooth mode and return to main menu. part 25 - connect to iphone or ipad 25.1 pair emz-20 with voiceover what you will learn: use the ereader as an iphone/ipad braille display and braille keyboard. before you begin: voiceover should be enabled on the iphone/ipad. exactly how to do it emz-20: enter bluetooth mode. the display should read bt. iphone/ipad: open settings. open accessibility. open voiceover. open braille. move to the bottom area labeled choose a braille display. find “nls ereader z” followed by the last five digits of your ereader serial number. voiceover should say it is not paired. double-tap the nls ereader entry. when prompted for the pin, enter 1111 on the iphone/ipad. double-tap pair. wait for pairing. move voiceover focus on the iphone/ipad and verify the emz-20 braille changes. open an editable field and test braille keyboard input. press a cursor-routing button and confirm voiceover/caret movement where supported. what should happen: iphone/ipad content appears on the 20-cell display and braille keyboard input works. if that does not happen: if the device does not appear or pair, nls recommends powering off both devices, turning the ereader back on, then the ios device, and repeating the process. if paired but braille is blank, touch/move focus on the ios screen. practice: perform the three tests: output, input, routing. part 26 - connect to mac with voiceover 26.1 pair emz-20 with a mac what you will learn: use the emz-20 as a voiceover braille display over bluetooth. before you begin: voiceover is running on the mac. exactly how to do it emz-20: enter bluetooth mode. mac: open voiceover utility. the nls guide describes vo+f8; depending on current mac function-key settings, fn may also be needed. in voiceover utility, select braille. move to displays and activate it. move to add and activate it. find “nls ereader zoomax” followed by the ereader serial number in the bluetooth devices table. interact with the ereader row using voiceover interaction commands. move to pair and activate it. when prompted, enter 1111 and press return. press escape to leave device selection. close voiceover utility when finished. test braille output with voiceover navigation, then test input and routing. what should happen: voiceover content appears on the emz-20 and supported commands/input work. if that does not happen: if the mac cannot find the ereader, confirm bluetooth mode and restart bluetooth/device pairing. if it pairs but no braille appears, verify the display is added in voiceover utility > braille. practice: navigate several mac controls and confirm the braille display follows voiceover. part 27 - connect to windows or mac by usb 27.1 put the emz-20 into usb mode what you will learn: use the usb-c port as a wired braille-display connection. before you begin: use a data-capable usb cable; the supplied charging cable is documented for this purpose. exactly how to do it emz-20: press s1 and open settings. open usb mode. the display should read usb. alternative: tap power on and activate the routing button over usb when the quick mode menu is available. on the right side, locate usb-c: it is directly behind the two small round power buttons and before the usb-a port. connect the usb-c end to the emz-20. connect the other end to the windows pc or mac. open your screen reader’s braille display settings and select the nls/zoomax ereader device as appropriate. test output, keyboard input, and routing. what should happen: computer screen-reader content appears on the emz-20. if that does not happen: if the ereader only charges but does not connect, verify usb mode, use a data-capable cable, and configure the display in the screen reader. practice: connect by usb and complete all three connection tests. part 28 - use with jaws and nvda nls documents emz-20 compatibility with jaws and nvda on windows. exact braille-driver wording can change as screen readers update, so use the current jaws/nvda braille settings together with the emz-20 usb/bluetooth mode. 28.1 verify with jaws what you will learn: confirm jaws is sending braille to the ereader. before you begin: emz-20 is connected by supported usb/bluetooth method and in the correct mode. exactly how to do it start jaws. open jaws braille settings / display configuration. add or select the nls ereader zoomax/compatible ereader entry presented by your jaws version. choose the correct connection if prompted. apply the settings. move jaws focus to another control and verify braille output changes. open notepad and type using the emz-20 keyboard. use a cursor-routing button and verify the caret/focus responds. what should happen: output, input, and routing work. if that does not happen: if windows recognizes the device but jaws does not, check jaws braille drivers/settings and current nls/jaws documentation before changing emz-20 system settings. practice: test jaws in notepad and file explorer. 28.2 verify with nvda what you will learn: confirm nvda is sending braille to the ereader. before you begin: emz-20 is connected and in usb/bluetooth mode. exactly how to do it start nvda. press nvda+n. open preferences > settings > braille. select the appropriate display or automatic if the current nvda version supports automatic detection for your connection. apply the settings. move windows focus and verify the 20-cell display changes. open an edit field and test keyboard input. test cursor routing. what should happen: nvda follows on the braille display. if that does not happen: if automatic detection fails, manually review the current supported display selection and usb/bluetooth connection. practice: test output, input, and routing. part 29 - keyboard lock and common recovery skills 29.1 unlock the keyboard what you will learn: recover when the display says keyboard locked. before you begin: the display reads keyboard locked or keys do not respond normally. exactly how to do it locate s1: far-left outer small round system key. locate s4: far-right outer small round system key. press s1 and s4 together. read the display and test n-up/n-down. if needed, nls also documents power on as an unlock method. what should happen: the keyboard responds normally. if that does not happen: if keys remain unresponsive, make sure the device is awake rather than suspended, then press power on. practice: lock and unlock only when you are comfortable with the locations of s1/s4. 29.2 reliable recovery commands task command go to main menu s1 or space+m back / escape space+e context menu s3 open current book s4 top of list/document space+dots 1-2-3 bottom of list/document space+dots 4-5-6 battery level space+# part 30 - troubleshooting 30.1 device will not turn on what you will learn: check power problems in the correct order. before you begin: use the supplied/appropriate charger. exactly how to do it confirm the charging cable is connected to usb-c on the right side behind both power buttons. connect the ac adapter to a known working outlet. allow charging time if the battery may be deeply discharged. press the first small round power button from the front: power on. listen for startup tones. if there is still no response, test another appropriate cable/adapter or contact your nls network library. what should happen: the device starts or you have isolated a likely power problem. if that does not happen: if the battery/case becomes unusually hot, swollen, damaged, or smells unusual, stop using/charging it and contact the library/support. practice: review the physical power/charging layout without connecting cables. 30.2 wi-fi will not connect what you will learn: separate password/input problems from network problems. before you begin: know the correct network and password. exactly how to do it confirm wi-fi is on under settings > wi-fi settings. confirm you selected the exact network name. re-enter the password carefully. confirm the braille input code used for the password. move closer to the wi-fi access point if signal is weak. try another known network if available to determine whether the problem is the ereader or the original network. what should happen: the ereader connects or the failure is narrowed to credentials/network. if that does not happen: if the network uses a browser/captive portal, the ereader may not be able to complete that login because it does not provide a general web browser. practice: reconnect to a known network. 30.3 paired to iphone but no braille appears what you will learn: restore voiceover braille output. before you begin: the ereader is shown as paired. exactly how to do it touch or move voiceover focus on the iphone/ipad. confirm voiceover is on. return to settings > accessibility > voiceover > braille and confirm the nls ereader is connected. confirm the emz-20 is still in/available for bluetooth display use. toggle bluetooth if necessary. restart both devices and re-pair if the connection remains unusable. what should happen: voiceover content appears on the emz-20. if that does not happen: if another braille display is selected or the pairing record is stale, remove/re-pair according to current ios procedures. practice: test output, input, routing. 30.4 file or book is missing what you will learn: check the correct storage and application. before you begin: know where the file was copied/downloaded. exactly how to do it open book reader > book list for books imported through bard or cartridge auto copy. open file manager for raw files/folders. check internal files, usb files, and sd card files separately. if an external device is absent, reconnect it and wait for recognition. if a file format is unsupported or packaged unexpectedly, test a known supported file. what should happen: you find the title or identify its storage/format issue. if that does not happen: do not delete or recopy repeatedly until you know which storage area currently contains the file. practice: locate one bard book and one external-media file. part 31 - care and safe handling use light fingertip pressure on refreshable braille cells. keep liquids, crumbs, and debris away from braille cells and keyboard. do not force usb-c, usb-a, or sd media into the wrong slot. use the supplied or appropriate charger. do not disassemble the battery or device. protect the unit during transport and use the lanyard only as intended. keep the indiana/nls property label intact if the device is loaned equipment. back up personal documents when possible; nls library books can usually be downloaded again. part 32 - independent practice course level 1 - physical orientation ☐ find all 20 cells. ☐ find routing buttons. ☐ identify dots 1-8 and space. ☐ identify s1-s4, bl/br, and n keys. ☐ locate sd, power on, power off, usb-c, and usb-a. ready to advance: you can complete every checked task without another person telling you which key to press. level 2 - basic operation ☐ power on. ☐ return to main menu. ☐ move up/down menu. ☐ use first-letter navigation. ☐ open/close context menu. ☐ check battery. ready to advance: you can complete every checked task without another person telling you which key to press. level 3 - reading ☐ open book reader. ☐ open a book. ☐ pan forward/back. ☐ move by line. ☐ move by page. ☐ use where am i. ☐ return with s4. ready to advance: you can complete every checked task without another person telling you which key to press. level 4 - files ☐ open file manager. ☐ browse internal storage. ☐ open sd/usb storage if available. ☐ use file info. ☐ copy a practice file. ready to advance: you can complete every checked task without another person telling you which key to press. level 5 - online ☐ connect wi-fi. ☐ open bard. ☐ search for a title. ☐ reach download/download and open. ☐ open nfb newsline if you have an account. ready to advance: you can complete every checked task without another person telling you which key to press. level 6 - iphone/ipad ☐ enter bluetooth mode. ☐ pair through voiceover > braille. ☐ use pin 1111. ☐ test output. ☐ test input. ☐ test routing. ready to advance: you can complete every checked task without another person telling you which key to press. level 7 - computer ☐ enter usb mode. ☐ connect usb-c to computer. ☐ configure screen reader. ☐ test output/input/routing. ready to advance: you can complete every checked task without another person telling you which key to press. level 8 - recovery ☐ unlock keyboard. ☐ use s1 main menu. ☐ use space+e back. ☐ use s3 context menu. ☐ recover from wi-fi or bluetooth failure logically. ready to advance: you can complete every checked task without another person telling you which key to press. part 33 - quick reference commands task command main menu s1 or space+m (1-3-4) application menu s2 context menu s3 current book s4 back/escape space+e (1-5) top space+1-2-3 bottom space+4-5-6 braille grade space+g (1-2-4-5) battery space+# (3-4-5-6) bluetooth toggle space+t (2-3-4-5) pan backward in book d2, n-left, or bl pan forward in book d5, n-right, or br previous line d1 or n-up next line d3 or n-down where am i dots 1-5-6 autoscroll on/off dots 3-4 word wrap toggle dots 2-4-5-6 physical side reference task command left side, front to back lanyard point → sd-card slot right side, front to back lanyard point → power on → power off → usb-c → usb-a part 34 - official nls resources nls braille ereader zoomax user guide nls braille ereader zoomax getting started nls equipment for nls materials the built-in help > user guide on the emz-20 is also an important reference because it reflects the software installed on your particular device. final independence checklist ☐ i can orient the emz-20 correctly. ☐ i can locate power on, power off, usb-c, usb-a, and sd without guessing. ☐ i can identify s1-s4, bl/br, d1-d6, and all n navigation keys. ☐ i can power on, suspend, and power off safely. ☐ i can navigate main menu and use the context menu. ☐ i can read and pan a book. ☐ i can navigate by line, paragraph, page, and volume. ☐ i can use bard after connecting wi-fi. ☐ i can use file manager and external storage. ☐ i can pair with iphone/ipad voiceover. ☐ i can connect to mac voiceover. ☐ i can connect to a windows/mac computer by usb. ☐ i can test braille output, keyboard input, and cursor routing. ☐ i can use help and recovery commands when i get lost. most important habit: do one action, then stop and read the 20-cell display. the emz-20 provides many fast shortcuts, but accurate reading between commands prevents most navigation mistakes. return to all manuals

entries.title: NotebookLM, Be My Eyes, and AI-Assisted Access Manual
entries.course: NotebookLM, Be My Eyes, and AI-Assisted Access
entries.snippet: Step-by-step keyboard manual for NotebookLM, Be My AI, and AI-assisted access.
entries.text: ai-assisted access manual - accessible learning center artificial intelligence notebooklm, be my eyes, and ai-assisted access manual use ai access tools by keyboard, verify their answers, and protect private information. basic how-tos advanced how-tos command list basic how-tos navigate an ai website keyboard commands: tab and shift+tab move through controls. enter activates links and buttons. space changes checkboxes. h moves by heading and b moves by button in jaws and nvda browse mode. open the tool and confirm its name and active account. press h to review page headings. press e or f in supported screen readers to find an edit field. type a short prompt using only public, fictional, or authorized information. submit it, then return to headings or browse mode to locate the response. read the complete response before acting. you should hear: a named prompt field, a submit control, and a structured response. if that does not happen: press escape once, check the focused control with insert+tab or nvda+tab, and navigate by landmarks or headings. ask for a useful image description keyboard approach: find upload, add image, or take picture by button navigation. remove private documents, addresses, faces, credentials, and medical information unless sharing is authorized. activate the image control and choose the intended image. verify the filename before submitting. ask a focused question such as, “describe the controls from top to bottom,” or “read the expiration date and state any uncertainty.” save the answer only after checking important details another way. if that does not happen: cancel the upload and confirm the image format, connection, and permissions. create a notebooklm notebook and add a source keyboard commands: use h for headings, b for buttons, and tab or shift+tab through dialogs. open notebooklm and activate create new notebook. enter a descriptive notebook name. activate add source. choose the source type and select only an authorized document or public link. wait for processing and verify that the source name appears in the source list. if that does not happen: do not add the source again until you check the source list and any processing alert. advanced how-tos verify a notebooklm answer against its source keyboard commands: use heading and link navigation to move between an answer, its citation links, and the source viewer. ask one specific question. read the entire answer and note names, dates, numbers, and claims. open each citation. read enough text before and after the cited passage to understand context. mark each claim supported, unsupported, or uncertain. use only supported claims in your work. if that does not happen: treat the answer as unverified and search the original source directly. compare two sources keyboard approach: use the source-selection controls before asking the question. add two authorized sources and confirm both names. select only those sources if the tool permits source selection. ask for agreements, differences, and direct citations. open the citations for each claimed difference. create your own short comparison using verified facts. if that does not happen: ask separate questions about each source and compare the verified answers yourself. use ai for visual access without overtrusting it keyboard approach: return to the prompt field and ask follow-up questions that isolate one detail at a time. ask the tool to separate visible observations from interpretation. ask where an item is located using clock-face or top-to-bottom language. ask it to repeat exact text, numbers, or colors and state uncertainty. verify medication, money, identity, navigation, safety, and legal information with a trusted person or authoritative source. if that does not happen: state what remains unknown. never convert an uncertain ai description into a confident instruction. write a safer prompt keyboard command: ctrl+a selects the current prompt text; ctrl+c copies; ctrl+v pastes. state the task and desired format. supply only the minimum authorized context. ask the tool to identify assumptions and uncertainty. request citations when the answer depends on sources. review the prompt for private information before submitting. if that does not happen: shorten the request and ask one question at a time. quick command list tab / shift+tab: next or previous control enter: activate or submit escape: close a menu or dialog h: next heading in jaws or nvda browse mode b: next button in jaws or nvda browse mode e: next edit field in jaws or nvda browse mode insert+tab / nvda+tab: identify focused control ctrl+a / ctrl+c / ctrl+v: select all / copy / paste return to manuals

entries.title: OneDrive, Dropbox, and Cloud Sharing Manual
entries.snippet: Step-by-step keyboard manual for OneDrive, Dropbox, and cloud sharing.
entries.text: cloud storage manual - accessible learning center cloud storage onedrive, dropbox, and cloud sharing manual save, organize, synchronize, share, and recover files safely. basic how-tos advanced how-tos command list basic how-tos find your synchronized folder keyboard commands: windows+e opens file explorer. alt+d focuses the address bar. alt+up arrow moves to the parent folder. press windows+e. use the navigation pane or address bar to open onedrive or dropbox. press alt+d and have the screen reader read the location. press escape to return to the file list. select a file and hear its complete name and status. you should hear: onedrive or dropbox in the current path. if that does not happen: a similarly named local folder may not synchronize. confirm the service is signed in before saving important work there. create a folder and save a file in it keyboard commands: ctrl+shift+n creates a folder in file explorer. f2 renames it. open the correct onedrive or dropbox location. press ctrl+shift+n. type a descriptive folder name and press enter. open the folder and save or paste a practice file into it. wait for synchronization, then verify the file is listed. if that does not happen: press escape, recheck the current path, and confirm you have permission to create folders. copy or move a file keyboard commands: ctrl+c copies, ctrl+x moves, and ctrl+v pastes. select one file and read its name. press ctrl+c to keep the original, or ctrl+x to move it. open the destination and confirm its path. press ctrl+v once. verify the result and wait for synchronization. if that does not happen: do not paste repeatedly. check both locations for duplicates, conflicts, or a permission alert. advanced how-tos share a file with named people keyboard command: shift+f10 or the application key opens a context menu in many windows configurations. select the file and verify its name and owner. press shift+f10 and choose share. enter the intended email addresses. choose can view or can edit. review recipients and permission before sending. if that does not happen: cancel and use the service’s labeled share command. sharing may open a web dialog. create and check a sharing link keyboard approach: open share, then locate link settings with tab or button navigation. choose specific people or people you choose whenever possible. turn editing off unless collaborators must change the file. set an expiration date if available and useful. copy the link. test it in a private browser window without exposing private data. if that does not happen: remove the link or stop sharing and create a narrower permission. recover an earlier version keyboard approach: select the file, open its context menu, and find version history. confirm the file and current owner. open version history and review dates, times, and editors. preview or download the older version when possible. make a backup of the current version. restore only after confirming what will be replaced. if that does not happen: keep the current file and ask the owner or administrator whether version history is available. resolve a synchronization conflict keyboard commands: f2 renames a selected file; alt+enter opens properties. stop editing both copies. compare filenames, modified dates, sizes, and locations. rename each copy clearly instead of overwriting either one. open and compare their content. keep the correct copy, then archive or delete the other only after verification. if that does not happen: preserve both copies and ask for help. never guess which conflict copy is current. quick command list windows+e: file explorer alt+d: address bar ctrl+shift+n: new folder f2: rename ctrl+c / ctrl+x / ctrl+v: copy / move / paste shift+f10: context menu alt+enter: properties ctrl+z: undo the most recent supported file action return to manuals

entries.title: Screen Readers: JAWS, Narrator, and NVDA
entries.course: Screen Readers: JAWS, Narrator, and NVDA
entries.snippet: Accessible screen-reader manual comparing JAWS, Windows Narrator, and NVDA.
entries.text: screen readers manual - accessible learning center foundational assistive technology manual screen readers: jaws, narrator, and nvda choose one screen reader and learn the same workplace skills with product-specific commands. all manuals ten screen readers lessons my progress choose the screen reader available to you three windows screen-reader choices screen reader best reason to choose it for this course important note jaws choose jaws when it is installed and licensed by you, your school, or your workplace. includes jaws-specific tools such as fscompanion and picture smart ai when available. windows narrator choose narrator when you need the screen reader built into windows 11. start or stop it with windows+ctrl+enter. its scan mode and views differ from jaws. nvda choose nvda when it is already installed or your organization approves the free, open-source windows screen reader. its browse mode and nvda modifier commands differ from jaws and narrator. use one primary screen reader at a time. running several simultaneously can produce overlapping speech and conflicting commands. an instructor may demonstrate a second product after the student can safely start, stop, and recover the primary choice. what stays the same windows and application commands such as tab, shift+tab, arrow keys, enter, spacebar, ctrl+c, ctrl+v, alt+tab, and windows+l usually stay the same. screen-reader commands differ when you request information, change reading modes, open element lists, adjust speech, or use product settings. equivalent concepts with different names screen-reader key: jaws key, narrator key, or nvda key. web-reading mode: jaws virtual cursor, narrator scan mode, or nvda browse mode. typing in forms: jaws forms mode, narrator with scan mode off, or nvda focus mode. command discovery: jaws keyboard help, narrator input learning, or nvda input help. ten-lesson learning path lesson 1: choose, start, and stop a screen reader — choose jaws, narrator, or nvda and start and stop it safely. lesson 2: keyboard help, speech control, and basic information — use keyboard help and control speech without losing focus. lesson 3: read by character, word, line, paragraph, and continuously — read and review text at several levels with the chosen screen reader. lesson 4: navigate windows, dialogs, and controls — move reliably through windows applications and identify focus. lesson 5: browse webpages by headings, links, lists, and landmarks — navigate structured webpages efficiently with the selected screen reader. lesson 6: complete forms and manage input modes — enter fictional information in web forms while controlling reading and typing modes. lesson 7: navigate tables, lists, and structured information — read relationships in tables and lists without losing row or column context. lesson 8: read, edit, and review workplace documents — use shared editing commands and screen-reader feedback in word or another document editor. lesson 9: help, settings, updates, braille, and jaws ai — find trustworthy help, make reversible settings changes, and understand product-specific advanced features. lesson 10: final screen-reader workplace project — complete a realistic windows, web, form, document, and troubleshooting workflow with the chosen screen reader. official references freedom scientific: navigating web pages with jaws freedom scientific: jaws reading commands microsoft: complete guide to narrator microsoft: narrator keyboard commands nv access: current nvda user guide nv access: current nvda commands quick reference progress preservation: this course replaces the former jaws-only presentation. existing jaws lesson submissions remain recognized in student progress. start screen readers lesson 1 return to manuals

entries.title: Screen-Reader Troubleshooting and Recovery Manual
entries.snippet: Step-by-step keyboard manual for screen-reader troubleshooting and recovery.
entries.text: screen-reader recovery manual - accessible learning center foundations and recovery screen-reader troubleshooting and recovery manual identify focus, mode, application, audio, and computer problems before restarting. basic how-tos advanced how-tos command list basic how-tos identify the active window keyboard commands: jaws: insert+t. nvda: nvda+t. narrator: narrator key+t. stop typing so you do not change unknown content. press the command for your screen reader. listen for the application, document, or dialog title. if it is wrong, press alt+tab once and check the title again. you should hear: a useful window or document title. if that does not happen: test speech in another safe window before closing anything. identify the focused control keyboard commands: jaws: insert+tab. nvda: nvda+tab. narrator: narrator key+tab reads the current item in common configurations. press the focus-information command. decide whether focus is in text, a button, a list, browser content, or a dialog. press tab once. request focus information again and compare the result. if that does not happen: check for a modal dialog, protected screen, or screen-reader mode intercepting keys. use keyboard help without performing commands keyboard commands: jaws: insert+1. nvda: nvda+1. narrator input learning: narrator key+1. turn keyboard help on. press the command you are unsure about. listen to its name or description. press the keyboard-help command again to turn help off. you should hear: key descriptions without the normal actions occurring. if that does not happen: stop pressing uncertain commands and open the screen reader’s commands or help documentation. recover when speech stops keyboard commands: windows+ctrl+enter toggles narrator. ctrl+alt+n starts nvda when its desktop shortcut is configured. jaws can be started from its desktop shortcut or start menu. press a volume key and confirm the computer is not muted. check headphones, speakers, bluetooth, and the selected output device. try the screen reader’s start command once. wait at least ten seconds and test with a safe key such as windows. use a second screen reader temporarily if necessary. if that does not happen: save work with ctrl+s where safe, then ask for sighted or remote assistance before restarting. advanced how-tos switch between browse and forms interaction keyboard commands: jaws: insert+z toggles the virtual cursor. nvda: nvda+space toggles browse and focus modes. request focus information and identify the web control. use browse mode to read headings, links, and surrounding instructions. move to the edit field or interactive control. switch to focus/forms interaction only when needed. return to browse mode after completing the control. if that does not happen: press escape once, check focus, and avoid repeatedly toggling modes without listening for confirmation. recover from a trapped dialog keyboard commands: tab and shift+tab inspect controls. escape cancels many dialogs. alt+f4 closes the active window. read the window title and focused control. move through the dialog once with tab and shift+tab. choose cancel if available. press escape only when canceling is safe. use alt+f4 only after deciding whether unsaved work or a confirmation may appear. if that does not happen: do not hold keys down. use alt+tab to check whether a hidden confirmation opened behind another window. restart in the safest order keyboard commands: ctrl+s saves in many applications. alt+f4 closes the active application. windows+x, u, r restarts windows. save work and confirm the filename and location. restart only the affected application first. if the problem continues everywhere, restart the screen reader. restart windows only after files are saved and applications are closed. after restart, test one simple task before reopening everything. if that does not happen: stop before repair or reinstall. back up settings and record the error, application, and steps that caused it. collect useful information for support keyboard commands: windows+v opens clipboard history when enabled. windows+shift+s opens snipping tool for a helper when visual capture is appropriate. write the application and screen-reader names and versions. record the exact task and commands used. copy the complete error message. state what was expected and what happened instead. list the safe troubleshooting already attempted. if that does not happen: describe what the screen reader announced word for word; do not guess at visual details. quick command list insert+t / nvda+t / narrator+t: window title insert+tab / nvda+tab: focused control insert+1 / nvda+1 / narrator+1: keyboard help jaws insert+z: virtual cursor nvda+space: browse or focus mode alt+tab: switch windows escape: cancel or close many dialogs ctrl+s: save alt+f4: close active window windows+ctrl+enter: toggle narrator practice recovery decisions return to manuals

entries.title: Social Media Accessibility Screen Reader Manual
entries.snippet: Social Media Accessibility Screen Reader Manual: step-by-step keyboard and screen-reader instructions, practice, troubleshooting, and command references.
entries.text: social media accessibility screen reader manual - accessible learning center skip to main content accessible learning center manual social media accessibility screen reader manual keyboard and mobile screen-reader instruction independent self-study guide all manuals table of contents start of manual purpose: this manual teaches how to use major social-media platforms with a screen reader and how to create posts that are accessible to other people. it assumes no prior social-media experience. platforms: facebook, linkedin, youtube, and x. interfaces change frequently, so the manual teaches stable navigation patterns first and then platform-specific controls. screen readers: desktop guidance applies to narrator, nvda, jaws, and voiceover where appropriate. mobile guidance applies to voiceover on iphone/ipad and talkback on android. how to use this manual use headings, landmarks, buttons, links, edit fields, and lists rather than tabbing through every item on long feeds. when a platform introduces a new layout, identify the main navigation region, search field, feed/timeline, post composer, notifications, profile, and settings before learning platform-specific shortcuts. use screen-reader application/focus mode only when the web app requires direct keyboard commands; return to browse/virtual mode for ordinary webpage navigation. before posting media, add meaningful alt text to images and accurate captions to video when the platform supports them. write hashtags in camelcase, avoid long strings of emoji, and avoid decorative unicode characters that screen readers may announce one symbol at a time. before changing privacy or audience settings, have the screen reader repeat the selected audience or account name. do not trust direct messages that ask for passwords, codes, gift cards, crypto, remote access, or urgent money transfers. table of contents part 1 - social media with a screen reader part 2 - screen reader navigation patterns part 3 - writing accessible social posts part 4 - image descriptions and alt text part 5 - video captions and audio description part 6 - hashtags, emoji, and links part 7 - facebook: orientation and feed part 8 - facebook: posting, comments, groups, and messages part 9 - linkedin: orientation and feed part 10 - linkedin: profile, posts, networking, and jobs part 11 - youtube: search and watching videos part 12 - youtube: player shortcuts and captions part 13 - youtube: comments, subscriptions, playlists, and uploading part 14 - x: orientation and timeline part 15 - x: keyboard shortcuts part 16 - x: posting, replies, direct messages, and alt text part 17 - mobile social media with voiceover part 18 - mobile social media with talkback part 19 - privacy, security, and scam safety part 20 - troubleshooting part 21 - independent practice course part 22 - quick reference part 23 - official resources part 1 - social media with a screen reader most social platforms are dynamic web applications. new posts load without a full page refresh, menus open in dialogs, buttons change labels after activation, and feeds can contain repeated controls. the key skill is maintaining context. main navigation: home/feed, search, notifications, messages, profile, settings. feed/timeline: a long list of posts. each post can contain author, time, text, media, reaction controls, comment/reply controls, and menus. composer: edit field/dialog for creating a post. post details: a focused page/dialog for one post and its replies/comments. notifications: activity related to your account. direct messages: private conversations; not automatically trustworthy merely because they appear inside a social platform. part 2 - screen reader navigation patterns task command / method next heading h in many screen readers/browsers next button b next link k in nvda/jaws; vo rotor on mac/ios next edit field e next landmark/region d or r depending on screen reader next list l screen-reader elements list nvda+f7 / jaws+f3 or insert+f7 / vo rotor command warning: screen-reader single-letter commands work only in browse/virtual mode. if typing h, b, or e enters characters into a post field, exit the edit field or return to browse mode. 2.1 rebuild context on any platform what you will learn: recover when focus gets lost in a dynamic feed. before you begin: a social-media webpage is open. exactly how to do it press escape once or twice to close an open menu/dialog if appropriate. use your screen reader to move to the page title or first heading. move by landmarks/regions to find navigation or main content. use headings or buttons to find the feed, search, notifications, or composer. have the screen reader repeat the focused item before activating it. what should happen: you regain a known location without refreshing or signing out. if that does not happen: if the page remains confused, use the browser address bar and reload the known platform homepage, then navigate again. practice: practice getting lost intentionally and recovering. part 3 - writing accessible social posts use sentence case rather than all capitals. keep important information in text, not only inside an image. break long posts into short paragraphs. put emoji at natural points and avoid repeating the same emoji many times. use descriptive link wording when the platform allows it. use camelcase hashtags: #screenreaderusers rather than #screenreaderusers. do not use decorative mathematical/script unicode characters as fake fonts; screen readers may announce them poorly or character by character. if a post depends on a chart, screenshot, flyer, or meme, add the essential information in alt text or the post body. part 4 - image descriptions and alt text alt text should communicate the image information needed to understand the post. describe purpose and key content, not every pixel. good: “three coworkers seated around a conference table reviewing a tactile diagram.” better for text-heavy image: include the important visible words in the post itself, then describe the visual context. avoid starting every description with “image of” unless the platform does not already identify it as an image. do not use auto-generated alt text as a substitute for reviewing important images. 4.1 add alt text before posting what you will learn: make an uploaded image understandable to screen-reader users. before you begin: a social platform supports author-supplied alt text. exactly how to do it upload/select the image in the post composer. move through the image editing controls until you find alt text, alt, edit, accessibility, or image description. open that control. type a concise description of the image’s important content and purpose. save/done the description. return to the post composer and review the audience and post text before publishing. what should happen: the platform stores your description with the image. if that does not happen: if the platform does not expose an alt-text control in the current app, put the essential image description in the post text and try the desktop/web composer if practical. practice: add alt text to a harmless test image. part 5 - video captions and audio description captions provide text access to speech and meaningful audio. auto-captions are useful but should be reviewed for names, jargon, numbers, and punctuation when you control the video. burned-in/on-screen captions are not always exposed as text to screen readers, but they still help many viewers; platform caption tracks are preferable when available. audio description narrates important visual information that is not obvious from dialogue/sound. if audio description is not supported as a separate track, include essential visual context in narration or the description/post text. part 6 - hashtags, emoji, and links example accessibility note #accessibletech good camelcase hashtag #accessibletech harder to parse as separate words ✅ new update available usually concise ✅✅✅✅✅✅✅ repetitive speech noise click here weak link text read the accessibility guide descriptive link wording part 7 - facebook: orientation and feed interface note: facebook changes its desktop and mobile layouts frequently. use headings, buttons, landmarks, and the platform’s labeled navigation rather than memorizing a long tab order. 7.1 find the facebook feed what you will learn: reach posts from the homepage. before you begin: you are signed in. exactly how to do it open facebook.com or the facebook app. find the main navigation/home control and activate it if needed. move to the main content/feed region. use headings, article-like groups, or screen-reader reading commands to move through posts. within a post, read the author and post text before moving to reaction/comment/share controls. what should happen: you can read one post at a time while maintaining author/context. if that does not happen: if focus lands in stories/reels or another carousel, move by landmark/heading to the main feed. practice: read five posts and identify each author. part 8 - facebook: posting, comments, groups, and messages 8.1 create a facebook post what you will learn: publish text with the intended audience. before you begin: you are on facebook home. exactly how to do it find the “what’s on your mind” or create post
