control. activate it and move to the post text field. type the post. if adding a photo, upload it and open the image-editing controls. use facebook’s add alternative text control when available and enter a description. move to the audience/privacy selector and have the screen reader read the selected audience. activate post only after reviewing text, media, alt text, and audience. what should happen: the post appears with the intended audience. if that does not happen: if the composer becomes difficult, press escape, reopen it, and add one element at a time. practice: create a friends-only test post and remove it afterward if desired. comments: open the comments control for the post, move to the comment edit field, type, then submit with the labeled button/enter as supported. groups: verify the group name before posting because group privacy/audience differs from your personal feed. messenger/dms: read the conversation name before sending; treat unexpected links/payment requests as suspicious. facebook currently provides an add alternative text option when editing photos before sharing. part 9 - linkedin: orientation and feed linkedin publishes dedicated screen-reader support articles and states that it tests with jaws, nvda, narrator, voiceover, and talkback. its desktop navigation is generally well-labeled but dynamic dialogs and feed cards can still be dense. 9.1 navigate linkedin by regions what you will learn: move among the major linkedin areas. before you begin: you are signed in on linkedin.com. exactly how to do it use the main navigation to identify home, my network, jobs, messaging, notifications, and me/profile. activate home. move to main content and locate the feed. read posts by heading/author text and then use buttons for reaction/comment/repost controls. use the me/profile menu to return to your profile when needed. what should happen: you can move between the major linkedin work areas without tabbing through every control. if that does not happen: if a mobile-optimized view appears unexpectedly in the browser, maximize the browser window or use the current desktop layout controls. practice: open home, jobs, messaging, and profile. part 10 - linkedin: profile, posts, networking, and jobs 10.1 add alt text to a linkedin image post what you will learn: create an accessible image post. before you begin: start a linkedin post and upload an image. exactly how to do it after the image uploads, find alt.text or alt. activate it. type the description. choose save/done. review post visibility and comment controls. publish the post. what should happen: linkedin stores author-provided alt text with the image. if that does not happen: if linkedin supplies automatic alt text, replace/review it when the image matters to understanding the post. practice: add alt text to one test photo. profile: linkedin provides screen-reader-specific help for profile intro, contact info, experience, skills, education, recommendations, and open to work options. networking: read the person’s name/headline before connect/follow; avoid sending connection requests from ambiguous search-result controls. jobs: use the jobs navigation item, search filters, job-details heading, and application controls. external applications may open another employer/ats site. messaging: confirm recipient/thread before typing; linkedin job scams can still occur inside legitimate messaging. part 11 - youtube: search and watching videos 11.1 search youtube with a screen reader what you will learn: find a video efficiently. before you begin: youtube is open in a desktop browser. exactly how to do it press / to move to youtube search, or navigate to the search edit field. type the search term. press enter. move through result titles/headings/links. read the channel name and result description before opening a video. activate the video title. what should happen: the watch page opens and the player is available. if that does not happen: if / types into another edit field, leave that field first or navigate directly to search. practice: search for a known channel and play one video. part 12 - youtube: player shortcuts and captions focus warning: youtube states that on the current computer experience the video player may need focus before player shortcuts work. task command / method play / pause k or space when player has focus captions on/off c mute m full screen f next video shift+n keyboard shortcut list shift+? search / seek slider tab to slider; use arrow keys after switching screen-reader cursor mode if needed 12.1 turn captions on and review settings what you will learn: use text captions during playback. before you begin: a video offers captions. exactly how to do it give focus to the video player. press c. if you need caption language/style, move to the settings button. open subtitles/cc and choose the available track/language. use the caption options area for visual styling if needed. press c again to turn captions off. what should happen: captions are displayed while speech continues. if that does not happen: not every video has accurate human-reviewed captions; auto-captions can contain errors. practice: toggle captions on two videos. part 13 - youtube: comments, subscriptions, playlists, and uploading subscribe: locate the subscribe/unsubscribe button near the channel/video information and confirm the new button state. comments: navigate to the comments heading/region, activate the add a comment edit field, type, and submit with the labeled comment button. playlists: use save to add a video to a playlist; confirm the exact playlist before closing the dialog. uploading: youtube studio > create > upload videos. add a clear title, description, audience settings, visibility, and captions. creators should review/edit automatic captions when possible. youtube also provides caption-management tools and caption-generation workflows. part 14 - x: orientation and timeline x publishes accessibility features including screen-reader/braille support, keyboard shortcuts, image descriptions, captions, reduce-motion settings, font/display customization, and autoplay controls. 14.1 read the x home timeline what you will learn: use x’s timeline without tabbing through every control. before you begin: you are signed in at x.com. exactly how to do it press g then h to move to home when x keyboard shortcuts are active. press j for the next post. press k for the previous post. press enter to open the current post’s detail view when needed. use escape/browser navigation to return to the timeline. what should happen: focus moves post by post through the timeline. if that does not happen: if j/k type into a text field, leave the field before using x shortcuts. press ? to review the active shortcut list. practice: move through ten posts and open one detail view. part 15 - x: keyboard shortcuts task command / method new post n like l reply r repost t direct message m open post details enter expand photo o search / send post ctrl+enter / command+enter next / previous post j / k load new posts . home g then h notifications g then n mentions g then r profile g then p messages g then m settings and privacy g then s full shortcut menu ? sequence: commands such as g then h are sequential: press g, release it, then press h. part 16 - x: posting, replies, direct messages, and alt text 16.1 create an accessible x post what you will learn: publish text and image description with keyboard access. before you begin: you are on x.com. exactly how to do it press n to open a new post. type the post text. if adding an image, upload it. find the +alt / add description control for the image. type a meaningful image description and save it. review the post text and media. press ctrl+enter on windows or command+enter on mac to send, or activate the post button. what should happen: the post is published with alt text when added. if that does not happen: if the alt control is not exposed in the current client, try the latest x web/mobile app or include critical image information in the post text. practice: post a harmless image with alt text, then read it back. x recommends sentence case, camelcase hashtags, line breaks for long text, limited emoji repetition, and avoiding special/decorative characters. replies use r; always verify which post is currently focused before replying. direct messages can contain phishing. do not assume a verified/known-looking account is trustworthy when it asks for credentials or payment. part 17 - mobile social media with voiceover swipe right/left through controls; double-tap to activate. use the voiceover rotor to move by headings, links, form controls, or containers where supported. use the two-finger scrub to go back/cancel in many contexts. when composing, move deliberately among audience, text, media, alt-text/caption, and post/share controls before publishing. x documents an ios magic tap option that can be configured for composing a post. for media, find the alt/accessibility/edit controls after selecting the image rather than assuming the description field appears automatically. part 18 - mobile social media with talkback swipe right/left through controls; double-tap to activate. use talkback reading controls for headings/links/controls when the app exposes them. use talkback’s global back gesture/system back to close dialogs or return. after uploading media, explore the image editing controls for alt text/description before posting. x documents talkback/android support along with reduce motion, autoplay, media preview, sound, and font-size settings. if a mobile app becomes difficult, try the platform’s mobile website or desktop browser with a screen reader before assuming the task is impossible. part 19 - privacy, security, and scam safety check the audience before every sensitive post: public/anyone, friends/connections, group, followers, or custom audience. assume public posts can be copied, screenshot, quoted, reposted, or archived. never send passwords, one-time codes, recovery codes, bank details, or remote-access codes through social dms. if a friend’s account suddenly asks for money or gift cards, verify through a separate known contact method. use mfa/passkeys on social accounts where available. review active sessions/devices and connected apps periodically. do not install browser extensions or apps sent through a dm just to view a post/video. part 20 - troubleshooting 20.1 feed navigation suddenly stops working what you will learn: recover from focus/mode problems. before you begin: a single-letter command no longer moves through posts. exactly how to do it press escape to leave any open menu/edit field. have the screen reader report the focused control. return to browse/virtual mode if you are in focus/forms mode. move to the main/feed region. retry the platform or screen-reader navigation command. what should happen: feed navigation works again. if that does not happen: if the platform changed layout, use headings/buttons/landmarks rather than relying on the old shortcut. practice: practice entering/exiting an edit field and restoring navigation. 20.2 post button seems disabled what you will learn: find a missing required step. before you begin: you finished writing a post. exactly how to do it review the composer from the beginning. check whether media is still uploading. check whether an audience/visibility selection is required. check for an error message or character/media limit. remove one optional media item and test again if needed. what should happen: the missing requirement/error becomes clear. if that does not happen: copy your post text to a temporary safe note before reloading a broken composer so you do not lose it. practice: practice recovering a draft. 20.3 alt text control is hard to find what you will learn: use the media-editing layer rather than the main composer. before you begin: an image is already attached. exactly how to do it move to the attached image/media controls. open edit, alt, accessibility, or image options. look for add/edit alternative text or description. if absent, try the platform’s current desktop web composer or current mobile app. if still unavailable, include the essential description in the post body. what should happen: the image receives an accessible description or equivalent text is provided. if that does not happen: platform features can vary by account/client; do not delay critical information solely because an alt-text control is unavailable. practice: find the alt-text control on two platforms. 20.4 screen reader repeats too many controls what you will learn: use structure rather than tab navigation. before you begin: a post has many like/reply/share/menu controls. exactly how to do it use heading/article navigation to move to the next post. use the platform’s next-post shortcut when available, such as j on x. use screen-reader elements lists/rotor to jump to a specific control only when needed. avoid tabbing through every reaction control on every post. what should happen: reading becomes faster and less repetitive. if that does not happen: if posts are not marked structurally, use find/search for author text or switch platform client/browser. practice: read ten posts without tabbing through every button. part 21 - independent practice course level 1 - orientation ☐ identify main navigation. ☐ find feed/timeline. ☐ find search. ☐ find notifications. ☐ find messages/profile. ready to advance: you can complete every checked item without another person telling you which control to use. level 2 - reading ☐ read five posts. ☐ open one post detail. ☐ read comments/replies. ☐ return to feed. ready to advance: you can complete every checked item without another person telling you which control to use. level 3 - posting ☐ open composer. ☐ type text. ☐ choose audience. ☐ post a harmless update. ☐ delete it if desired. ready to advance: you can complete every checked item without another person telling you which control to use. level 4 - accessible media ☐ upload image. ☐ add alt text. ☐ review description. ☐ publish to limited audience. ready to advance: you can complete every checked item without another person telling you which control to use. level 5 - facebook ☐ read feed. ☐ create post. ☐ comment. ☐ open group. ☐ open messenger thread. ready to advance: you can complete every checked item without another person telling you which control to use. level 6 - linkedin ☐ open home. ☐ profile. ☐ jobs. ☐ messaging. ☐ create image post with alt text. ready to advance: you can complete every checked item without another person telling you which control to use. level 7 - youtube ☐ search. ☐ play/pause. ☐ toggle captions. ☐ use keyboard shortcut list. ☐ subscribe/save/comment. ready to advance: you can complete every checked item without another person telling you which control to use. level 8 - x ☐ use j/k. ☐ open post. ☐ like/reply. ☐ create post with n. ☐ add alt text. ready to advance: you can complete every checked item without another person telling you which control to use. level 9 - mobile ☐ navigate one platform with voiceover/talkback. ☐ create a draft. ☐ find media accessibility controls. ready to advance: you can complete every checked item without another person telling you which control to use. level 10 - security ☐ verify audience. ☐ recognize suspicious dm. ☐ review account security/mfa. ready to advance: you can complete every checked item without another person telling you which control to use. level 11 - troubleshooting ☐ recover from edit-field mode. ☐ recover from lost feed focus. ☐ find alt text after media upload. ready to advance: you can complete every checked item without another person telling you which control to use. level 12 - independence ☐ read, post, comment, message, add accessible media, and adjust privacy without assistance. ready to advance: you can complete every checked item without another person telling you which control to use. part 22 - quick reference accessible content checklist ☐ sentence case ☐ short paragraphs ☐ camelcase hashtags ☐ meaningful image alt text ☐ accurate captions ☐ essential visual information also conveyed in text/audio ☐ limited emoji repetition ☐ no decorative unicode fake fonts ☐ audience checked before posting youtube task command / method search / play/pause k captions c mute m full screen f next video shift+n shortcut list shift+? x task command / method new post n like l reply r repost t dm m next/previous post j/k home g then h notifications g then n profile g then p settings g then s shortcut list ? part 23 - official resources facebook - edit photos and add alternative text linkedin - screen reader support linkedin - add alternative text to images youtube - use youtube with a screen reader youtube - keyboard shortcuts youtube - manage caption settings x - accessibility features x - add image descriptions x - how to post and keyboard shortcuts final independence checklist ☐ i can identify navigation, feed, search, notifications, messages, profile, and settings on a social platform. ☐ i can read a feed without tabbing through every control. ☐ i can create a text post and verify the audience. ☐ i can add useful image descriptions/alt text. ☐ i understand captions and audio-description principles. ☐ i write camelcase hashtags and avoid inaccessible decorative text. ☐ i can use facebook feed, posting, comments, groups, and messages. ☐ i can use linkedin home, profile, posts, networking, messaging, and jobs. ☐ i can search and watch youtube with a screen reader. ☐ i can use youtube player shortcuts and captions. ☐ i can use x timeline and keyboard shortcuts. ☐ i can create an x post with image description. ☐ i can use social apps with voiceover or talkback. ☐ i understand audience/privacy settings and social-media scam risks. ☐ i can recover from lost focus, edit-field mode, missing alt-text controls, and dense feeds. most important habit: before you publish, verify three things in order: content, accessibility, audience. before you trust a direct message, verify identity through a separate trusted path. return to all manuals

entries.title: Victor Reader Stream 3 Manual
entries.snippet: Victor Reader Stream 3 Manual: step-by-step keyboard and screen-reader instructions, practice, troubleshooting, and command references.
entries.text: victor reader stream 3 manual - accessible learning center skip to main content accessible learning center manual victor reader stream 3 manual keys, navigation, books, audio, and online features independent self-study guide all manuals table of contents start of manual purpose: this manual teaches the victor reader stream 3 from the beginning. it assumes no prior experience with the device and gives physical orientation, exact key sequences, expected speech feedback, troubleshooting, practice, and independent-use checklists. reference: this guide is based on humanware's current stream 3 support materials and user guide version 1.6, with nls/bard information cross-checked against current nls resources. terminology: this manual calls the # key confirm and the * key cancel, matching the device's spoken/manual terminology. how to use this manual keep the stream upright with the numeric keypad facing you and the speaker holes on the bottom edge. learn the physical layout before trying online services. use key describer mode when you forget a key. use key 1 to move among bookshelves and keys 4/6 to move among books on a bookshelf. use keys 2/8 to choose a navigation level and keys 4/6 to move backward/forward at that level. press play/stop to begin or pause reading. press key 5 for where am i? information. press key 0 for device/book information. press and hold key 1 to open the built-in user guide. do not enter bard or bookshare credentials when another person can hear them unless you are comfortable with that privacy risk. table of contents part 1 - what the victor reader stream 3 is part 2 - physical orientation part 3 - charging, power, and battery part 4 - key describer mode part 5 - the bookshelf system part 6 - basic playback part 7 - navigation by heading, page, time, and text part 8 - go to commands part 9 - where am i and info part 10 - sleep timer and clock part 11 - bookmarks part 12 - managing books and files part 13 - sd card and computer file transfer part 14 - text, epub, brf, music, podcasts, and notes part 15 - wi-fi and airplane mode part 16 - bluetooth part 17 - nls bard part 18 - bookshare, nfb-newsline, internet radio, podcasts, and tunein part 19 - recording and audio notes part 20 - settings and software updates part 21 - nls authorization part 22 - troubleshooting part 23 - independent practice course part 24 - quick reference part 25 - official resources part 1 - what the victor reader stream 3 is the victor reader stream 3 is a pocket-size talking-book and media player from humanware. it supports daisy and nls digital talking books, electronic text, braille files, music, podcasts, online book services, internet radio, recording, wi-fi, bluetooth, an sd card, and internal storage. offline bookcase: books and files stored in internal memory or on the sd card. online bookcase: wi-fi services such as nls bard, bookshare, podcasts, radio, and other configured services. bookshelf: one category of content inside a bookcase. navigation level: chapter, heading, page, time jump, paragraph, line, word, character, or another structure supported by the current book. confirm: the # key. cancel: the * key. part 2 - physical orientation 2.1 front face hold the stream upright with the keypad facing you. at the very top of the front face are three special keys. left: square go to key. center: round online key. right: diamond-shaped bookmark key. just above the go to key is a tiny hole for the built-in mono microphone. below those three keys is a telephone-style 12-key numeric pad. key 5 has two raised dots. keys 2, 4, 6, and 8 have tactile raised edges. below the numeric pad are four playback keys. rewind is bottom-left and has a raised edge. fast forward is bottom-right and has a raised edge. play/stop is centered between them. sleep is directly above play/stop. 2.2 left side near the top-left side is the power/toggle button. directly below power is the status led. below the led is a rocker-style up/down control. it changes whichever setting power/toggle has selected: volume, speed, tone, or pitch. at the bottom-left side is a stereo microphone/line-in jack. 2.3 right, top, bottom, and back right side near the top: record button, identified by a raised red circle. top edge: sd-card slot under a small silicone cover. bottom edge center: usb-c port for charging and computer connection. bottom edge left of usb-c: headphone/external-speaker jack. bottom edge right of usb-c: four small holes for the built-in speaker. back: model and serial-number label surrounded by a rubber outline. orientation practice: without powering on the device, locate go to, online, bookmark, 5, play/stop, sleep, power, up/down, record, sd slot, usb-c, headphones, and speaker. part 3 - charging, power, and battery 3.1 charge the stream what you will learn: connect power safely. before you begin: use the supplied usb-c cable and a suitable usb power adapter. exactly how to do it locate the usb-c port at the bottom center. insert the usb-c plug without forcing it. connect the other end to the power adapter. plug the adapter into ac power. leave the stream charging. a full ac charge can take up to about three hours. what should happen: when the player is off and charging, the led blinks. when it is on while charging, the led stays steady. if that does not happen: if it does not charge, try the supplied adapter/cable and another outlet. computer usb charging can be slower or insufficient. practice: charge the device and check battery status. 3.2 turn on or off what you will learn: power the device intentionally. before you begin: the stream has some battery charge. exactly how to do it locate power on the upper-left side. press and hold it until the stream starts. wait for spoken startup feedback. to power off, press and hold power again until shutdown begins. what should happen: the stream starts or shuts down with speech feedback. if that does not happen: if the unit is unresponsive, connect ac power and retry. if necessary use the documented power-button reset procedure. practice: turn the stream on, identify the active bookshelf, then shut it down. battery status: press and hold confirm (#), or press info (0), to hear battery/charging status. part 4 - key describer mode 4.1 learn keys safely what you will learn: have the stream announce keys without carrying out normal actions. before you begin: the stream is on. exactly how to do it press and hold info (0) to enter key describer mode. press any front key. listen to its name/function. try the side controls and playback keys. press and hold info (0) again to exit. what should happen: keys are described instead of performing their ordinary command. if that does not happen: if the stream performs commands, key describer mode was not entered; retry the long press. practice: identify every key without looking at a printed guide. part 5 - the bookshelf system task key / control move to next bookshelf 1 previous/next book on shelf 4 / 6 play selected book play/stop online/offline bookcase online key built-in user guide press and hold 1 5.1 choose a bookshelf and book what you will learn: find content by category. before you begin: the stream contains at least one book/file. exactly how to do it press 1. listen to the bookshelf name. press 1 repeatedly until the desired bookshelf is announced. press 4 or 6 to move backward/forward through books. listen to each title. press play/stop on the desired book. what should happen: the selected book begins where you last stopped, when resume information is available. if that does not happen: if a bookshelf says zero books, choose another shelf or add content. practice: locate three different shelves and one title on each. 5.2 switch online and offline what you will learn: move between local and internet content. before you begin: wi-fi may be needed for online services. exactly how to do it tap the round online key above number 2. listen for online or offline bookcase. press 1 to hear the first bookshelf in that bookcase. tap online again to return. what should happen: the bookcase changes while the same basic bookshelf navigation model remains. if that does not happen: if online services do not work, wi-fi may be off or airplane mode may be on. practice: switch bookcases three times and identify each. part 6 - basic playback task key / control play / pause play/stop jump back 5 seconds short press rewind jump forward 5 seconds short press fast forward progressively rewind press and hold rewind progressively fast-forward press and hold fast forward 6.1 read an audio book what you will learn: start, pause, and review audio. before you begin: select an audio book. exactly how to do it press play/stop. listen for at least 20 seconds. press play/stop to pause. short-press rewind. press play/stop. short-press fast forward. pause again. what should happen: playback starts/stops and short presses move about five seconds in audio content. if that does not happen: in text content, short rewind/fast forward can move by line and held presses use percentage jumps instead of audio time. practice: practice until you can use all four playback controls by touch. part 7 - navigation by heading, page, time, and text 7.1 choose a navigation level what you will learn: move by the structure supported by the current book. before you begin: open a structured daisy or text book. exactly how to do it press 2 or 8. listen to the current navigation level. continue pressing 2/8 until you hear the level you want, such as heading, page, time jump, paragraph, line, word, or character. press 4 to move backward at that level. press 6 to move forward. what should happen: the stream moves according to the selected level. if that does not happen: not every book contains every navigation level. if 'page' or a heading level is absent, the book may not include it. practice: navigate by at least three different levels. text navigation: text-to-speech books can expose paragraph, sentence, word, and character navigation. html/xml/docx/epub content may also expose headings. part 8 - go to commands 8.1 go directly to a page or heading what you will learn: jump instead of stepping repeatedly. before you begin: use a book that contains the requested structure. exactly how to do it press the square go to key above number 1. listen to the type of destination requested. enter the number with the numeric keypad. press confirm (#). what should happen: the stream moves to that page/heading/destination. if that does not happen: if the number does not exist, the stream announces an error or remains near the current position. practice: go to two valid pages or headings. go to can also support time, percentage, beginning/end, book number, and online-service actions depending on context. while on a bookshelf, go to can be used to enter a relative book number, then confirm. part 9 - where am i and info 9.1 ask where am i? what you will learn: hear current reading position without changing it. before you begin: a book is open. exactly how to do it press 5. listen to title and current position information. press and hold 5 when you want additional device/book identification information such as serial/model information. what should happen: the stream reports context without moving your place. if that does not happen: information varies by book type. practice: use where am i? in an audio book and a text book. 9.2 hear general information what you will learn: review battery, storage, book, and device information. before you begin: the stream is on. exactly how to do it press 0. use 4 and 6 if multiple information items are available. listen for battery, storage, title, position, or device information. press cancel (*) to leave if needed. what should happen: you can review status without opening settings. if that does not happen: exact items vary with current content and device state. practice: find battery status and one storage/device item. part 10 - sleep timer and clock 10.1 set a sleep timer what you will learn: have the stream stop after a chosen interval. before you begin: a book is playing or paused. exactly how to do it press sleep once. listen to the announced timer. press sleep repeatedly to cycle available timer values. stop on the desired time. to cancel, cycle until sleep off is announced. what should happen: the player will stop/shut down according to the configured sleep behavior. if that does not happen: available values can be customized in settings; common choices include 15, 30, 45, and 60 minutes. practice: set 15 minutes and then turn sleep off. time/date: press and hold sleep to hear the current time and date. part 11 - bookmarks 11.1 insert and return to a bookmark what you will learn: mark a location for later. before you begin: open a book. exactly how to do it move to the location. press bookmark. follow the spoken prompt to insert a bookmark and confirm if requested. continue reading elsewhere. use the bookmark navigation options to return to the saved marker. what should happen: the stream stores the bookmark for the book. if that does not happen: bookmark behavior can vary by content type. audio, highlight, and numbered bookmarks are also supported. practice: create and return to two bookmarks. text-entry role: the diamond bookmark key also changes lowercase/uppercase/numeric text-entry modes when typing in fields such as wi-fi or account credentials. part 12 - managing books and files 12.1 use manage books what you will learn: perform context-specific file actions. before you begin: focus a disposable book/file. exactly how to do it press 3. listen to available management actions. use 4/6 or the announced navigation keys to review them. choose an action only after hearing the selected title again. press confirm to proceed or cancel to leave. what should happen: the available actions reflect the current bookshelf/content. if that does not happen: deleting a book removes that local copy. re-download may require internet/service access. practice: open manage books on a practice file and cancel. part 13 - sd card and computer file transfer 13.1 insert an sd card what you will learn: add removable storage. before you begin: power can be on or off, but handle the card gently. exactly how to do it locate the silicone-covered sd slot on the top edge. open the cover. orient the card correctly and insert it until seated. wait for stream detection and spoken feedback. what should happen: the stream detects the sd card and its supported bookshelf folders/content. if that does not happen: never force the card. if it is not recognized, power-cycle and verify formatting/card health. practice: insert and identify an sd card if available. 13.2 transfer files from windows what you will learn: copy supported content using usb-c. before you begin: have a windows computer and usb cable. exactly how to do it connect the stream to the computer using the bottom-center usb-c port. wait for windows to detect it as a portable/mtp device. open file explorer. open the stream's internal memory or sd-card storage. copy supported files into appropriate folders/bookshelves. use windows' safe-device practices and disconnect the cable. let the stream rescan content. what should happen: transferred books/files appear on the relevant bookshelf. if that does not happen: if the stream is not detected, try another usb port/cable and unlock/restart the device if needed. practice: transfer one harmless mp3 or text file. supported formats: current nls/humanware references list formats including daisy, brf, docx, epub, html, mp3, flac, ogg, wav, txt, xml, and others. part 14 - text, epub, brf, music, podcasts, and notes text bookshelf: electronic text read through the stream's text-to-speech voice. brf/braille files: handled as text/braille content with the configured braille translation table where applicable. epub/html/docx: may expose heading navigation when the source file contains structure. music bookshelf: audio files and folders; music speed remains normal by default and bass/treble options are available. saved podcasts: downloaded podcast episodes stored for offline playback. notes: recordings and note files created/managed on the device. accessibility principle: a well-structured source file gives better heading/page navigation than an unstructured text conversion. part 15 - wi-fi and airplane mode 15.1 turn wireless on what you will learn: disable airplane mode so wi-fi/bluetooth can operate. before you begin: wireless use is permitted where you are. exactly how to do it press and hold the online key. listen for airplane mode status. if it announces airplane mode on, press/hold again or use settings to turn airplane mode off. open settings with 7. navigate to wireless and then wi-fi. confirm wi-fi is on. what should happen: wireless features become available. if that does not happen: humanware documents airplane mode as on by default; when it is on, wi-fi and bluetooth are disabled. practice: turn airplane mode on and off once. 15.2 connect to wi-fi what you will learn: join a wireless network directly on the stream. before you begin: know the network name and password. exactly how to do it press 7 for settings. navigate to wireless > wi-fi > new connection. choose scan for connection. use 4/6 to find the network and press confirm. enter the wi-fi password with multi-tap text entry. use bookmark to switch lowercase, uppercase, and numeric entry when needed. press confirm. check wi-fi status afterward. what should happen: the stream connects and announces network status. if that does not happen: if the password is rejected, check case, punctuation, and text-entry mode. use key describer/user guide to relearn multi-tap entry if needed. practice: connect to a trusted wi-fi network. part 16 - bluetooth 16.1 pair bluetooth headphones or speaker what you will learn: use wireless audio output. before you begin: airplane mode is off and the bluetooth device is in pairing mode. exactly how to do it press 7. navigate to wireless > bluetooth. turn bluetooth on. choose the option to scan/pair a device. use 4/6 through discovered device names. press confirm on the intended device. wait for connected confirmation. what should happen: stream audio routes to the paired bluetooth device. if that does not happen: if the device is not found, put it back into pairing mode and move it closer. airplane mode must be off. practice: pair and disconnect a noncritical bluetooth audio device. privacy: bluetooth device names can reveal personal names/model information. verify the exact device before pairing in public places. part 17 - nls bard eligible u.s. nls patrons can configure bard on the stream 3 and search/download books over wi-fi. 17.1 add an nls bard account what you will learn: enable the bard online bookshelf. before you begin: you have active bard credentials and wi-fi is connected. exactly how to do it press 7 for settings. use navigation to open online settings. open book services. move to nls bard. choose add account and press confirm. enter the bard email address with multi-tap entry, then confirm. enter the password, using bookmark to switch case/numeric mode, then confirm. wait for the service-enabled announcement. what should happen: an nls bard bookshelf appears in the online bookcase. if that does not happen: if validation fails, verify the same credentials on the bard website and check wi-fi. do not repeatedly guess passwords if the account may lock. practice: add the account only when you are ready to protect the credentials. 17.2 search and download a bard book what you will learn: find bard content directly from the stream. before you begin: bard is configured and wi-fi works. exactly how to do it tap online to enter the online bookcase. press 1 until nls bard is announced. use go to to reach search or use 4/6 to the search option. press confirm. use 2/8 through search types and confirm the desired one. enter the search text. review results with 4/6. press 5 for a short description. press bookmark to add a result to the bard wish list when available. press confirm to download, or play/stop to begin reading the selected result when supported. what should happen: the book downloads or begins reading according to the selected action. if that does not happen: if no results appear, broaden the search. if downloading fails, check wi-fi and bard status. practice: search for one known author or title. nls authorization: nls books also require the stream to be authorized. humanware provides online authorization/key-download procedures; see part 21. part 18 - bookshare, nfb-newsline, internet radio, podcasts, and tunein bookshare: configured under online settings > book services using eligible account credentials. nfb-newsline: available to eligible u.s. users when configured. internet radio: search and save stations using online services. podcasts: search/add feeds and download/manage episodes. tunein: can be used without an account for basic listening; account pairing enables library/favorites features. wikipedia/wiktionary references: available as online reference features in supported configurations. availability: online services can change independently of the stream firmware. if a service disappears, verify current humanware support information before resetting the device. part 19 - recording and audio notes 19.1 make a recording what you will learn: create a spoken note with the built-in microphone. before you begin: use a quiet environment and respect recording consent. exactly how to do it locate the record button near the top of the right side. press record to start according to the current recording configuration. speak toward the small built-in microphone hole above go to. use the record control again to stop/save as prompted. find the recording in the notes/recording location. what should happen: a recording is created in the configured format/location. if that does not happen: if the recording is silent, check recording source and volume settings. practice: record a ten-second non-sensitive note. external recording: the bottom-left-side microphone/line-in jack can accept an external source. settings control preferred source, recording volume, file type, and save location. part 20 - settings and software updates 20.1 navigate settings what you will learn: change one setting at a time and verify the result. before you begin: the stream is on. exactly how to do it press 7. use the announced navigation keys to move among major categories such as general, navigation/playback, wireless, recording, and online settings. press confirm to enter a category. use 4/6 or 2/8 as announced to review choices. press confirm to accept or cancel to back out. what should happen: the chosen setting changes only after confirmation. if that does not happen: if you become lost, press cancel repeatedly and reopen settings. practice: find language, sleep configuration, and wireless without changing them. 20.2 check for updates what you will learn: install current stream software when appropriate. before you begin: connect to stable wi-fi and preferably ac power. exactly how to do it press 7. navigate to online settings > software update. choose check for updates. press confirm. follow spoken prompts if an update is available. do not interrupt power during installation. what should happen: the stream reports current software or installs an available update. if that does not happen: if the update fails, restore stable wi-fi/power and retry. humanware also provides manual sd-card update packages. practice: check for updates without forcing an unnecessary reinstall. part 21 - nls authorization 21.1 refresh nls user keys over wi-fi what you will learn: authorize nls playback when humanware/nls instructs you to do so. before you begin: wi-fi is connected. exactly how to do it press 7 until general settings is reached. navigate to online settings and press confirm. open software update. move to check for updates. press confirm. wait for the server check and listen for a user-keys processed message when applicable. what should happen: the stream receives available authorization keys. if that does not happen: if nls books remain unauthorized, follow humanware's current nls authorization support steps or contact nls/humanware rather than repeatedly changing unrelated settings. practice: know where this command is, even if authorization is already working. part 22 - troubleshooting 22.1 no sound what you will learn: check playback and output before resetting. before you begin: a book is selected. exactly how to do it press play/stop. short-press power until volume is selected. press the left-side up control several times. unplug headphones if you expect the built-in speaker. disconnect bluetooth if audio may be routed wirelessly. what should happen: audio becomes audible through the intended output. if that does not happen: if not, try another book and headphones, then inspect settings. practice: practice identifying the current audio output. 22.2 cannot find a book what you will learn: rebuild your location: bookcase, bookshelf, book. before you begin: content should be present. exactly how to do it tap online to verify whether you are in offline or online bookcase. press 1 repeatedly through bookshelves. use 4/6 through titles. use go to book-number navigation if you know the relative position. check the sd card/computer transfer if local content is missing. what should happen: you locate the content or identify which storage/service is missing. if that does not happen: do not reset the stream just because you are on the wrong bookshelf. practice: find one local and one online title. 22.3 wi-fi will not connect what you will learn: check airplane mode and credentials. before you begin: a known network is available. exactly how to do it press and hold online and verify airplane mode is off. open wireless > wi-fi > status. rescan the network. re-enter the password carefully, checking uppercase/lowercase/numeric mode with bookmark. move closer to the router. what should happen: the stream connects or gives a specific failure. if that does not happen: if the network uses a captive portal or unsupported enterprise setup, direct stream connection may not be possible. practice: reconnect to a trusted network. 22.4 bard search or download fails what you will learn: separate service/account issues from basic wi-fi. before you begin: bard is configured. exactly how to do it verify wi-fi status. confirm another online service works if available. open nls bard bookshelf. retry a simple title/author search. if account validation fails, test the credentials on bard outside the stream. check current humanware/nls service notices before deleting the account. what should happen: you identify whether the problem is connectivity, credentials, service availability, or content. if that does not happen: avoid removing a working account until simpler checks are completed. practice: practice the diagnostic sequence. 22.5 device seems frozen what you will learn: use safe recovery before reset. before you begin: the stream does not respond normally. exactly how to do it press play/stop and cancel to see whether playback/menu focus is simply paused. connect ac power. press and hold power for the documented shutdown/reset behavior. restart and check info for battery/software state. what should happen: the stream restarts or returns to normal operation. if that does not happen: if it remains unresponsive, use humanware's current reset/troubleshooting guidance or support rather than forcing ports/cards. practice: know the safe recovery order. part 23 - independent practice course level 1 - physical orientation ☐ locate every front key. ☐ locate power/up-down. ☐ locate sd, usb-c, headphones, speaker. ☐ use key describer. ready to advance: you can complete every checked item without another person telling you which key to press. level 2 - local reading ☐ choose bookshelf. ☐ choose book. ☐ play/pause. ☐ rewind/fast-forward. ☐ use where am i. ready to advance: you can complete every checked item without another person telling you which key to press. level 3 - navigation ☐ choose heading level. ☐ move by heading. ☐ choose time/page/text level. ☐ use go to. ready to advance: you can complete every checked item without another person telling you which key to press. level 4 - utility ☐ set sleep timer. ☐ hear time/date. ☐ insert bookmark. ☐ use info. ready to advance: you can complete every checked item without another person telling you which key to press. level 5 - storage ☐ insert sd card. ☐ connect to computer. ☐ transfer one safe file. ☐ find it on stream. ready to advance: you can complete every checked item without another person telling you which key to press. level 6 - wireless ☐ toggle airplane mode. ☐ connect wi-fi. ☐ check status. ☐ pair bluetooth audio. ready to advance: you can complete every checked item without another person telling you which key to press. level 7 - bard ☐ open online bookcase. ☐ open bard shelf. ☐ search. ☐ hear description. ☐ download/read test title. ready to advance: you can complete every checked item without another person telling you which key to press. level 8 - other online services ☐ identify bookshare/nfb/radio/podcast/tunein options available on your unit. ready to advance: you can complete every checked item without another person telling you which key to press. level 9 - recording ☐ create short recording. ☐ find it. ☐ play it. ☐ delete disposable recording. ready to advance: you can complete every checked item without another person telling you which key to press. level 10 - independence ☐ start from powered off. ☐ find local book. ☐ navigate/read/bookmark. ☐ find online book. ☐ use sleep timer. ☐ shut down. ready to advance: you can complete every checked item without another person telling you which key to press. part 24 - quick reference front key map task key / control go to square key above 1 online / bookcase toggle round key above 2 bookmark / text-entry mode diamond key above 3 bookshelf 1 navigation level up/down 2 / 8 manage books 3 previous / next item 4 / 6 where am i? 5 settings 7 playback mode 9 info 0 cancel * confirm # play / stop bottom center rewind / fast forward bottom left / bottom right sleep / time-date above play/stop core reading pattern task key / control choose bookshelf 1 choose book 4 / 6 start reading play/stop choose navigation level 2 / 8 move at that level 4 / 6 current position 5 direct jump go to then number then # built-in user guide hold 1 part 25 - official resources humanware victor reader stream 3 support humanware stream 3 training and troubleshooting humanware stream 3 faq nls commercial players compatible with nls materials nls digital audiobook players final independence checklist ☐ i can physically orient the stream and identify every major control. ☐ i can charge, power on/off, and check battery status. ☐ i can use key describer and the built-in user guide. ☐ i understand offline/online bookcases and bookshelves. ☐ i can choose a book and control playback. ☐ i can navigate by structure and use go to. ☐ i can use where am i, info, sleep timer, and bookmarks. ☐ i can use an sd card and transfer files by usb. ☐ i can connect wi-fi and understand airplane mode. ☐ i can pair bluetooth audio. ☐ i can configure and use nls bard when eligible. ☐ i understand other online service categories. ☐ i can make a recording and find it. ☐ i can navigate settings without making accidental changes. ☐ i can check for software updates. ☐ i understand nls authorization/key refresh. ☐ i can troubleshoot sound, missing books, wi-fi, bard, and an unresponsive device. most important habit: when lost, rebuild context in this order: online or offline bookcase, bookshelf with key 1, book with 4/6, navigation level with 2/8, then move with 4/6. use key 5 to confirm where you are before changing settings. return to all manuals

entries.title: VoiceOver Manual for Mac
entries.snippet: VoiceOver Manual for Mac: step-by-step keyboard and screen-reader instructions, practice, troubleshooting, and command references.
entries.text: voiceover manual for mac - accessible learning center skip to main content accessible learning center manual voiceover manual for mac macos keyboard commands, navigation, and applications independent self-study guide for mac all manuals table of contents start of manual apple voiceover user guide purpose: this manual is written directly to the person learning voiceover. it explains exactly what to press, what should happen, and how to recover when the result is different. vo: vo means the voiceover modifier. by default, use control+option together. caps lock can also be configured as the voiceover modifier. function keys: apple notes that voiceover commands using f1-f12 may also require fn depending on your mac keyboard settings. table of contents part 1 - what voiceover is part 2 - turn voiceover on and off part 3 - voiceover modifier and keyboard help part 4 - move through the mac interface part 5 - interact with groups part 6 - activate controls part 7 - desktop, dock, and menu bar part 8 - finder and spotlight part 9 - apps and windows part 10 - voiceover rotor and item chooser part 11 - quick nav part 12 - web navigation part 13 - read and edit text part 14 - tables and structured content part 15 - notifications and screen sharing part 16 - braille displays and braille access part 17 - trackpad gestures part 18 - voiceover utility part 19 - speech, pronunciation, verbosity, and punctuation part 20 - customize commands and activities part 21 - troubleshooting part 22 - independent practice course part 23 - quick reference commands part 24 - official apple resources part 1 - what voiceover is voiceover is the screen reader built into macos. it speaks and can display in braille the item currently selected by the voiceover cursor. you can control the mac with keyboard commands, trackpad gestures, or a connected braille display. voiceover cursor: the item voiceover is currently describing. keyboard focus: the control receiving keyboard input. interaction: entering a group, toolbar, table, web area, or other container so you can move through its contents. activation: performing the action of the selected control. rotor: a navigation tool that lets you choose categories such as headings, links, or form controls. item chooser: a searchable list of items available in the current context. part 2 - turn voiceover on and off 2.1 turn voiceover on what you will learn: start voiceover. before you begin: be at the mac keyboard. exactly how to do it hold command. press f5 once. release both keys. if your mac requires fn for function keys, try command+fn+f5. listen for voiceover speech. what should happen: voiceover announces that it is on and begins speaking the focused item. if that does not happen: if nothing happens, open system settings > accessibility > voiceover and turn voiceover on there. practice: turn voiceover off and on twice. task command turn voiceover on/off command+f5 alternative on touch id mac hold command and quickly press touch id three times part 3 - voiceover modifier and keyboard help 3.1 learn the vo modifier what you will learn: use voiceover commands correctly. before you begin: voiceover is on. exactly how to do it place one finger on control and one on option. hold both keys together. while holding them, press right arrow once. release all keys. repeat using left arrow. what should happen: voiceover moves to the next or previous item. if that does not happen: if nothing changes, make sure both control and option were held while the arrow key was pressed. practice: move forward five items and backward five items. 3.2 use keyboard help what you will learn: safely learn what keys and commands do. before you begin: voiceover is on. exactly how to do it press vo+k. press a key or voiceover command you want to identify. listen to voiceover describe it. try several commands. press escape to leave keyboard help. what should happen: voiceover identifies commands without carrying them out normally. if that does not happen: if the command performs an action instead, keyboard help may not have opened; press vo+k again. practice: identify vo+space, vo+right arrow, vo+left arrow, and vo+shift+down arrow. part 4 - move through the mac interface task command next item vo+right arrow previous item vo+left arrow read from current position vo+a read from top vo+b pause/resume speech control 4.1 move one item at a time what you will learn: navigate without using a mouse. before you begin: voiceover is on. exactly how to do it press vo+right arrow once. stop and listen to the item name and type. press vo+right arrow again. press vo+left arrow once and confirm you returned. continue one item at a time. what should happen: voiceover describes a different item after each move. if that does not happen: if movement seems stuck, you may be inside a group or control. press vo+shift+up arrow to move outward, then try again. practice: explore ten items on the current screen without activating them. part 5 - interact with groups task command interact with group vo+shift+down arrow stop interacting vo+shift+up arrow 5.1 enter and leave a group what you will learn: reach controls that are inside toolbars, tables, web areas, and other containers. before you begin: voiceover is focused on a group or container. exactly how to do it listen for voiceover to announce a group, toolbar, table, or similar container. press vo+shift+down arrow. press vo+right arrow to move through items inside it. when finished, press vo+shift+up arrow. continue vo+right arrow at the outer level. what should happen: you can move inside the group and then return to its parent level. if that does not happen: if voiceover skips controls you expect to be inside a group, interact with it. if you feel trapped, press vo+shift+up arrow more than once. practice: enter a toolbar, inspect three items, then leave it. part 6 - activate controls task command activate selected control vo+space 6.1 activate a button or link what you will learn: perform the action of the selected item. before you begin: voiceover is focused on the desired control. exactly how to do it use vo+right/left arrow until voiceover announces the exact button, link, checkbox, or other control. stop and confirm the name. press vo+space. listen for what changed before pressing another key. what should happen: the button activates, link opens, checkbox toggles, or control performs its action. if that does not happen: if the wrong action occurs, you activated the wrong item. return and confirm the control name before pressing vo+space. practice: find a harmless button and activate it deliberately. part 7 - desktop, dock, and menu bar task command move to dock vo+d open apple menu vo+shift+m 7.1 open an app from the dock what you will learn: use the dock without a mouse. before you begin: voiceover is on. exactly how to do it press vo+d. use vo+right/left arrow through dock items. stop when the desired app is announced. press vo+space. what should happen: the application opens or comes to the front. if that does not happen: if the dock does not appear, make sure voiceover is active and try vo+d again. practice: open finder or another safe app from the dock. 7.2 use the menu bar what you will learn: open menus and choose commands. before you begin: an app is active. exactly how to do it press vo+m or use the appropriate voiceover menu-bar navigation command for your configuration. move through menu headings. open the desired menu with vo+space. use arrow keys or vo navigation through menu items. press enter/vo+space on the command. press escape to close without choosing. what should happen: the selected menu command runs. if that does not happen: if focus remains inside the application, use the apple menu shortcut vo+shift+m as a reliable starting point. practice: open the apple menu and close it with escape. part 8 - finder and spotlight 8.1 open spotlight what you will learn: find an app, file, or setting quickly. before you begin: be anywhere in macos. exactly how to do it press command+space. type a search term such as textedit. use up/down arrow or voiceover navigation through results. press return on the desired result. what should happen: the selected app/file/result opens. if that does not happen: if spotlight does not open, check whether another app has reassigned command+space. practice: open textedit with spotlight. 8.2 navigate finder what you will learn: browse files and folders. before you begin: finder is open. exactly how to do it use vo+right/left arrow through finder controls. interact with the file list/table when announced using vo+shift+down arrow. use arrow keys or voiceover navigation through items. press command+o or return/vo+space as appropriate to open the selected item. use vo+shift+up arrow to leave the file list. what should happen: you can select and open files/folders. if that does not happen: if arrow keys do not move through files, make sure focus is inside the file list. practice: open a folder and return to its parent. part 9 - apps and windows task command switch apps command+tab close window command+w quit app command+q ignore next keypress vo+tab 9.1 switch applications what you will learn: move between open apps. before you begin: at least two apps are open. exactly how to do it hold command. press tab repeatedly while continuing to hold command. listen for the desired app. release command. what should happen: the selected application becomes active. if that does not happen: if the app you want is not listed, it may not be open. practice: switch between finder and textedit three times. part 10 - voiceover rotor and item chooser task command open rotor vo+u open item chooser vo+i 10.1 use the rotor what you will learn: navigate by category rather than item-by-item. before you begin: be on a webpage or context where rotor categories are available. exactly how to do it press vo+u. move among rotor categories with left/right arrow. choose a category such as headings, links, buttons, or form controls. move through matching items with up/down arrow. press enter/vo+space on the desired item or exit the rotor as appropriate. what should happen: you jump among items in the selected category. if that does not happen: if a category is missing, it may not apply to the current context or may be disabled in voiceover settings. practice: open a webpage and move by headings. 10.2 use item chooser what you will learn: find an item from a searchable list. before you begin: be in an app or webpage with many controls. exactly how to do it press vo+i. type part of the item name if search is available. move through matching items. press enter on the desired item. what should happen: voiceover moves to the chosen item. if that does not happen: if nothing matches, try a shorter search term. practice: use item chooser to find a known button or link. part 11 - quick nav quick nav lets you use shorter navigation commands in supported contexts, especially webpages. it can be enabled with the left and right arrow keys pressed together in many voiceover configurations. important: when quick nav is on, ordinary typing/navigation behavior can change. if keys behave unexpectedly in a text field, check whether quick nav is active. use quick nav for efficient webpage navigation. turn it off before typing if it interferes with text entry. use keyboard help or apple's current quick nav documentation to confirm the exact command set for your macos version. part 12 - web navigation voiceover can navigate webpages by dom order, groups, headings, links, buttons, form controls, landmarks, tables, images, frames, and live regions. 12.1 scan a webpage by headings what you will learn: understand a page before reading every line. before you begin: safari or another accessible browser is open on a webpage. exactly how to do it press vo+u. choose headings in the rotor. move through heading items with up/down arrow. stop on a heading that sounds relevant. activate or exit the rotor to move to that section. use vo+a or normal navigation to read from there. what should happen: you can jump directly to major sections. if that does not happen: if the page has no headings, use landmarks, links, or buttons instead. practice: find the main heading and two subheadings on a webpage. 12.2 navigate form controls what you will learn: complete fields and buttons on a webpage. before you begin: be on a webpage containing a form. exactly how to do it use the rotor and choose form controls. move to the desired text field, checkbox, popup, or button. if required, interact with the control using vo+shift+down arrow. type or choose the value. stop interacting when finished. move to the next form control. what should happen: you can complete the form without manually reading every page element. if that does not happen: if typing triggers navigation, check quick nav and focus/interaction state. practice: fill a safe practice form. part 13 - read and edit text 13.1 read text what you will learn: read continuously from your current location. before you begin: focus is in readable text. exactly how to do it move voiceover to the desired starting point. press vo+a. listen while voiceover reads. press control to pause speech. press control again to resume where supported, or restart reading from the desired position. what should happen: voiceover reads from the current location. if that does not happen: if it reads the wrong area, move the voiceover cursor to the text first. practice: read one paragraph and pause halfway. 13.2 edit text what you will learn: type, move the insertion point, and correct text. before you begin: be in an editable text field or document. exactly how to do it move to the text field. interact if required. type a sentence. use left/right arrow to move the insertion point by character. use option+left/right arrow to move by word in standard mac text editing. use backspace/delete to remove text. type the correction. use vo+a or text-navigation commands to review. what should happen: the text changes at the insertion point. if that does not happen: if typed letters trigger voiceover navigation, verify that keyboard focus is in the text field and quick nav is not intercepting typing. practice: type a sentence with one deliberate error and correct it. part 14 - tables and structured content when voiceover reaches a table, interact with it to navigate its cells. voiceover can announce row/column information depending on verbosity and the app. 14.1 navigate a table what you will learn: move through structured rows and columns. before you begin: voiceover is focused on a table. exactly how to do it press vo+shift+down arrow to interact. use voiceover/arrow navigation through cells. listen for row and column information. move systematically rather than jumping randomly. press vo+shift+up arrow when finished. what should happen: you can inspect table cells and leave the table. if that does not happen: if voiceover only says 'table' and skips cells, interact with it first. practice: read at least three cells from a simple table. part 15 - notifications and screen sharing task command open notifications menu vo+n 15.1 review voiceover notifications what you will learn: find recent voiceover/macos notifications. before you begin: voiceover is on. exactly how to do it press vo+n. move through available notifications. activate an action if desired or press escape to close. what should happen: the voiceover notifications menu opens. if that does not happen: if there are no notifications, the menu may be empty. practice: open and close the menu. macos tahoe adds voiceover features for screen sharing. when sharing a mac screen, review voiceover utility's screen sharing category and apple's current screen sharing documentation for the exact setup that matches your situation. part 16 - braille displays and braille access voiceover supports compatible refreshable braille displays over bluetooth or usb. macos tahoe also includes braille access and braille keyboard input features. connect a supported display through bluetooth or usb. open voiceover utility > braille to review display, translation, layout, status, and braille access settings. cursor-routing keys can move voiceover focus or the insertion point to the cell represented by the routing button. braille keyboard input can use supported display keys for braille entry and assigned commands. braille access can provide a more notetaker-like environment on supported configurations. 16.1 verify a braille display connection what you will learn: confirm the display actually works with voiceover. before you begin: pair/connect the braille display. exactly how to do it open voiceover utility. open braille settings. confirm the display appears. move voiceover with vo+right arrow. check that braille changes. type in a text field if the display provides input. press a routing key and confirm focus/caret movement. what should happen: braille output follows voiceover and supported input/routing works. if that does not happen: if bluetooth says connected but braille does not update, check voiceover utility > braille and the display's connection mode. practice: perform the three tests: output, input, routing. part 17 - trackpad gestures voiceover can use a mac trackpad for gestures similar to iphone/ipad. enable the voiceover trackpad commander before relying on gestures. task command next item flick right previous item flick left activate item double-tap or split-tap interact two-finger flick right stop interacting two-finger flick left read from top two-finger flick up read from cursor onward two-finger flick down pause/resume speech two-finger tap change rotor two-finger rotate screen curtain three-finger triple-tap part 18 - voiceover utility task command open voiceover utility vo+fn+f8 or vo+fn+8 voiceover utility is the main configuration application for voiceover. general: overall voiceover behavior and startup options. verbosity: speech, braille, text, announcements, and hints. speech: voices and pronunciation. navigation: cursor tracking, interaction, wrapping, and movement behavior. web: webpage navigation and web rotor settings. sound: voiceover sound effects. visuals: voiceover cursor and visual panels. commands: customize keyboard commands and gestures. braille: translation, layout, status, displays, and braille access. activities: save different voiceover settings for particular tasks or apps. voiceover recognition: recognition features for otherwise inaccessible content. screen sharing: settings for voiceover during screen sharing. part 19 - speech, pronunciation, verbosity, and punctuation 19.1 change speech voice or rate what you will learn: make voiceover easier to understand. before you begin: voiceover utility is open. exactly how to do it open speech. open voices. move to the current voice and choose another voice if desired. adjust speaking rate gradually. test the result by navigating several items. keep the setting that remains clear during longer listening. what should happen: voiceover speaks with the selected voice/rate. if that does not happen: if speech becomes too fast to understand, return to the previous rate or reduce it. practice: try two rates and choose the more comfortable one. 19.2 change verbosity what you will learn: control how much information voiceover announces. before you begin: voiceover utility is open. exactly how to do it open verbosity. review speech, text, announcements, and hints settings. change one setting at a time. navigate a few controls to hear the effect. restore or refine the setting as needed. what should happen: voiceover gives more or less detail according to your choices. if that does not happen: if you become unsure what changed, reset only the changed category rather than changing several more options. practice: reduce one repetitive announcement, then restore it. part 20 - customize commands and activities voiceover utility lets you customize additional key commands and trackpad gestures. activities let you save different voiceover settings for particular apps or tasks. best practice: learn the default commands first. customize only after you understand what the default command does, and document your changes so you can recover after troubleshooting or updates. part 21 - troubleshooting 21.1 voiceover is not speaking what you will learn: restore speech in a logical order. before you begin: voiceover should be on. exactly how to do it press command+f5 and listen for the voiceover state. check mac volume and audio output. press vo+a to request reading. press control in case speech was paused. open voiceover utility and verify the selected voice/speech settings. turn voiceover off and on again if necessary. what should happen: voiceover speech returns. if that does not happen: if the mac has no sound in any app, troubleshoot system audio rather than voiceover alone. practice: memorize the order: voiceover state > volume/output > speech command > utility settings > restart voiceover. 21.2 voiceover skips controls what you will learn: recover when controls seem unreachable. before you begin: voiceover is moving but not reaching the desired control. exactly how to do it move with vo+right arrow slowly. listen for group, toolbar, table, or web area. press vo+shift+down arrow to interact. explore inside with vo+right arrow. press vo+shift+up arrow to leave. use vo+i item chooser or vo+u rotor if appropriate. what should happen: you reach controls that were previously skipped. if that does not happen: if the app is genuinely inaccessible, try an alternate control path or report the accessibility problem to the app developer. practice: find a control inside a group and activate it. 21.3 typing produces commands instead of text what you will learn: restore normal text entry. before you begin: focus should be in a text field. exactly how to do it confirm voiceover is focused on the text field. interact with the field if needed. check whether quick nav is on. turn quick nav off if it is intercepting letter keys. type a short word. use arrow keys to verify the insertion point. what should happen: letters appear in the text field. if that does not happen: if letters still do not appear, check keyboard focus and whether the app uses a special editing mode. practice: open textedit and type a short sentence. part 22 - independent practice course level 1 - core commands ☐ turn voiceover on/off. ☐ move next/previous. ☐ activate a control. ☐ use keyboard help. ready to advance: you can complete each checked task without another person telling you which key to press. level 2 - groups and apps ☐ interact with a group. ☐ leave a group. ☐ open an app from dock. ☐ switch apps with command+tab. ready to advance: you can complete each checked task without another person telling you which key to press. level 3 - finder and search ☐ open spotlight. ☐ find an app. ☐ navigate a finder file list. ☐ open a folder. ready to advance: you can complete each checked task without another person telling you which key to press. level 4 - web ☐ open rotor. ☐ move by headings. ☐ move by links. ☐ complete a safe form control. ready to advance: you can complete each checked task without another person telling you which key to press. level 5 - text ☐ type a paragraph. ☐ move by character/word. ☐ correct an error. ☐ read from current position. ready to advance: you can complete each checked task without another person telling you which key to press. level 6 - advanced ☐ use item chooser. ☐ use quick nav appropriately. ☐ navigate a table. ☐ review notifications. ready to advance: you can complete each checked task without another person telling you which key to press. level 7 - customization ☐ open voiceover utility. ☐ adjust speech rate. ☐ review verbosity. ☐ restore preferred settings. ready to advance: you can complete each checked task without another person telling you which key to press. level 8 - braille/trackpad ☐ connect and test a braille display if used. ☐ use routing keys if available. ☐ practice key trackpad gestures if used. ready to advance: you can complete each checked task without another person telling you which key to press. part 23 - quick reference commands task command voiceover on/off command+f5 next item vo+right arrow previous item vo+left arrow activate vo+space interact vo+shift+down arrow stop interacting vo+shift+up arrow read from current vo+a read from top vo+b pause/resume speech control keyboard help vo+k help menu vo+h commands menu vo+h twice item chooser vo+i rotor vo+u notifications vo+n ignore next keypress vo+tab voiceover utility vo+fn+f8 dock vo+d apple menu vo+shift+m part 24 - official apple resources apple voiceover user guide apple voiceover general commands apple voiceover navigation commands apple accessibility support final independence checklist ☐ i can turn voiceover on and off. ☐ i understand the vo modifier. ☐ i can move next/previous and activate controls. ☐ i can interact with and leave groups. ☐ i can use dock, spotlight, finder, and app switching. ☐ i can use the rotor and item chooser. ☐ i can navigate webpages by structure. ☐ i can type, edit, and read text. ☐ i can use voiceover utility. ☐ i can troubleshoot common navigation and speech problems. ☐ i know where to find apple's current voiceover documentation. return to all manuals

entries.title: Windows 11 Accessibility Manual
entries.snippet: Windows 11 Accessibility Manual: step-by-step keyboard and screen-reader instructions, practice, troubleshooting, and command references.
entries.text: windows 11 accessibility manual - accessible learning center skip to main content accessible learning center manual windows 11 accessibility manual narrator, nvda, and jaws independent self-study guide all manuals table of contents start of manual purpose: this manual teaches the built-in accessibility features of windows 11. it is designed to stand alone and assumes no previous experience with windows accessibility settings. scope: this guide focuses on accessibility features built into current windows 11: magnifier, text and pointer settings, color filters, contrast themes, narrator overview, live captions, audio accessibility, hearing devices, voice access, voice typing, on-screen keyboard, sticky/filter/toggle keys, mouse keys, eye control, focus and notification settings, and accessibility shortcuts. core shortcut: press windows+u at any time to open settings > accessibility. how to use this manual change one accessibility setting at a time, test it, and then decide whether to keep it. press windows+u to return to the accessibility settings hub. use tab and shift+tab to move among controls; use arrow keys in lists and spacebar to toggle many switches. keep a written record of settings that make the computer easier to use. some features depend on hardware, language, windows edition, or device capability. built-in accessibility features can be combined; for example, magnifier can be used with narrator, and sticky keys can be used with keyboard shortcuts. do not disable an accessibility feature that another person depends on without their permission. if a shortcut triggers something unexpected, press escape and return to windows+u before changing more settings. table of contents part 1 - windows 11 accessibility overview part 2 - open and navigate accessibility settings part 3 - text size and visual effects part 4 - mouse pointer and touch part 5 - text cursor part 6 - magnifier part 7 - magnifier reading part 8 - color filters part 9 - contrast themes part 10 - narrator overview part 11 - live captions part 12 - audio, mono audio, and visual alerts part 13 - hearing devices part 14 - voice access part 15 - voice typing part 16 - on-screen keyboard part 17 - sticky keys, filter keys, and toggle keys part 18 - mouse keys part 19 - touch and pen accessibility part 20 - eye control part 21 - focus, notifications, and visual clutter part 22 - accessibility flyout and sign-in screen part 23 - windows hello and easier sign-in part 24 - combining features safely part 25 - privacy and security part 26 - troubleshooting part 27 - independent practice course part 28 - quick reference part 29 - official microsoft resources part 1 - windows 11 accessibility overview windows 11 groups accessibility settings into broad areas for vision, hearing, and interaction. microsoft also provides tools for focus and cognitive accessibility. vision: text size, visual effects, mouse pointer and touch, text cursor, magnifier, color filters, contrast themes, and narrator. hearing: audio settings, visual alternatives to sounds, captions, and hearing-device support. interaction: speech, keyboard, mouse, and eye control. focus: notification timing, reduced animation, taskbar simplification, and other distraction-reduction settings. part 2 - open and navigate accessibility settings 2.1 open accessibility settings what you will learn: reach the central windows accessibility hub quickly. before you begin: windows 11 is running. exactly how to do it press windows+u. wait for settings to open. press tab once or more until the accessibility categories/settings are announced or visibly focused. use up/down arrow through available accessibility pages when focus is in the navigation list. press enter on the category you
