headset you intend to use. exactly how to do it open zoom settings. open audio settings. find the microphone selection. read the selected microphone. choose the correct microphone if necessary. speak at a normal level. watch or listen for zoom's input-level/test feedback. use test mic if available and follow the recording/playback procedure. adjust the input volume only if needed. what should happen: zoom detects your voice and, when using the test feature, plays it back. if that does not happen: if zoom detects no voice, check the headset's physical mute switch, windows/macos microphone privacy permission, selected device, and hardware connection. practice: say a full sentence at normal speaking volume and verify the microphone detects it. 7.3 check your camera before joining what you will learn: confirm which camera zoom will use. before you begin: connect or uncover the camera. exactly how to do it open zoom settings. open video & effects or video settings. read the selected camera name. choose the correct camera if more than one exists. check the video preview if you use vision, or confirm camera status through screen-reader labels/physical privacy indicators. close settings. what should happen: zoom is set to the intended camera. if that does not happen: if the camera is unavailable, close other apps that may be using it and check operating-system camera privacy permission. practice: identify how to switch cameras without entering a real meeting. part 8 - understand the meeting window when you join a meeting, the meeting controls toolbar contains the controls you use most. zoom allows toolbar customization, so a control can be directly on the toolbar or inside more. audio: mute/unmute and select microphone/speaker. video: start/stop video and choose camera/effects. participants: view who is in the meeting. chat: open in-meeting messages. share: share a screen, window, whiteboard, or other content if permitted. react: raise hand, reactions, and non-verbal feedback. more: additional controls such as captions, recording, settings, and features not placed directly on your toolbar. leave: exit the meeting. hosts may instead see end with choices to end for everyone or leave. important: a host or administrator can prevent participants from using features such as screen sharing, chat, video, captions, recording, or reactions. part 9 - mute and unmute 9.1 mute or unmute yourself what you will learn: control whether other participants can hear your microphone. before you begin: be inside a meeting and connected to computer audio. exactly how to do it windows: press alt+a. mac: press command+shift+a. listen for zoom's audio status announcement or inspect the microphone icon. if you were unmuted, you should now be muted. press the same shortcut again. if the host allows you to unmute, you should now be unmuted. when muted and the zoom meeting window has focus, you can hold the spacebar temporarily to speak if push-to-talk is enabled/available; release spacebar to return to mute. what should happen: your microphone toggles between muted and unmuted. if that does not happen: if zoom says the host has prevented you from unmuting, you must wait for the host to allow it. if alt+a/command+shift+a does not work, locate the audio button and activate it. practice: practice toggling twice and state whether your microphone is muted at the end. part 10 - start and stop video 10.1 turn your camera on or off what you will learn: control whether your camera video is being sent. before you begin: be inside a meeting. exactly how to do it windows: press alt+v. mac: press command+shift+v. listen for the video status or check the camera icon. press the same shortcut again to reverse the state. if the host has disabled participant video, zoom may prevent you from starting it. to choose a different camera, open the menu next to the video button and select the desired camera. what should happen: video changes between on and off when permitted. if that does not happen: if the camera does not start, check camera privacy permission, camera selection, hardware privacy shutter, and whether another app is using the camera. practice: turn video on, identify the selected camera, then turn video off. part 11 - participants 11.1 open the participants panel what you will learn: find out who is in the meeting and review participant status. before you begin: be inside a meeting. exactly how to do it windows: press alt+u. mac: press command+u. wait for the participants panel to open. press tab until focus moves into the participants list if it is not already there. use up arrow/down arrow to move through participant names when supported. listen for status information such as muted, host, co-host, raised hand, or other available labels. press alt+u on windows or command+u on mac again, or activate the panel close control, to close the panel. what should happen: you can review participant names and close the panel. if that does not happen: if the shortcut does not open the panel, tab through the meeting toolbar to participants and activate it. practice: open participants, identify three names/statuses, and close the panel. part 12 - in-meeting chat 12.1 open chat and send a message what you will learn: send a text message during a meeting. before you begin: chat must be allowed by the host/account. exactly how to do it windows: press alt+h. mac: press command+shift+h. wait for the chat panel. move to the message-entry field with tab if necessary. check the recipient selector if the meeting allows private messages. make sure you know whether you are sending to everyone or one person. type your message. press enter/return to send. move to the message history with shift+tab or the appropriate navigation controls if you want to read previous messages. use arrow keys or screen-reader navigation to read messages. close chat with the shortcut or panel close control. what should happen: the message appears in the selected chat destination. if that does not happen: if chat is missing or you cannot send, the host or administrator may have restricted chat. do not assume a keyboard problem. practice: send a short test message in a meeting where you have permission. privacy: always confirm the chat recipient before sending. a message intended for one person can be embarrassing or sensitive if sent to everyone. part 13 - captions and accessibility zoom accessibility settings can change chat display size, caption font size/color/font/position, automatic video dimming for flashing content, gif animation behavior, and screen-reader alerts. 13.1 turn on captions in a meeting what you will learn: display spoken meeting content as captions when available. before you begin: be inside a meeting where captions are enabled/allowed. exactly how to do it move to more on the meeting toolbar if show captions is not already visible. open more. move through the menu until show captions is focused. activate show captions. if zoom asks for a language or caption choice, select the spoken language used in the meeting. wait for captions to appear. to stop displaying captions, return to the same control and choose the appropriate hide/stop option. what should happen: captions appear as people speak. if that does not happen: if show captions is unavailable, the feature may be disabled by account policy or not enabled for the meeting. practice: turn captions on in a test meeting and find where they appear. 13.2 make captions easier to read what you will learn: change how captions look on your device. before you begin: be signed into zoom workplace. exactly how to do it open your profile/account menu. choose settings. open accessibility. find the closed captioning section. adjust font size. choose caption color/background combinations if available. choose the font type if desired. choose whether captions are pinned at the bottom or shown as a movable/resizable overlay, if your version offers that option. enable always show captions in meetings and webinars if you want zoom to display captions automatically whenever they are available. close settings. what should happen: captions use your chosen display preferences. if that does not happen: if a setting is unavailable, update zoom workplace and verify your platform supports it. practice: increase caption size, close settings, then return and restore your preferred size. 13.3 configure screen reader alerts what you will learn: control which zoom meeting events your screen reader announces. before you begin: use a screen reader and be signed in. exactly how to do it open zoom settings. open accessibility. find screen reader alerts. move through the available meeting-action, chat, and permission alerts. enable alerts you need. disable alerts that are too repetitive. use restore if you want to return to zoom's default alert choices. what should happen: your screen reader announces the selected zoom events. if that does not happen: if zoom feels overly verbose, reduce only the specific alerts that are unnecessary rather than disabling all feedback. practice: review the alert list and identify at least three announcements that are useful to you. part 14 - raise hand, reactions, and non-verbal feedback 14.1 raise and lower your hand what you will learn: signal that you want to speak. before you begin: be inside a meeting where reactions/non-verbal feedback are allowed. exactly how to do it windows: press alt+y. mac: press option+y. listen for or inspect the raised-hand status. wait for the host to acknowledge you. when you no longer need the hand raised, press the same shortcut again. what should happen: your hand status changes between raised and lowered. if that does not happen: if the shortcut does not work, open react and choose raise hand. the host/admin may have disabled some reaction features. practice: raise your hand, verify it is raised, then lower it. 14.2 send a reaction what you will learn: use a temporary emoji reaction without interrupting the speaker. before you begin: be inside a meeting where reactions are enabled. exactly how to do it move to react on the meeting toolbar. open it. choose a reaction such as thumbs up, clapping hands, heart, or another available emoji. activate the reaction. wait for the reaction to appear temporarily. open react again if you need to choose non-verbal feedback such as yes or no where available. what should happen: the selected reaction appears according to the meeting's settings. if that does not happen: if only a limited set appears, the account or meeting may use selected emojis rather than the full emoji set. practice: send a thumbs up reaction in a practice meeting. part 15 - share your screen or a window 15.1 share a specific window what you will learn: share only the application you intend to show. before you begin: close private information before sharing. exactly how to do it open the application/window you want to share before opening the share picker. return to the zoom meeting. windows: press alt+s. mac: press command+shift+s. wait for the share screen/share content picker. move through the available screens, windows, tabs, whiteboards, or other share sources. choose the specific window you intend to share rather than the entire desktop whenever practical. if you are sharing video/audio content, review any share sound or optimize video options before starting. activate share. wait for zoom to indicate that sharing has started. navigate to the shared application and present your content. to stop sharing, move to the floating share toolbar and activate stop share, or use the appropriate shortcut/control. what should happen: participants see only the chosen content until you stop sharing. if that does not happen: if zoom does not offer screen/window choices, check host permission, account policy, and operating-system screen-recording/privacy permission. on macos, screen recording permission may be required. practice: share a non-sensitive window in a test meeting, verify sharing, then stop. privacy: before sharing your whole desktop, close email, chat pop-ups, password managers, personal notifications, client records, and anything else that should not be exposed. part 16 - leave a meeting 16.1 leave as a participant what you will learn: exit the meeting without ending it for everyone. before you begin: be inside a meeting. exactly how to do it move to the leave button on the meeting toolbar. activate leave. if zoom asks you to confirm, choose leave meeting. wait for the meeting window to close. what should happen: you leave while the meeting can continue for others. if that does not happen: if you are the host, zoom may show end rather than a simple leave button. read the choices carefully before selecting end meeting for all. practice: join a private test meeting and locate the leave control before doing anything else. part 17 - schedule a meeting 17.1 schedule from zoom workplace what you will learn: create a meeting with a date, time, and meeting options. before you begin: be signed into zoom workplace. exactly how to do it open home. activate schedule. wait for the scheduling window. enter the meeting topic/title. set the date. set the start time. set the duration/end time as provided by your zoom version. if you need a recurring meeting, open repeat/recurrence and choose daily, weekly, monthly, every weekday, custom, or another available pattern. review security choices such as passcode and waiting room. choose whether host video and participant video should start on or off if those options are available. choose audio options appropriate to your organization. review calendar integration if zoom will create an outlook/google/zoom calendar event. activate save. if an external calendar event opens, add invitees and send the calendar invitation. what should happen: the meeting appears in your upcoming meetings/calendar. if that does not happen: if save is unavailable, verify that date/time and any required security settings are valid. practice: schedule a practice meeting for a future day, then open its details. part 18 - start a meeting you host 18.1 start your scheduled meeting what you will learn: enter your meeting as the host. before you begin: be signed into the same zoom account that scheduled the meeting. exactly how to do it open home or meetings/calendar. find the scheduled meeting. read the title/date/time to confirm it is the correct meeting. activate start. wait for the meeting window. connect audio. verify microphone and video state. if participants are in the waiting room, open participants and admit them when ready. what should happen: you enter with host controls. if that does not happen: if zoom treats you as a participant instead of host, confirm you are signed into the account that scheduled the meeting. practice: start a private practice meeting and locate the security and participants controls. part 19 - invite others 19.1 copy a meeting invitation before the meeting what you will learn: copy the join information so you can send it by email or message. before you begin: have a scheduled meeting. exactly how to do it open the meeting card/details. open the more/ellipsis menu if copy invitation is not directly shown. choose copy invitation. open the email or messaging application you want to use. paste the copied invitation. review the meeting title, date/time, join link, meeting id, and passcode before sending. send it only to the intended recipients. what should happen: the recipient receives the zoom join information. if that does not happen: if copy invitation is missing, open the meeting details or use the zoom web portal to copy the invitation. practice: copy a practice invitation into a blank document and identify the join link, meeting id, and passcode. 19.2 invite someone during a meeting what you will learn: invite another person while the meeting is already running. before you begin: be the host or have permission to invite. exactly how to do it open participants. at the bottom of the participants panel, activate invite. choose a supported invitation method such as contacts, email, copy invite link, or copy invitation. if using copy invite link/invitation, paste it into a message to the intended person. close the invite window when finished. what should happen: the invited person receives usable join information. if that does not happen: if some invite methods are missing, your account may not have those integrations enabled. practice: open the invite window in a practice meeting and identify at least two invitation methods. part 20 - host and security controls hosts can control participant permissions. zoom documents options such as allowing or preventing screen sharing, chat, renaming, unmuting, starting video, whiteboards, and recording, depending on account and meeting configuration. 20.1 review meeting security without changing anything what you will learn: understand where host controls are located. before you begin: start a meeting as host. exactly how to do it find and open security on the meeting toolbar, or open the host controls area used by your current zoom layout. move through the available options one at a time. identify whether waiting room is enabled. identify whether participants can share screen. identify whether participants can chat. identify whether participants can rename. identify whether participants can unmute themselves. identify whether participants can start video. close the menu without changing anything. what should happen: you know which participant capabilities the meeting currently allows. if that does not happen: if security is missing, you may not be host/co-host or your zoom layout may place the controls under another host menu. practice: review the security menu before hosting an important meeting. part 21 - waiting room 21.1 admit a participant from the waiting room what you will learn: let the correct person enter your meeting. before you begin: be host/co-host in a meeting with waiting room enabled. exactly how to do it open participants. find the waiting room section. move to the person's name. read the full display name before admitting them. activate admit. wait for the person to move into the active participant list. what should happen: the selected person joins the meeting. if that does not happen: if you do not recognize the person, do not admit them until you can verify their identity through an appropriate method. practice: use a second test device/account if available to practice the waiting-room flow. part 22 - breakout rooms breakout rooms divide a zoom meeting into smaller sessions. the host can assign rooms manually or automatically; participants may be asked to join a room, and some meetings allow self-selection. 22.1 join a breakout room as a participant what you will learn: move from the main meeting into an assigned breakout room. before you begin: the host has opened breakout rooms and assigned or allowed you to choose a room. exactly how to do it wait for zoom's breakout-room invitation prompt. read the room name if shown. activate join. wait for the breakout-room meeting area to load. use audio, video, chat, and other permitted controls normally. when you want to return and the meeting allows it, activate leave. choose leave breakout room rather than leave meeting if you want to return to the main session. what should happen: you enter the breakout room and can return to the main meeting. if that does not happen: if no invitation appears, the host may not have assigned you yet. if you accidentally choose leave meeting, you may exit the entire meeting. practice: before joining a real breakout session, remember the difference between leave breakout room and leave meeting. part 23 - recording recording availability depends on account, host permission, organization policy, and local laws/policies. participants may need permission to record. 23.1 recognize recording controls and notifications what you will learn: understand what happens when recording starts. before you begin: be in a meeting where recording is permitted. exactly how to do it listen for zoom's recording notification or inspect the recording indicator. if you are host and recording is allowed, locate record on the toolbar or under more. choose the available recording method, such as computer/local or cloud, according to your account. follow any disclosure/consent requirements that apply to your organization and jurisdiction. to stop, return to the recording control and choose stop recording. after the meeting, allow zoom time to process or convert the recording if required. what should happen: you can tell whether recording is active and stop it intentionally. if that does not happen: if record is missing, your account, administrator, or host may not allow it. practice: locate the recording control in a practice meeting without starting a recording unless you have permission. part 24 - zoom team chat zoom workplace can include team chat for direct and channel conversations. availability depends on your account. 24.1 open a zoom team chat conversation what you will learn: read and send a message outside a meeting. before you begin: be signed into zoom workplace with team chat enabled. exactly how to do it open team chat from the zoom navigation bar. move through the chat/channel list. select the intended conversation. move to the message history and read recent messages. move to the compose field. type your message. press enter/return or activate send according to your compose settings. confirm the message appears in the conversation. what should happen: the message is sent to the intended zoom team chat conversation. if that does not happen: if team chat is missing, your organization may not have enabled it or your navigation bar may place it under more. practice: open one safe conversation and identify the history and compose areas. part 25 - profile, status, and settings 25.1 open zoom settings what you will learn: reach zoom's local app preferences. before you begin: be signed into the desktop app. exactly how to do it move to your profile picture/account control. activate it. choose settings. move through categories such as general, audio, video & effects, meetings & webinars, team chat, accessibility, and keyboard shortcuts. open the category you need. change only the setting you intended. close settings when finished. what should happen: the selected setting takes effect or is saved automatically. if that does not happen: if your desired setting is not in the desktop app, it may be an account-level setting available only in the zoom web portal. practice: open settings and locate audio, accessibility, and keyboard shortcuts. part 26 - keyboard shortcuts meeting task windows mac mute/unmute alt+a command+shift+a start/stop video alt+v command+shift+v start/stop screen sharing alt+s command+shift+s open/close chat alt+h command+shift+h open/close participants alt+u command+u raise/lower hand alt+y option+y switch active speaker view alt+f1 check current zoom settings switch gallery view alt+f2 check current zoom settings global shortcuts: zoom can allow some shortcuts to work even when zoom is not the active application. review the global shortcut option in settings > keyboard shortcuts before enabling it so you understand what keys will affect zoom system-wide. part 27 - windows screen reader use zoom provides accessibility settings for screen-reader alerts and supports keyboard navigation throughout the desktop application. narrator, jaws, and nvda users should combine standard tab/shift+tab navigation with zoom's direct meeting shortcuts. 27.1 navigate a meeting with a windows screen reader what you will learn: control a meeting without relying on the mouse. before you begin: start narrator, jaws, or nvda before joining. exactly how to do it join the meeting and wait for the meeting window to have focus. use alt+a to confirm audio status. use alt+v to confirm video status. use alt+u to open participants. use tab to move into the participant list, then arrow through names if supported. close participants. use alt+h to open chat. move to the message field with tab. type a test message if appropriate. use alt+y to raise/lower your hand. use tab through the meeting toolbar when you need a control that has no convenient shortcut. listen for zoom's screen-reader alerts after actions such as mute/unmute, chat events, and permission changes. what should happen: you can perform core meeting actions with direct shortcuts and keyboard focus. if that does not happen: if zoom announces too many or too few events, open settings > accessibility > screen reader alerts and adjust individual alert categories. practice: join a test meeting and perform audio, participants, chat, and raise-hand actions without a mouse. part 28 - voiceover on mac voiceover adds its own navigation commands on top of zoom's mac shortcuts. use vo+right/left arrow to inspect controls, vo+space to activate, and interact with groups when necessary. task mac command voiceover next item vo+right arrow voiceover previous item vo+left arrow activate current voiceover item vo+space interact with group vo+shift+down arrow stop interacting vo+shift+up arrow zoom mute/unmute command+shift+a zoom video command+shift+v zoom share command+shift+s zoom chat command+shift+h zoom participants command+u zoom raise/lower hand option+y 28.1 join and operate a meeting with voiceover what you will learn: use zoom independently on mac. before you begin: voiceover is on before zoom opens. exactly how to do it open zoom workplace with command+space, type zoom workplace, press return. use vo+right arrow to identify controls on the zoom home screen. open join or activate a join link. on the pre-join screen, use vo+right arrow through display name, audio, video, and join controls. use vo+space to toggle or activate controls. after joining, use zoom's direct shortcuts for common meeting actions such as command+shift+a for audio. use command+u for participants and command+shift+h for chat. when you need to inspect the toolbar manually, use vo+right/left arrow. if voiceover announces a group, use vo+shift+down arrow to interact and vo+shift+up arrow to leave it. what should happen: you can join and use the core meeting controls without sighted assistance. if that does not happen: if you feel trapped in a group, press vo+shift+up arrow to move outward. if a zoom shortcut does not respond, verify the meeting window has focus. practice: use the zoom test meeting to practice audio, video, participants, chat, and leave. part 29 - zoom web app zoom can run in a browser when allowed. browser behavior and shortcuts can differ from the desktop app, and some features may be limited. choose join from your browser if the meeting page offers it and you do not want/cannot use the desktop app. grant microphone/camera browser permissions only when needed. use the browser's normal tab/shift+tab navigation plus zoom web app controls. be aware that browser shortcuts can conflict with zoom keyboard shortcuts. for the most complete and predictable accessibility experience, use a current supported browser and zoom's current web app documentation. part 30 - zoom mobile app the zoom workplace mobile app is available on ios and android. the basic meeting concepts are the same, but controls are touch-based. tap the screen during a meeting if controls have hidden themselves. use mute/unmute, start/stop video, participants, more, share, and leave controls. voiceover users on iphone/ipad move with swipe left/right and activate with double-tap. talkback users on android move with swipe gestures and activate with double-tap. mobile caption/chat text size can depend on the device's accessibility/font settings. part 31 - troubleshooting 31.1 nobody can hear you what you will learn: find whether the cause is mute state, device choice, permission, or hardware. before you begin: be in a meeting or open audio settings. exactly how to do it press alt+a on windows or command+shift+a on mac and confirm whether you are muted. check whether the host has prevented participants from unmuting. open zoom settings > audio. confirm the intended microphone is selected. speak and check zoom's input feedback. check the microphone's physical mute switch. check windows/macos microphone privacy permission for zoom workplace. reconnect the headset/microphone. use test mic. what should happen: zoom detects your voice and other participants can hear you when unmuted. if that does not happen: if the operating system also cannot detect the microphone, fix the hardware/system issue before changing more zoom settings. practice: run this checklist before an important meeting. 31.2 you cannot hear other people what you will learn: troubleshoot output audio. before you begin: meeting audio should be active. exactly how to do it check the computer's volume and mute state. open zoom settings > audio. confirm the intended speaker device. activate test speaker. if using bluetooth headphones, verify they are connected to the computer. check whether you actually joined computer audio in the meeting. leave and rejoin computer audio if necessary. try another speaker/headset if available. what should happen: you hear meeting and test audio. if that does not happen: if other applications also have no sound, troubleshoot the operating system or output device rather than zoom alone. practice: verify the speaker device before your next meeting. 31.3 your camera will not start what you will learn: check video problems in a sensible order. before you begin: your camera is connected/uncovered. exactly how to do it press alt+v or command+shift+v. check whether the host has prevented participants from starting video. open zoom settings > video & effects. confirm the correct camera. close other apps that may be using the camera. check the physical camera privacy shutter/switch. check windows/macos camera privacy permission. restart zoom if necessary. what should happen: the camera becomes available when permitted. if that does not happen: if no app can use the camera, troubleshoot the hardware/system first. practice: identify the selected camera and physical privacy control. 31.4 you cannot share your screen what you will learn: determine whether the problem is host permission, account policy, or operating-system permission. before you begin: be inside a meeting. exactly how to do it try alt+s/command+shift+s or activate share. if zoom says only the host can share, ask the host to allow participant sharing. if share is missing, it may be restricted by admin/meeting policy. on macos, check screen recording/screen & system audio recording privacy permission for zoom. restart zoom after changing required system permissions. try sharing a single window. what should happen: the share picker opens and your selected content can be shared. if that does not happen: if the host/admin has disabled sharing, you cannot override that restriction from your device. practice: practice finding the share control even when you do not actually start sharing. 31.5 you are in the waiting room what you will learn: recognize that zoom is working and you are waiting for admission. before you begin: you have joined a meeting that uses waiting room. exactly how to do it read the waiting-room message. do not repeatedly leave and rejoin unless instructed. confirm that your display name identifies you clearly enough for the host to recognize you. wait for the host to admit you. if the wait is unusually long, contact the organizer through another agreed communication method. what should happen: you enter when the host admits you. if that does not happen: if the host does not recognize your display name, you may remain waiting longer. use an appropriate recognizable name before joining when possible. practice: learn to distinguish a waiting-room message from a connection-error message. 31.6 zoom says the meeting id or passcode is invalid what you will learn: correct invitation-entry problems. before you begin: have the original invitation. exactly how to do it return to the original invitation rather than relying on a handwritten number if possible. re-enter the meeting id. re-enter the passcode exactly. check similar characters such as o/0 and i/l/1. make sure you are joining the correct occurrence of a recurring meeting. try the full join link from the invitation. contact the organizer if the invitation may have been changed or cancelled. what should happen: you join successfully or confirm that the meeting information itself is outdated. if that does not happen: if the link also fails, the meeting may have ended, been deleted, or been changed by the host. practice: compare a meeting id/passcode with the original invitation before entering it manually. part 32 - independent practice course level 1 - open and orient ☐ open zoom workplace. ☐ identify home/navigation, profile, and settings. ☐ open audio settings. ☐ open keyboard shortcuts. ready to advance: you can complete every checked task without another person telling you what key or control to use. level 2 - join ☐ open the join dialog. ☐ identify meeting id, display name, audio/video choices. ☐ join a test meeting. ☐ recognize a waiting room if shown. ready to advance: you can complete every checked task without another person telling you what key or control to use. level 3 - audio and video ☐ mute/unmute with shortcut. ☐ start/stop video. ☐ open audio settings. ☐ verify speaker and microphone. ready to advance: you can complete every checked task without another person telling you what key or control to use. level 4 - meeting panels ☐ open participants. ☐ read participant names. ☐ open chat. ☐ send a test message. ☐ close both panels. ready to advance: you can complete every checked task without another person telling you what key or control to use. level 5 - accessibility ☐ turn on captions when available. ☐ adjust caption size. ☐ review screen-reader alerts. ☐ raise/lower hand. ready to advance: you can complete every checked task without another person telling you what key or control to use. level 6 - screen sharing ☐ open the share picker. ☐ choose a safe window. ☐ start sharing. ☐ stop sharing. ready to advance: you can complete every checked task without another person telling you what key or control to use. level 7 - host basics ☐ schedule a practice meeting. ☐ start it as host. ☐ review security. ☐ use waiting room. ☐ copy the invitation. ready to advance: you can complete every checked task without another person telling you what key or control to use. level 8 - breakouts and recording concepts ☐ recognize a breakout invitation. ☐ know leave breakout room vs leave meeting. ☐ locate record without starting it. ☐ explain who controls participant permissions. ready to advance: you can complete every checked task without another person telling you what key or control to use. level 9 - troubleshooting ☐ diagnose no microphone. ☐ diagnose no speaker audio. ☐ diagnose no camera. ☐ diagnose inability to screen share. ☐ explain host/admin restrictions. ready to advance: you can complete every checked task without another person telling you what key or control to use. part 33 - quick reference windows meeting shortcuts task windows command mute/unmute alt+a start/stop video alt+v start/stop share alt+s open/close chat alt+h open/close participants alt+u raise/lower hand alt+y mac meeting shortcuts task mac command mute/unmute command+shift+a start/stop video command+shift+v start/stop share command+shift+s open/close chat command+shift+h open/close participants command+u raise/lower hand option+y before every important meeting ☐ open zoom early. ☐ check for zoom updates. ☐ confirm speaker. ☐ confirm microphone. ☐ confirm camera if needed. ☐ keep the invitation available. ☐ join with the intended display name. ☐ check mute status before speaking. ☐ close private content before screen sharing. ☐ know where leave is. part 34 - official zoom resources getting started with zoom workplace desktop app joining a zoom meeting zoom keyboard shortcuts zoom workplace settings and accessibility participant meeting controls sharing your screen or desktop muting and unmuting yourself meeting reactions and non-verbal feedback managing breakout rooms meeting security settings inviting others to a meeting zoom getting started guide for new users final independence checklist ☐ i can open zoom workplace and sign in. ☐ i understand the main zoom window and settings. ☐ i can join from a link. ☐ i can join with a meeting id and passcode. ☐ i can test my speaker and microphone. ☐ i can select my camera. ☐ i can mute/unmute myself. ☐ i can start/stop video. ☐ i can open participants and chat. ☐ i can use captions when available. ☐ i can raise/lower my hand and use reactions. ☐ i can safely share and stop sharing a window. ☐ i can leave a meeting intentionally. ☐ i can schedule and start a meeting. ☐ i understand the host, participant, waiting room, and breakout-room roles. ☐ i understand that hosts/admins can restrict features. ☐ i can troubleshoot audio, video, join, and sharing problems logically. ☐ i know where to find zoom's current keyboard shortcuts and accessibility settings. ☐ i know where to find zoom's official support documentation. most important habit: do one action, then stop and confirm what changed. this reduces accidental unmuting, unintended video, messages sent to the wrong destination, incorrect screen sharing, and accidental meeting exits. return to all manuals

entries.course: Zoom, Microsoft Teams, and Google Meet
entries.snippet: Step-by-step keyboard manual for Zoom, Microsoft Teams, and Google Meet.
entries.text: online meetings manual - accessible learning center online communication zoom, microsoft teams, and google meet manual join, participate, present, and leave meetings using the keyboard. basic how-tos advanced how-tos command list basic how-tos join a meeting safely keyboard commands: tab and shift+tab move through join controls. space changes a focused checkbox. enter activates join. open the invitation and verify the organizer, date, and meeting link. open the link and confirm the meeting application or browser tab. tab through microphone, camera, name, and audio choices. join muted unless instructed otherwise. activate join and wait for the meeting title or waiting-room announcement. you should hear: your microphone and camera states, followed by the meeting or waiting room. if that does not happen: do not press join repeatedly. check for a browser permission dialog or an “open application” prompt. mute or unmute keyboard commands: zoom: alt+a. teams: ctrl+shift+m. google meet: ctrl+d. confirm the correct meeting is active. press the command once. wait for a spoken or sound confirmation. when uncertain, tab to the microphone button and read its state. if that does not happen: do not toggle repeatedly. a host or organization may prevent unmuting. start or stop the camera keyboard commands: zoom: alt+v. teams: ctrl+shift+o. google meet: ctrl+e. confirm the meeting and whether video is appropriate. press the correct command once. listen for “start video” or “stop video,” which usually describes the action available next. if that does not happen: locate the camera button and check camera permissions or host restrictions. open chat and send a message keyboard command: zoom: alt+h opens or closes meeting chat. in teams and meet, locate chat by button navigation because shortcuts and layouts change. open chat and confirm its heading. move to the message field. type a short message and review it. press enter to send only when the application indicates enter sends. return to meeting controls after confirming the message appeared. if that does not happen: check whether focus is in chat history, a recipient selector, or the message field. advanced how-tos raise and lower your hand keyboard command: zoom: alt+y. in teams and meet, locate reactions or raise hand by its button name. activate raise hand once. listen for confirmation. wait to be recognized. lower your hand after speaking. if that does not happen: find the button and read whether its current action is raise hand or lower hand. turn captions on keyboard approach: navigate to captions, closed captions, or more actions, then activate the captions control. open captions before important discussion begins. select the spoken language if requested. confirm that caption text is appearing. remember that automatic captions may misidentify names or technical words. if that does not happen: ask the host whether captions are enabled and request an accessible transcript or notes. share a window safely keyboard command: zoom: alt+s starts or stops sharing when permitted. for teams and meet, activate the labeled share control. close private files, messages, and notifications. open only the content you intend to share. start sharing and choose a specific window rather than the entire screen. read the selected window name before confirming. describe visual content aloud and provide the source file or accessible alternative. stop sharing and confirm that sharing ended. if that does not happen: cancel the chooser. never select a source whose name you cannot verify. leave without ending the meeting for everyone keyboard approach: find leave, then read the confirmation choices. save anything needed from chat according to the meeting policy. activate leave. if you are the host, choose leave meeting unless you truly intend to end it for everyone. confirm that focus returns to the desktop or previous application. if that does not happen: read the dialog carefully; do not choose end meeting for all by accident. quick command list zoom alt+a / teams ctrl+shift+m / meet ctrl+d: microphone zoom alt+v / teams ctrl+shift+o / meet ctrl+e: camera zoom alt+u: participants zoom alt+h: chat zoom alt+y: raise or lower hand zoom alt+s: start or stop sharing tab / shift+tab: next or previous control version note: commands shown are for windows. web and desktop versions can differ. return to manuals
